records.script: They do not need to high step to prevent their pant legs from getting wet if the water gets too high. Their ability to score 3 objects in autonomous could move mountains.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team demonstrated unique ways to thrive among the critters of the competition Bayou. Their herringbone gear design made their robot operate as smooth and cunning as a gator swimming through the swamp. With a modified claw grabbing the creativity award.
This team is iterative design royalty, gathering inspiration from everywhere. With two intakes and 28 autonomous modes, this team can do it all. Their final design gave us butterflies.
These birds of a feather, flock together by packing their wings to help mentor teams to fly. These electrified flamingos brought the color to gracious professional.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team enlists their members from far and wide but you may not see them if they hide. Their robot marches in red and black. A dedication to image, they do not lack. So come on down to hunker in the bunker.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Working a vision of design and fashion, this community team has a cube shooter, yolo, and LED's. A grand master of Yoda of industrial design.

They spin cobwebs every time they get onto the field. By stringing together hardware and software solutions, they climb to the top. You would almost think they had eight legs for all of their innovations in control.

This team has tentacles that reach around their country, inspiring young engineers and communities. Their enthusiasm for FIRST and dedication to sharing their HEART with everyone is obvious. They were highly regarded for many awards and their POLVO values will ensure they remain a top team. BOA SORCHEE.

Teams in this category must be top flight in all aspects of design and performance. In this competition, one team has separated itself and broken away from the pack. Winner of the quality award is "Breakaway" from Searcy, Arkansas.

This team recognizes that to inspire a passion for engineering they need to provide a foundation to build upon. Through their countless outreach programs they bring STEM to light and help their global community GEAR UP in red, yellow, and black.

This years FIRST impact award recipient is dedicating to “lei’ ing” the STEM foundation and “connecting” the global community with accessible and equitable STEM education and technology. This team’s dedication to reaching across the oceans to breakdown barriers has resulted in the creation of student written, open source, customizable and culturally sensitive curriculum written in 6 languages, used in 51 countries and 25 schools. Maybe more impressively, this team is inspiring the future of STEM by showcasing projects in classrooms that solve real world problems. Some of their recent efforts include a portable data collecting catamaran, an autonomous water sampling drone, a micro plastic sifting robot and an affordable heart rate monitor and app. While other people may be busy vacationing, surfing and basking in the sunshine, this team uses their unique location and knowledge to focus on reaching indigenous and marginalized communities across Polynesia and North America with the goal of connecting with at least one new community a year. Congratulation to Team i’obotics (2348) from Hawaii. Ho’omaik’i (congratulations)

This team has a strong foundation and fully embraced FIRST's core values. With sustainability plans, outreach, and more, they are set up for long-term success. And with their clear identity, they can always be found on the mountain.

Even for a rookie team, they are already well afloat. In less than a year, they grew from an exciting idea to building a whole fleet. They explore the community and are well known, far and wide. Join me in a toast for rookie inspiration.
For extreme enthusiasm look no further than the sea of green. Their spirit is superheated both at home and on the road. These pandas climb to the top with team spirit.

This team shines the light on the principles and excitement of FIRST. Their great direction on outreach and inclusion with the community and education creates coherence for many years to come. They are beaming with team sustainability.

This well-machined robot is an autonomous triple threat. They impressed the judges by scoring 3 cubes while hands-free. When the match starts, they scream out of the gate consistently elevating their alliance to victory.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This noble robot always orients itself toward victory. Their robot’s linkage system conveys top-tier engineering prowess, on the field of battle and off. They have earned their seat at the round table of greatness.

This team looked for artistic and functional inspiration from nature. Their three-degree-of-freedom dual game piece manipulator worked better than its inspiration. By the way, the Broussard Police Department has some questions about some missing Squirrel Monkeys.

This team’s gracious professionalism is as rare as their name implies. Their continued technical assistance to one of the rookie teams allowed that team to be successful in this competition. They rose above the field and are great examples for all to follow.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When you compete in galaxies far, far away, it’s important that your image is easily identifiable. This team’s integration of theme and appearance and machine makes them recognizable in any galaxy because nothing is more identifiable than Han Solo's ride.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team has built itself into a thunderous competitor by designing elegant functionality into every part of their robot. It is inspiring to watch their aesthetic elevator work flawlessly with the rest of their machine. This robot has proved that they are so much more than just any ole knick-knack.

This team described and displayed the importance of innovation from its conception through manufacturing and its deployment on the field. Their smooth articulating arm flew through the air and blew us away. This squad was ready on the field for every implosive threat.

This team successfully spreads the FIRST philosophy near and far. They also have a well-built robot that lights up the competition as well as a strong team structure with rapport across their community and four support schools. Like many settlers before them, this team battled strong in the wild-west competition here today.

This team shattered expectations and didn’t crack under pressure. The machine’s telescoping arm and modular subsystems robustly withstood all rigors and tests of the competition. The only break in this team was away from the competition.

This team's underground ability to reach far and wide has provided them many successes. They have been granted a million (dollar) unique opportunities and with their energy will continue to zoom to new levels with their recruiting and community outreach. This wild team is not cloaked in secrecy but inspires many with outstanding success!

The sky is the limit for this team as they have spread the FIRST philosophy close to home and to far-away places. Whether walking like Woodie, providing a sweet ride for kids with impaired mobility, or presenting flowers to hospitals and nursing home patients, they’ve arrived at FIRST class status. This team is LASER-focused on FIRST Core Values and dedicated to spreading that vision wherever they go.

This rookie team recently discovered a map that has led them to FIRST robotics. During their first adventure, they discovered the purpose and vision of FIRST and future treasure awaits. “HEY, YOU GUYS!!!!!”

These seafaring people were very good at adapting to a new world. When this team’s robot did not perform as expected, they adapted to a new role of pirating and plundering their way through the competition. Not giving up, they drove their way to success inspiring teamwork with their alliances. SKOLL!

When you first gaze at this team’s hat, you may look for a shiny red nose. It’s their spirit and enthusiasm that glows and guides them through the competition. Their impressive antlers are far-reaching in their school and community.

The team is wild about STEM. When it comes to dedication, family always comes first. Their efforts within their school family have increased interest in science and mathematics by four-fold in their school. Although most cats do not like water, this team rises to the occasion helping local law enforcement to keep their heads above water.

records.script: This team was able to use the April tags for full-field odometry for a consistent high performing autonomous. Their auto is so fast, it’s like they trained it on a track. No one on land, sea, or space can touch this auto.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team compels strategic performance and impels creativity…in the way it vacuums its way to scoring!
This self-made team gave a detailed description of their engineering process. They *elevated* their game by repeatedly iterating their designs. This python swerves around the competition.
This team took G. P. into cyber space. They bring their positivity and respect everywhere they go. If your team is ever feeling down, just read “How Jada Saves the Day!”

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Parade on over to congratulate this team on making a sustainable system. They have no issue *swimming* to the top to make an impression. Let’s give a *fin* to the *gold* standard in imagery, the RoboKrew!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Their good looking robot elevates this well-dressed team to new heights. With smooth movements and efficient controls, this cohesive well-built bot does not duck its safety responsibilities, either. Their robot provides helpful clues that a good *cru* can put together a robot that does not get the blues.

This team’s robot is so automated that tele-op feels like autonomous. Their use of kalman filters impressed the judges to no end. Catch the drive team eating cookies because the robot is busy doing all the work.

This team truly knows what it means to be a good neighbor. They were happy to share their space, time and energy with a team that needed their help. They exemplified the meaning of co-opertition by making sure everyone got to the field. These superheroes turned out to be the greatest helpers of all.

This team redesigned parts to improve reliability. Their heavy plate aluminum construction forced them to gamble with the weight limit. This team may roll the dice, but not with their robot’s build quality.
This team reached school districts near and far. Keeping in mind that sustainability is the name of the game, the judges agree “if you build it, they will come.”

This team stood out to the judges for *three* key reasons: Their gracious professionalism, the ongoing growth of their outreach, and the sustained performance they have demonstrated. Our judges were impressed by *too* much to list. If we could say *one* thing, though, it is that we are excited to celebrate how they spread the mission of FIRST. Get ready to blast-off with our Impact Award winner!
There’s nothing *blue* about this team! Remember your safety glasses and hold on to your hamsters, folks. Gallop on over with this inspirational team.
We can hear them across the red, white and blue sea. Waving their hands in the air with enthusiasm, this team definitely takes the *pi*.
This colorful team had an interest that made us sparkle. Their tiny outreach bot keeps the next generation wanting more. Thanks for taking us along on your excellent adventure!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: This team sprung to action, clawing their way up the ranks. Their unwavering dedication to improvements set them apart. Despite their name, this team didn’t need to man the controls of their robot to achieve success. Congratulations, Team number 4627 Manning Robotics

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s creativity in robotics shows that they can not only knock it out of the park, but also pick up the pieces – or cones – along the way. This year’s winner of the creativity award is constantly tipping the scales in their favor. Congratulations, Team number 6364 Ten Ton Robotics

This team FORGED several unique MECHANICAL components and combined them into a cohesive, well performing robot. They kept the hearth fires burning, creating a robot that puts cones through the spin cycle within it’s ‘washing machine’ interior. Let’s erupt with applause - Congratulations, Team number 6390 Hephaestus

In the judges’ chamber, tales of good deeds were coming fast and furious from all around the room. So much graciousness was shared by so many teams. But, time and time again, we heard mention of how “island hospitality” from afar came ashore on our Island. Congratulations, Team number 359 the Hawaiian Kids

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has risen up to address the dawn of a new era with a reimagined look, shining through their robot and their whole team. By resetting their program and presence at the competition, they visually demonstrated their illuminating resilience. Congratulations, Team number 7135 System Reset

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team swung into action, showcasing truly impressive machining. With legroom to spare, this bot will rack up plenty of frequent flyer miles. The judges were thoroughly impressed and would be thrilled to take this carry-on ‘bot around the world, as a shining example of Industrial Design. Congratulations, Team number 4613 Barker Redbacks

The team has a low-slung bot, that soars across the field to smash the competition. They use an advanced control system to stay the course, and maintain their precision with ease. Rather than treading water, their innovative approach sailed straight into this award. Congratulations, Team number 7287 Atom Smashers

This team turned trash into treasure, using alternative materials in their ‘bot, to effectively meet their competition strategy. All members reinvented their fundraising plans when they lost sponsors, found the parts for the build, sold pizza and taught future innovators how to build robots. Congratulations, Team number 7787 Reynolds Reybots

With their lightning-fast robot, this team is living up to its name and leaving their competitors in disarray. They’ve calculated their way to the top, with pages of Lagrange math transformations. Congratulations, Team number 4253 Raid Zero

This team who - despite significant obstacles, have shown persistence and tenacity in their purpose. We are woven into their web of vision and mission, providing STEM opportunities for the underserved and disadvantaged beyond their country’s borders. The inclusive STEM passion emanating from this team draws future scientists - from elementary schools to Alumni - closer to the middle of this massive web. They are building future leaders and mentors will continue to advocate for a better world. Congratulations, Team number 1622 Team Spyder

This year’s winner is transforming our Culture by demonstrating the importance of reaching beyond their own team. Engaging disadvantaged communities and opening up STEM to the world. They have established a history of smashing barriers – geographic, political and personal. This Team fosters a strong Pathway from FLL, to FTC, to FRC and not just within their own community. They start teams and continue to mentor them - providing financial support where needed to ensure success. They are removing barriers to participation by solving Foundational issues faced by half the world’s population. They promote an “Everyone” mentality through their “ME FIRST” program. Congratulations, Team 1868 - _Space Cookies_

From Social Media posts, four days-per-week practice schedules, and enough documentation to fill a library…. This team has taken the Rookie field by “storm” The Rookie All-Star Award is presented to: Team 9079 Mechanics Storm

Out of the gate, this rookie team is truly inspiring. Though they are starting from the ground up, they can already be found all over town: • Cultivating future roboticists • Helping special needs kids realize THEIR robot dreams • And even teaching their teachers new tricks in rocketry. With their impressive 5 year plan, this team has already built a constellation of supporters. Congratulations, Team number 9180 Ursa Major!

This team had a visit from the dreaded robot inspectors, and got bad news. The next morning, Ten Tons of weight was lifted off their shoulders, and they were able to leap over troubled waters, and their sunny spirit shone through. Congratulations, Team number 7332 the PuddleJumpers

This team mixes both outreach and sponsorship to keep their team going strong. The diversity of their sponsors and their dedication to teaching others about STEM are core to how they embody the mission of FIRST. This team is well positioned to battle against all odds. Congratulations, Team number 3256 Warrior Borgs
No universo desse regional, essa equipe deixou sua marca. Eles brilharam constantemente com seus 3 movimentos precisos e elegantes. Durante o autonomo, essas estrelas levantaram poeira.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Essa equipe nadou livremente na arena da competição. Conseguiu de maneira criativa se ancorar e manter a embarcação segura mesmo nos locais mais turbulentos. E assim com seus oito tentáculos roxos abraçaram esse premio.

Sua eficiência no processo inspira às novas e velhas gerações de engenheiros e engenheiras. A regularidade de suas práticas mostrou a excelência em diversas áreas valorizadas pela FIRST. Apesar do logo apontar para um animal solitário, a coesão da equipe refletiu no atendimento dos padrões almejados para atingir a Excelência em Engenharia.

Esta equipe demonstra valores fundamentais da First, unindo espírito esportivo e altruísmo. A equipe criou um fórum para fomentar o trabalho colaborativo. Por fim ela ajudou outros times iniciantes da região norte-nordeste no desenvolvimento dos seus projetos.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: ESSA EQUIPE COM MUITA GARRA, DEFENDEU SUA IDENTIDADE. DO PITCH AO ROBÔ, A EQUIPE ESPALHOU SUA MARCA AS LUZES ACENDERAM E A JUMA FOI SOLTA.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Vindos do sul do país Com design de nível industrial, objetivo e eficiente. Eles mostraram que está tudo sob controle. 1156 Under Control
Nenhuma peça do jogo escapa deles. Com seu conjunto de artefatos precisos e velozes, eles conquistaram a posição de Alpha nos controles.
Uma equipe iniciante com uma grande inovação. Trouxe o conceito de Digital Twin para a FRC. Treinamento antecipado para os pilotos e experiência de jogo para não-pilotos.
Esse time veio de perto, logo ali, um tirinho. Quatro pontos de sólido apoio, com estrutura robusta e bem acabada. Foram mais simples, práticos e eficientes.
Esta equipe é representada por uma ave. Uma ave que dissemina engenharia dentro e além do seu território com ideias fora da caixinha. Diretamente do parque ecológico, Mega Harpy.

This team really impact on their community and make it clear with their passion, organization and values. You can ask all the students they have been working with, or teachers worldwide. And if you still doubt: you can just look into the seeds spread. This team showed everyone that when we work hard and together our impacts are not big, are Mega. Showing with signs that they build more than robots, they build trully Zords.

Uma equipe nova, bem estruturada e multidisciplinar, gerando impacto positivo para a sociedade. Com um processo seletivo bem elaborado, soube trazer diversão ao campeonato com seu jogo. E invocou para seu robô a sabedoria de uma lendária raposa.

Esta equipe valoriza muito a cultura do ensinar através da prática. E apesar de pouco tempo, já inspiram e acolhem a comunidade com seus experimentos. Diretamente do maior laboratório maker da América Latina, Techmaker Robotics.
Você pode até ainda não tê-los visto mas com certeza já os escutou. Pela sua presença de espírito, cooperação e musicalidade. Esse prêmio não é pra qualquer um, Potibot.
Não é a toa que essa equipe está conosco há anos. Com metodologias e a criação de clubes, mostraram que se importam com seu legado. Mesmo dentro da tempestade, garantiram seu lugar ao sol

When it comes to finding their way, this team would never drop the ball or drag their feet. Their navigation skills were always on point and they could not be way-"lei"-ed. They are a brilliant orange flame on the field, always finding their spot autonomously.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When one sees the robot, it looks like a sandcrawler. They made Archimedes proud with their lever design. Their intake sucks out the competition by being creative and not being afraid of innovation. They may need a sword but it won't be made of steel. Telescopic arms made of carbon fiber, oh… what a light concept!

The sun and the moon must be in alignment because all the other teams felt the swell. They rose above and passed through the competition on the playing field. Their example of engineering excellence poured over the weekend like a tsunami.
There are not 300 of them, but their alliance is 100 strong. Their machine shop is not a wooden horse.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team reappeared after almost being shut down. They've made a new blast, bringing us in their house. They cast their *magic* and caught us in their spell.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Their modular design is like "clockwork". Their robot compacts easily, is simple and practical, and it travels well. Even their president thinks their "robotik"/suitcase robot is cool.

The judges were impressed with this team's custom made drive train and P.I.D. control. We had our EYE on their innovation, which led to their success on the field. There is no conspiracy that this team is well deserving of this award.
They traveled from afar to build their robots. They have no place to call home. This team is 116 pixels strong.

When it comes to quality, this team hits on all levels with a streamlined roller design that stands "tall" above the rest. By CADing their design including their gearbox, then machining their parts in house, this second year team has made a bot that's hard to break.
They soar over the rest of the competition. They inspire the community using their code. Willy Wonka would be proud.

This team sees the need for worldwide outreach, not only in FIRST but in other humanitarian causes as well. They've magnified the need for diverse thought in STEM. In terms of major impact, this team has made the right contacts and made quite a spectacle.

This team embodies the FIRST spirit and soars above the field and beyond. They spread the wings throughout the community and across generations to further the mission and goals for FIRST. It is all about inspiration, enthusiasm, and celebration with EagleKits, EagleReach, and everything EagleForce.

(MC note: read this as a poem. "/" indicates line breaks.) This team in red / Shares what they know and have / To help others get ahead. / With documented templates and community events / They prove how sustainable impact can be / When students lead students.

The winners of the Autonomous Award have demonstrated exceptional mettle in robotics control. Demonstrating their prowess in tracking and scoring, they forged their way through the jungle of the field. Their open source repo shows them to be true top predators

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When ramming the cube didn’t work, this team had to get a grip. Their flexible claw provided a universal fit when it comes to creativity, this team definitely commits

This team is truly the zest when it comes to engineering excellence in the FIRST Robotics program. They’ve squeezed out some truly impressive designs with their innovative thinking, precise execution and strategic approach. Their ability to peel away problems and find creative solutions is a peeling tot both competitors and judges, and their teamwork is truly the juicy cherry on top. Their accomplishments are proof that when life gives you lemons, you can make a winning robot instead

This team embodies Gracious Professionalism on and off the field. When there are troubles, you can count on every team member to pitch in. By building a network of resources in their area, this red feathered team leverages the cardinal principles of collaboration to uplift others

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The spirits of this roaring sea of blue captivate audiences on and off the field. LED’s on their bot not only convey a cohesiveness of brand and machine, but give messages to human players mid match. Whether you believe in ghosts or not, these predators will surely catch your eyes

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Witnessing a true display of digital mastery of industrial design, this team’s ingenious blend of CNC, 3D printing, and good ‘ol hand milling blew the judges minds. The fusion of form, function and beefy hardware telescoped into our heart, leaving a vacuum of cerebral sensations to be filled with on field success

This team has skillfully split the handling of game elements, demonstrating their adaptability in the competition. Their variable speed control ensured consistent rotation in deliverying cones and cubes to the grid with precision. Added by their advanced vision system their shots hit the mark every time.

This Iron team needed to share their strength and resilience and created new ways of working and mentoring due to restrictions the world presented. From a far away land this team exhibit FIRST core values 100% of the time

This team demonstrated excellent build quality and attention to detail in their design and fabrication. Their robot endured the rigors of competition without a single breakdown. You wont find any cheesy dust on this robot

These enthusiastic activists inspire us towards a future built on accessibility, curiosity and teamwork. With 27 outreach events reaching over 6,500 students this year, this unwaveringly courageous team has spread the values of FIRST throughout their greater community. Be sure to spread the news and award you metals of honor to this armored team

This team hosted multiple events, providing opportunities for young students to learn about science, technology engineering and math. Students were exposed to the world of robotics and the ability to pursue careers in STEM education. The impact of this team was felt worldwide.. Their team members come from diverse backgrounds and possess a wide range of skills, but they work together seamlessly to push the boundaries of robotics and make a positive impact on society. This team even developed an app for scouting that is open for all teams to use. Tip you Fedoras to this team.
Two schools put this team together…. As they search for a home that would be forever. They entered into the rotation for rookie inspiration, proving a promising start

A key aspect during competition is coopertition, this team, through their non-stop cheering and screams for ALL participating teams created and environment that fostered a strong sense of camaraderie and sportsmanship among all teams . This team exemplifies Team Spirit and although there may be a specific member who loses their voice after this competition the support was heard far and wide.

This is a team that sparks STEM interest in their local community. They have a 3-year plan including a FIRST Tech Challenge to FIRST Robotics Competition pipeline and partnerships with elementary schools that demonstrates their commitment to outreach and sustainability. We are confident that this flame will continue to build an inferno as they inspire not just the engineers of today but also the engineers of tomorrow
This team was all but colorless when it came to their autonomous. This team was able to consistently place cones high up and balance well. There is no gray area in who deserves this award! Team 973!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team packed the with with industry inspiration. With UNI-FIXED strategy they roll to score! The robot really SUCKED...in cubes and cones with it's powerful vacuum. Congrats team 5817, UNI-REX!
This team DYNAMICALLY moves to capture cubes and cones, then quickly springs to towering heights in efforts to charge the power grid. With stability considered, this team is definitely a top STEED!
This colossal team was so gracious to our rookies, they could stop talking about the gifts from the heavens! Their TITAN spirit was felt throughout all the land!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Get your suitcase and travel with from the historic East Coast to the refreshing West Coast and around the world! Your tour guides are well versed in co-opertition and creativity, with a visually striking and cohesive theme from machine to team. Along your adventure you will encounter stampeding stallions or flying falcons, but none compare to the long necked Jerome the Giraffe! Congratulations Team 4738, the Patribots of San Diego, California.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot ROSE to the occasion. Their design was not HALF BAKED. As a matter of fact, you CAN stick a fork in it. Team Bread 5940 has the recipe down for Industrial Design!

You might think they would have used Orange Pi’s to get April Tags recognized, but four other computers did the trick, this lead to Woodside High as our Pick. For their innovative vision system using 4 Rapsberry Pi’s and cameras for vision and control, the judges choose the Woodside Wildhats.

As much as they enjoy winning, their priority is to foster, collaborate and build leaders. In the summer they play with bikes, make smoothies, spiking Legos and making you wonder. If they check your robot, it won't fail! They share their colorful warehouse game and code on GITHUB.
This team SOARS above the rest. Their perseverance sets this team apart, even if it meant their bot needed a second take. They're a FLOCK of experts in engineering and Quality.

This team's dedicated outreach team strives to bring engineering and stem fields to underrepresented communites. They empower girl scouts, children with learning disabilities and international students alike. Their sustained outreach efforts prove they are anything but unert.

These agents of change certainly understand how to make an impact. Their efforts translate to increased STEM accessibility not just for members of their own community, but globally. Working to better their community, the pandemic did not hinder progress but served as a call to be more productive than ever. They mobilized resources to produce free PPE for all in need. Don’t let their dark attire fool you. Working deep under cover, they engaged their local government in building an axis good to spread the FIRST mission worldwide. The FIRST impact award goes to Team 4400, Cerbotics!

Tackling all the biggest challenges FIRST, this team impressed the judges with their technical know how, hard work and enthusiasm! Setting their sights high, they charged up to meet the challenge. With continuous improvement and iteration, this team has potential in ALL categories. This more than octet of techies display an incredibly work ethic and measurable success!
Excitement abounds with this rookie team! Cyphers are their favorite or so it seems. From far away they travelled to fulfill their dream!
You saw and heard them in the stands all weekend. This team's spirit soared throughout the arena in a wave of purple, drowning the crowd in a wave of enthusiasm and inclusiveness.

This team demonstrates the FIRST mission to everyone they encounter. Their FIRST events, robotics engineering camps and open houses are inescapable. These incredible ladies have "invaded" our hearts with their presentation!

Blazing into autonomous hot off the line, this team's object detection grabbed cubes double-time. Path planning ability sure did impress, aligning cones and cubes with devilish finesse. With a button for each node, their drivers never tired, as automated placements set the scoreboard on fire.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This award goes to a team that showed us that you don't need a huge budget to build an impressive robot. They sprung into action with impressive balance as they swerved around the field. When they did fall, they picked themselves back up, and were ready to pounce again.

Engineering is a complicated process with many twists and turns. This team utilized advanced math, trade studies, and many prototypes to determine their final cybernetic designs. Rick Deckard has nothing on this team as they rose to the top of the automaton pack.

This team lent a paw, a claw and a saw When the bagels needed more than a bite. If anyone needs to learn quickly, they’ll provide you with a wiki. Whether in the pit or on the field of play, Omnicats can balance and charge up all day!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This teams image makes you aware and you can’t help but stare When they blend the team with the machine With the bowtie and pink to make you think!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Striking a balance between function and form, like choosing where to score. Rome wasn't built in a day, maybe it took 3. Come on up here, Nerd Herd is me.

Control is important for any robot, but when you have a truly unique mechanism, you need a unique control scheme to go with it. Every team needs to keep make sure their robot stays pointed in the right direction. This award goes to the only team whose robot could point in two directions at once.

The judges want to recognize a hard-working team that arrived here only to find they needed to trim a few thorns from their robot. But much more than that, they are tirelessly working to make the most of opportunities and inspire change in their community. The judges recognize them as role models, for changing lives through careful tending of stems in their community. Thanks to them, the concrete is a bit more colorful in Watts.

This team's robot really stood out on the field. However, it was their design process that really swung the judges' decision in their favor. When it comes to building robots, this team doesn't monkey around.

This team demonstrates tremendous respect for other teams and their community. They host a collaborative kickoff workshop and open scrimmages to support FRC competimates. They also hold summer camps for hundreds of “young engineers” from 4th to 8th grade, with inspiring projects like investigating DNA. Further, they team with industry to hold diversity dialogs and a neurodiversity panel. They are truly renaissance people!

This team has a long-standing mission to change the image of engineering and engineers in their community. With that in mind, they have demonstrated success in bringing people into FIRST who might otherwise never have had the opportunity to know or develop their love for technology. A survey of their alumni showed 100% pursuing higher education, a significant change from the general rate for their school. The team is a reliable friend to many other FRC teams across our region and has assured continuity and continued expansion of FIRST through engagement with FTC and FLL team and events, leveraging a focus on women in STEM. But FIRST itself in just the start for them: the team is a role model as a tireless supporter of Boys and Girls Club events, Hispanics in STEM, and homeless elementary school students. They are an inspiration to us for concentrating on their strengths to overcome the challenges they face, while guiding other FRC teams to follow in their nerdy footsteps.

This rookie team had just a few weeks to build their robot, and they rose to the challenge. While here at the competition, they have even been 3D printing their own pins to hand out. After their first big bite of FRC, we hope to see these sharks back next year

These hawks flew a long way to show their pride here. When they are not building robots, they are building rockets and helping war refugees. In cold weather, they keep looking fabulous in their fashionable scarves.

This team clearly understands the overall goal of FIRST. It realizes that goal is not just for this year, but for the very long run to produce scientists and engineers. This team has a very disciplined program to groom interest in middle school students with science fair presentations and their "Hopper the Dreamer" comic book.

Clever teams utilize autonomous programming, even when their robot is remotely controlled. This team LIGHTS THE PATH for others by sharing their pose-estimation code as open source. With IRON CLAWS, this student-built and student-run team is ready to POUNCE.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: A Proximal strategy for a Distal affect on the field, this team designed a custom complex roll-jointed arm that folds compactly into the center of their robot using simple gears and pulleys. A high-speed vision system connected the mechanics and controls for on-field elegance and speed.

This high-standards team wasn’t satisfied so they constructed a shorter arm to reduce errors, rigorously tested their wiring to prevent failure, and installed four cameras to assure precision game piece placement… everytime. Their BREAKTHROUGH robot now RISES to the CHALLENGE with superior performance while still looking good.

Amidst the fierce competition, one team stood out for their dedication to collaboration and sportsmanship. When faced with a situation where their moniker could have rung all to true, they chose to rise above and embrace the spirit of FIRST. Taking responsibility for an accidental collision, they swiftly offered their support and resources to repair any damage. With an exemplary attitude towards field staff and referees, they gracefully accepted any penalties and embodied the essence of fair play.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has masterfully blended their cultural inspiration with their passion for robotics, creating a truly captivating visual experience. They used their rebranding to foster a more inclusive and inviting atmosphere for their entire community, maintaining an homage to their original school mascot. The bold use of purple unifies their identity, connecting the team and their impressive machine, while giving a subtle nod to the majestic highlands that inspire them.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: In a world where mythical creatures inspire brilliance, one team has harnessed the power of a legendary fusion. Their black and orange-clad creation showcases clean wiring, an elegant and practical design, and a smooth linear rail system. By changing their intake, they've ensured that the competition is left in the dust, proving that this PREHISTORIC powerhouse doesn't suck...but it does ROAR.
So many great bots are ripping up the field. Will humans ever keep up? Though this team mastered automatic traverse of the field, they put it to the test – bot versus human. Score one for humanity

A team can have it all, or a team can lose before the competition even starts. The judges would like to recognize a team that could have rolled over, but they had both the FAITH and the BOLTS to get it together. And they played their hearts out.

This team took full ownership over their robot quality from the design plan all the way to the machining. They enforced checkpoints throughout the season to ensure prototypes either matured or were abandoned before reaching the robot. They pride themselves on building everything in-house, even swerve modules, so they can guarantee the quality of the components they use. When the judges visited, they found the team deep in GRR-UTS (sound like “guts”) of their robot, replacing a loose component that they found during a post-match checklist.

This team is working hard toward an ambitious goal. Not only are they building innovative robots, but they are working to transform a culture. They understand that not all learning can be done through books which is why these COOL CATS are working through all levels of their government to promote STEM and FIRST.

This team has organized outreach events, led workshops, hosted competitions, and sponsored teams - building strong FIRST LINKAGES everywhere they go. Their strong advocacy for STEM with their local government has impacted countless people and driven real change. Their focus on mentorship and accessibility reaches many in their surrounding isolated communities. They are truly NUTS about the FIRST mission and THEY are the change we love to see!

This team came together from their surrounding community with a shared passion for STEM and robots. They are already EMPOWERING the next generation by mentoring local FLL teams. Their first robot also has a few TRICKS up its sleeve to help make them an effective competitor. ABRA-CA-DABRA here is our Rookie All-Star winner.

When you look across the field, the sea of red and black stands out, making it clear that this team is truly united. Their unwavering support for their alliance partners is evident, as they energetically join in on cheers and chants. This team not only displays their own spirit, but they amplify the enthusiasm of those around them, OVERLOADING the stands with contagious energy.

This team has demonstrated ingenuity by growing their team membership with a focus on diversity. While doing that, they also built up their support base with current and new sponsors. This team’s old lab was a giant, leaky mess, and home to lots of drama. So, it was demolished and the team moved into TWO shipping containers and a shed, where they remain to this day, fighting through the rain and the mud to develop their robot.
The battle to raise the stakes charged their game Their high performance robot blended sensors, code and mechanics collected high winnings They rolled the dice and the cards were in their favor

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: (note to emcee: read the last two sentences “their…impressive” in a Darth Vader voice) Taking risks is nothing new for this team. Always reach high and keeping their eyes on the prize, this team went with the twists and turns. Their creativity is impressive. Most impressive.

This deserving team has impressed the judges with their utterly clean, simple, and robust design and package. The design looks very elegant and maneuvers stealth-like as a star-wars droid floating on the field of battle. Try not to tip them over.

(notes to emcee: read this in a rap manner) They’re gentle, they’re kind Orange you glad they’re not hard to find Because they help lots of others Their gracious professionalism abounds When the pits close They always stick around Okay… *mic drop* goodnight.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.teamName: Victorian Engineered Robotic Nation or V.E.R.N.
records.script: This team not only stands out on the field but also in the stands. A blast from the past, with a futuristic twist, their robot has sleek wooden features. When you hear steam punk you think of them.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: (notes for emcee: Walk around field and Meow And Purr like a CAT while reading the script) This team has de-meow-strated that when it comes to balance, aesthetic and efficiency they always land on their feet. They are the Paw-fect example of a real world industrial product.
This team impressed the judges by CHAMPIONING the control of the robot. Their innovative use of current monitoring to detect the capture of a game piece let them CHARGE to success.
This team fought against all odds in order to compete in this year’s competition. From working within an accelerated timeline to keeping spirits high. These Samurais are located closer to home!
This smooth robot is so well-oiled it never squeaks. When it’s mechanical arm waves, it is out of this world. We are big FINS of this far out design of astronautic quality.

This year’s engineering inspiration award goes to a team that is a shining light for science and technology in their community. Their lion-like commitment resulted in over 1000 hours impacting students from grades K through 12 to better their community. The judges look forward to seeing this team soaring high in the future.

This team aims to make STEM accessible for everyone — with outreach to Girl Scouts/Boy Scouts, special education students, and bringing hope and advocacy to teams that would not otherwise have this support. While bringing everyone along for the ride, this pack parades their excitement in STEM in everything they do. That includes sharing with sponsors, fellow teams, and their local community. They are hauntingly impressive — their alliance with FLL teams is established and growing through STEM development courses and Arizona Native American communities. The cat is out of the bag!
They came together with a poi-pose With a commitment to science and technology this group just clicked Rookies all, they would not let their aspirations come to a fin

This team’s commitment to spirit and awe, Was something contagious and one could see from afar A breeze from the west, a kiss from the sun Made a tropical paradise for everyone. It’s not Tommy Bahama, And no, don’t call your Mama, From the Fire and Ice It’s Mechanical Paradise!

The team sustainability award goes to a team that lights up their community attracting all to join them. Their students are fueled up to excel in their field and burn brightly in the competition. This team has built up a fire that will go on for ages.

This team blinded us with science when they showed us how they integrated their autonomous functionality into the rest of their code. You got autonomous in my teleop, you got teleop in my autonomous. And all that without changing out of their pajamas.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: (MC note: we highly encourage you to sing this.) This team's unique mechanism spun us right 'round, baby, right 'round. Like a record, baby, right 'round, 'round, 'round.

This team had an effective and well-integrated mechanism that was so unique that we initially weren't sure what it was for. It was as impressive as the rest of their performance when they used it on the field, though. It helped them work with their teammates to climb to the top spot.

This team understands the spirit of FIRST is to energize the competition by spreading their arms wide to other FRC teams. They redefined STEAM to uplift diverse voices in the community. In the best tradition of renaissance engineering, this team honors their namesake.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Among all the teams, one rose higher than the rest. Their team dynamic was consistent across the team and machine. No contradiction here, winning this award is certainly not a paradox.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's sleek robot impressed the judges with their component integration, fit, and finish. It reminds us of a stealth fighter as it zips across the field and flies over the charge station. It's a GREYT robot from a GREYT team.

FIRST Robotics is an excellent learning experience for students. However, one team was able to cut precious seconds off of their cycle times by building a machine that could learn for itself. This made them stand out in the sea of other robots.

Good design is often clean and simple, particularly when resources are limited. This team decided that they would create a robot that was devilishly clean, from its little horns to its wheels. For showing it can be a gift to be simple, we give this team the judges’ award.
This robot fits together like a swiss watch. And its machining is almost as intricate. And it would *almost* fit in your pocket.

All teams had to pack it in... but this team literally packed it in their luggage. When they are at home they inspire education in youth and the principles of FIRST. They are red hot like molten lava.

This team's engineering leadership redesigns a robotic safety feature / while mentoring that it is okay to make mistakes, like setting your robot on fire / but the book they published isn't FOUR the birds!

This team’s spirit and cohesive identity is apparent in their bot, their pit, and moreover in the pride they have for their team. Their passions flew high and their spirit BLUE us away. For their persistent enthusiasm, this team is receiving the team spirit award.

The sustainability award recognizes a team that creates a long-term stable ecosystem for itself. This team saw that the broader state and community around them was dry as a desert after the challenges of the last several years. This team brought back some diamonds to be a catalyst for expanding FIRST not just for themselves, but for their home state. For their work in growing FIRST throughout Arizona, we award this team the sustainability award.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Detecting small power changes sent these travelers to the top of their three tier telescope. To avoid problems with wheels slipping, our intrepid adventurers developed a unique software solution. Their four different auto modes compete with game pieces in hand, ready to play. Just like their original namesake, they are the fastest hunk of junk in the gallery.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Taking the right pieces to the right place and scoring was a challenge for all. This team accomplished that consistently and smoothly with a unique catch and release innovation. With a novel intake hopper and the ability to catapult objects back with precision to score. There were no lemons in their creative approach, just oranges.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: We don’t want this team to feel Blue as they developed a very strong design process, material analysis and feasibility studies to enable success. Their engineering discipline drove a modular design that made project management easy and not claw fight.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team recognized that so many teams were struggling that they proactively started watching matches to identify robots that needed help, and offering pit crew support whenever they can. Whether they provide spare parts or help with repairs or coding fixes, this team wants every team to perform to the very best of their ability. With a heart of gold this team is better recognized by their preferred metal . . . Aluminum.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: We have READ that this team colored the competition by keeping things simple. You’ll be BLUE if you were looking for any secondary colors on this robot They have harnessed the color YELLOW which is associated with sunshine and energy and makes it easy to see this team glow. Making it complex by keeping it simple isn’t a Paradox to this team.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Who would have thought that herd mentality could produce such a well-designed robot? This simple, elegant design is a terror on the field, scoring points while displaying flying colors and solid construction. The team continues to expounded FIRST practices throughout their development process, creating a significant moo-vment within their school.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Making the driver’s job easy was the primary focus of this great control system. By combing multiple cameras and sensors with a single button push, this team’s robot can auto-align from any location to any target. As their name makes clear, they quickly move from place to place, never staying anywhere too long.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team overcame some unique challenges and demonstrated perseverance by forging a path forward, expanding their passion for STEM and creating a Bot out of almost nothing. They are a true embodiment of “It takes a Village. . . “ This Samurai has risen to the occasion ..

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Despite this year’s fierce competition one team’s quality stood out from the rest. Their attention to detail and commitment to excellence was evident in every aspect of their robot. From the fine parts craftsmanship to the impressive three jointed arm and color aware intake, this team left no stone unturned in their pursuit of excellence. Gearbox placement was strategic and efficient, allowing for optimal performance on the field. It’s clear that this team’s hard work and dedication has paid off.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: From the moment you meet any of this team’s members you get inspired by their FRC program depth. Spending nearly 4000 hours volunteering this year, all of their team members have mentored inside and outside their community and fueling 7 FLL teams into existence. Whether you look east or have a WESTVIEW you will find more than a dozen options on how this team has been inspiring others

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: From little ones to seniors, this team embodies all of FIRST’s goals and objectives under their expansive wingspan. Giving their blood, sweat and tears for their country, while innovating to save the environment worldwide, This team rises from the ashes once again to display its aura.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: The winners displayed infectious and inclusive enthusiasm for STEM and FIRST. This teams resonates with their sponsors, mentors, students and outreach participants as a unified community, which powered them to take flight. Their spirit doesn’t just build good robots, they build good people

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: These warblers sung to the judges their plan for sustainability while honoring FIRST’s principles. They wrote a user’s manual for an obsolete CNC machine and wowed the judges with their speaker series for women into STEM. We expect this Nightingale song will be heard long into the future.

Whether cone, cube, or balance, with their innovative autonomous modules, this team can strike like an eagle and dynamically approach their target. As a team, they can navigate even the toughest skies.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's robot is capable of reaching any goal. This team managed to accomplish this with a fraction of the space of other robots, telescoping to score and compete reliably with bigger contenders.

This team started the season with a clear goal, well-prioritized work, and rigorously-tested requirements. Early design and organization enabled the team to build a robot with impressive autonomous capabilities and elegant scoring capacity. Their robot's agile movement, stable base, and freedom to score in any goal exemplify their professional, exceptional approach to engineering and design.

This team is a gracious host inside and outside the competition. They don't just care for their team members - they care for the FIRST community. They bring nearby teams together for a multi-team kickoff season, supercharging everyone with ideas to carry on into their build season. Be it a part, a shop, a PR system, they're only a Slack away from helping. They've built a personal brand on Gracious Professionalism and keep their doors open to help during kickoff, build, and competition. To this minute, they are still welcoming teams into their collaborative network.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: On a crusade for a simple aesthetic, this team embraced their school’s color and mascot. Wearing shirts with purple logos, this team matched their streamlined bot’s purple tape scheme and their pit decor.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This bot was synthesized in a lab with a balance between form and function. It is well-wired, has swappable arms, and a creative-yet-reliable cone shooter. This team proved they are more than a heavyweight on the periodic table.

With a full view of the field in their corner, this team is able to accurately detect the position of cones and cubes with great skill. Sniffing out the game pieces with their BeagleBone, this team showed its tenacity in being able to knock out the competition.

Teams are often inspired by the same ideas and end up with similar designs as a result. However, this team had to overcome unique challenges, including language barriers and limited access to the FRC community, and they developed a unique robot as a result. They welded together a crane-like machine using parts from a DIY laser cutter, and the judges enjoyed watching their *AERIAL* autonomous routine every match.

This team did the math, and used their coding and CAD skills to design in redundancy, rigidity, and reliability. As an example, their easily-replacable wiring enabled a fast swap to their end effector. Their overall approach enabled their robot to easily survive the rigors of competition.

The first thing you notice when you talk to this team is their clarity of purpose, which stretches tip-to-tail through their program. Teaching is the goal above all else, and it steers everything from how they train new members through building 1-on-1 relationships with value-aligned sponsors who will support them in the long run. Realizing they could go farther than merely training their entire school, these cold-blooded educators sank their teeth into the problem and partnered with an after-school program to expand their low-cost robotics kits to communities who couldn't access programs like FLL. They work in the community to give other reptiles an example that looks like them, inspiring their others to see themselves with a future in STEM.

This team has shined a light both inside and outside of the robotics community. Their exceptional lobbying and outreach efforts resulted in the successful passing of legislation to increase robotics funding in the area. In addition, they recognized a lack of engagement among students from under-represented groups and took action by creating lasting programs that have had measured effects on promoting diversity in their organization and bringing STEM to underserved communities. Through their innovation and dedication, they have made a meaningful impact on the robotics community and have inspired others to do the same. For their exceptional achievements, the Impact Award goes to Team 115 - MVRT.

This team took every part of the FIRST mission and manual to heart and was determined to offer a STEAM opportunity to every single student on their campuses, regardless of background. Combining their ambition, multicultural clubs, and FIRST Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion resources, they won the hearts of 14 sponsors and partners. Their enthusiasm even sparked their peers and community to support their efforts to spark up a children's Lego Mindstorms workshop. Their ability to make the most of what they had and excel was not only evident in the consistent success of their robot, but also in the creation of their team and it's community presence.

Charged up with their STEM skills, they amplified their impact by going out to their community. If you're out in the neighborhood, you may have found them under the shopping center's Christmas lights, showcasing STEM-related hobbies. Or you might've stepped inside their "Fix-it Clinic" to get your sewing machine fixed. You can see them sitting with kids at a STEM camp, or walk with them in support of Women of Impact.

With a diverse membership, this team has striven to build a “brave space” – where everyone is encouraged to speak up whether calling out issues or asking for help. This team wears their uniform safari themed shirts to celebrate their school mascot and cheers loudly whether celebrating birthdays, team achievements or more. There are no cowardly lions here.

With a clear emphasis on leadership at all levels, this team makes sure they have the process needed to keep going. Lifting themselves up by their *bootcamps*, their students teach younger students, yielding a 75% continuation rate onto their FRC team. In fact, this is so successful that new students admitted to the school report it as a prime motivator for their enrollment. Documentation emphasizing the rules of design makes continuation a cinch, and sponsors get the message with a one-on-one, hands-on approach. They might seem janky, but we think they'll be here for years to come.
Their Autonomous functions blend into tele-op MODE, with a virtual field to make it easier to CODE. Testing autos with quite a bit of REPETITION, this team “knocked out” the COMPETITION.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: A robot with a nose in TOW, The team soars high, ready to THROW. They are effective, fast, and NIMBLE, A single degree of freedom, keeps it SIMPLE. They’ve got the moves, the style, the FUNK, 3 DOF, 2 DOF, 1 DOF, DUNK!

Ahead of the curve, not breaking DOWN, Their process is iterative and RENOWNED. The “laterator”, well-DESIGNED, Keeps them ahead, time after TIME. Their success, you cannot SPOOF, Congrats to Team 254, Cheesy POOFS.

These past few years have seen a tremendous impact to our lives. It is a BREATH OF FRESH AIR to see this team going to the EDGE to ensure we are all enjoying a safe and welcoming event. Their love for volunteers and fellow teams are exemplified in their pins, safety maps, and invitations to “clear our minds” in an otherwise busy world. We agree this team brings Gracious Professionalism to a new dimension!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Light blue, solid in their GEARS, Strong and light, tempered over the YEARS, This team has impeccable VISION, And SHARPENING their brand is their MISSION, Their sponsor integration is a real TREAT, But we know you’re all on the EDGE of your SEAT. For their great work and creative INGENUI-TY, Congrats to Titanium Robotics, Eleven SIX-TY.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With remarkably simple systems and a clean design, This team impressed us with their success. From design to execution, bolts to blueprints, and redesign to re-execution, this bot does the most with the BEAST, With a bite that burns, this winning team ELEVATED themselves to the top of the competition.

This team’s robot control has the precision of lighting BOLT, their innovative arm comes out the side of the bot, with a JOLT! Automatically getting cubes and cones in the correct orientation with a “FLIP”, talking to this team is a lighting-powered TRIP!

The judges were really IMPRESSED, with their steed, moving in DARKNESS, Stronger than STEEL, light as a FEATHER, The competition, they can WEATHER. From the stands you can hear the SUCTION, Their carbon design with powerful CONSTRUCTION.
This zesty team, robust and STRONG, Extendo arm is fast and LONG, superb quality you might well KNOW, The citrus team with a lime green GLOW.

This team boasts a robust internal training and mentorship program, ensuring that new members quickly find their “sea legs”. They advocate for STEM education in their local community, securing national funding, and empowering other teams to join them. Their “fluid” approach to Outreach “washes” over language barriers by teaching conversation skills. And by joining forces with international teams, they reach well beyond their shores. Their commitment continues to make “waves” with medical partnerships. "Go baby go"!

This team’s impact will leave you in TEARS, With all those they have helped across the YEARS. Their documentation was quite extensive and showed the breadth of their REACH, In three years, twenty-three hundred students they did TEACH. Taking Lego robotics to a new HEIGHT, They turned it into therapy, vocational training, and a shining LIGHT. Saving a FRC regional with funding and SPACE, This team is many-a-student’s home and safe PLACE. To create opportunities and transform communities, this team does STRIVE, Please join us and congratulate team five-nine-eight-FIVE!

Starting with just a few members, they grew with a shared interest in engineering and robotics. Impressing the judges with their leadership potential, innovative thinking, and problem solving abilities, this team actively reached out and collaborated with both local and international teams. This team flew across the Pacific Ocean and demonstrate a strong community engagement by hosting events to promote STEM education.

The judges were impressed with the amazing engineering design process this team developed. Having overcome funding issues due to a delayed start, the team pushed through to deliver a robot not only amazing, but also inspiring. Promoting a positive, diverse, and welcoming community, the judges HOPPED with joy when they saw the BUNNY EARS.

With their bot, they glide and SPIN, Their moves so fluid, we can’t help but GRIN In their outfits they dance with GRACE, In formal attire they own the PLACE It’s amazing how they make it SPEAK, With their robot’s penguin BEAK.

This team’s sustainability is a sure BET, with mission goals that are well SET. With training & recruiting that goes the whole year ROUND, their budgeting philosophy ensures their future is safe and SOUND.

This team *swept us off our feet* with their incredible use of autonomous control. Everyone can *sea* their autonomous features were a key feature in their robot design and performed consistently all weekend long. This robot was a complete *tsunami* on the field.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Judges flipped out over this team's robot. This creative design helped them rotate around the competition. This team didn't have Miles Morales or Peter Parker to swing in, but their unique wrist impressed the judges.
This team's approach to robot design lit up the field. The robot match play pulverized out the competition like the purple root of their home state. It's solution to charge up didn't fork it up.
Many teams depend on local hosts to compete. This team's hospitality runs full circle. Hear the lion roar, join the Circuit of Life.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Fly through the air, visit their pit and play their game. With bright colors on the outside, we know they are good to the CORE. Doompity-doo, we've got a perfect award for you.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team is so optimized that their team name is an acronym. Just like a transformer, this robot is modular, similar to the famous autobot, bumblebee. Their robot's striking balance sings just like a nightingale.
To win the Innovation in Control Award, it's important to always stay on track. However, this team proved that not all who wander are lost.
This team may not be from the wild west, but their robot roped the judges in. Their ability to corral cubes made them soar above the rest. Even when the floods came, these Eagles persevered.

Everything about this team's design process and robot exudes quality. Their robot *blue* us away with its good cable management, swerve guards, electronics cover, crush blocks, and more. Their goals of serviceability, durability, and robustness aren't Greek to us.
This team went to Washington. With their talons they secured funding for robotics for all. They are a "FAMILY" that is passionate about helping ALL students learn. SOARING to new heights...

Making a national impact, this team makes it LOUD! You can trust this team to lend a sympathetic ear but the team doesn't keep secrets. You know this team from an open alliance forum. 10 years in the making, a charged-up steamup playground - this team makes an impact.

The judges were super impressed by these sea creatures, even though they are they only fish in this pond. From building a winning robot to the science fair they are headed to next month, we know they will serve FIRST well into the future.
Make it loud, that's what we've come to expect at competition. Their megaphone, numbers, and voices all let us know they're here. When I say 21, you say (02).

This group of scholars is pumping new life into their team by reorganizing their system to improve the flow of knowledge. Documentation is at the heart of this team. Always looking professional in their lab coats.

This team's robot had a hands off approach, leveraging autonomous capabilities throughout a match. In autonomous mode they consistently scored twice in the grid, and even balanced on the charging station after that. Alexander Graham would have been proud of their carbon fiber arm.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their robot is as strong as a bull. Creative use of an arm on a swivel makes it highly efficient and versatile. They came from an area known for the mountains and a presidential retreat.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This rookie team has a solidly built robot that was part of a winning alliance at a district qualifying event. This rookie team started a new FLL team in their school this year. Kickstarted by FIRST Alumni, this team roared their way to the championship!
This team easily articulated their design journey. With their low center of gravity they zip across the field. Whether at rest or in motion, these Newtons end the game in style.

Graciousness in competition is a is quality that has stood the test of time. This team has demonstrated CIVITAS at every step of their journey in the FIRST Chesapeake District this year. This team might best be remembered by the phrase SPECTEMUR AGENDO, "let us be judged by our acts."

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team exudes their theme, in the pits, stands, and on their robot. You are sure to have seen the aquatic creatures throughout the competition. They aren't "koi" about it.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot was durable, sturdy, and unstoppable on the field. This team's detailed design documentation and clean fabrication led to a well-performing design. With their protected copper wiring they slither across the field.
Control of the robot can be a complex and intercoordinated job. Their team twisted itself into knots to make their robot perform. For this team, third time's the charm.

This team charged into a "stylish" new project. It may not have been "fashionable," but they dedicated half their team to a community need during build season and became a true role "model." When in Rome, do as the Spartans do... they give back!
This team towered over the field scoring cones on all levels. Their clean robust design was the epitome of quality throughout the robot. Whether alone or in a colony, this team stayed afloat.

With a nearly 20 year history in FRC, this team focuses their passion for STEM to help other young people achieve that "aha!" moment of excitement. This team is so proud that they AND other teams use their STEM lessons not just in the FIRST Chesapeake area, but also in West Virgina and Pennsylvania. This team has partnered with the Smithsonian Institution and a museum in Kentucky, who both teach this team's STEM lessons, DAILY.

Representing more than 100,000 students in their county, this team has a large base of students to share their love of STEM with. They successfully recruited and grew their team by triple in the last two years. They have both a summer camp and virtual camps teaching STEM concepts, created by and led by this team's members. Hosting one of the largest off-season events with 35 teams in 2022 , this team knows how to do outreach to their community.

With workshops and mentoring FLL teams, this team does it all. They are working with Congress to help spread the message of FIRST. They read along with Pre-Schoolers about GERALD, and making them crazy about STEM.
Grants and Camps and FIRST LEGO League, Oh My! This team ensures that everyone has access to STEM. So "COME WHEN YOU CAN" and celebrate with these amazing Titans of robotics.

This team came with their heads and spirits held high. They worked with other teams to get their robot ready for the fierce battles that awaited them. As novices on the field, they learned and excelled at being better for the future.
This team raises the roof with their cheers. They are always willing to lend a helping hand to teams having a ruff day. These DAWGS Bolt to the stands to howl for everyone.

This team maintains a strong pipeline of future STEM professionals by maintaining FTC teams, VEX teams, and summer programs. They are quick to recruit at outreach events in the air, space, and in the bay. Through training, new members SWARM to all aspects of FRC.
At the start of each match, this team had a bird’s eye view of the field. Their custom path generation leads to game proficiency and endless possibilities. The iceman cometh for its award.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: From the Pacific Northwest comes a creative force. This team used various household items to help solve their engineering challenges. With their cat-like sensors and flight controls, this team is ready to sting!

As a competitor in their natural habitat comes an engineering animal. Through custom designed and fabricated components, they have a definite advantage. This “Monumental” team gave the competition more than it could “bear”.

This team is extraordinary in SO many ways. In the last two decades, this team has demonstrated that their outreach and assistance extends off the field, for example, setting up a 501c3 that sponsored six other teams. Don’t confuse their rock star tattooed look, this team has specific people in their group to assist others during the competition - they deserve a big fat kiss.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: These spirited robotics enthusiasts travel far and wide, spreading the joy of learning wherever they go. With their beautifully designed training kits they make robotics fun for all. Their tall and funky Cubie ambassador puts smiles on everyone’s faces and inspires the next generation of technical wizards.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When designing a robot, this team focuses on what lies beneath. Their data logging, robust design, and modularity ensure this bot won't CRACK. This award was snatched by their giant maw.

This team demonstrated a BOULDER approach to achieve sensory integration. Giving them “A” FRAME of reference that set them apart. Their point of view came a long way to reach the PEAK of Innovation in control.

Out on the plains, there were no bots to be seen. A team arrived to spread STEM and the spirit of FIRST across the land. Astronauts have inspired youth for many generations, and these students are carrying on that legacy.

These brilliant minds are a force to be reckoned with. Their commitment to quality has not only resulted in an exceptional end product but also a streamlined and efficient process. They are a powerhouse and set the bar high for all those who strive for quality in their work.

From the slopes of the far west comes a team that lifts and inspires. Their education, training, and community outreach are hands down the best. Incubating new levels of STEM within their community they make all of the schools in the Grand Valley proud.

This experienced team rocks inclusivity and fosters an environment where every student belongs and is well-utilized. Their legislative advocacy work obtained the funds to help after-school STEM activities SOAR. Their work changing the system for kids on the spectrum is “Building a Better Tomorrow.”

This team started with a walk and now gallops through the competition. Even a door stop could not get in their way. This team’s move to expand from FTC to FRC proved that their workhorse Charlie could compete with the big boys!

This team is not for the birds and soars to promote STEM, inspires new members and learning. Their team and mentors are spreading their wings, developing new curriculums and paths to new opportunities. They will not get Rusty flying to higher FIRST achievements and team goals.
People say teamwork makes the dream work. Their enthusiasm and energy revved up the arena. They didn’t need Harleys, Top hats, or bows to impress us with their contagious team spirit.

Year after year, these people build off of their mammoth foundation. This team swats away their challenges and boosts their community. Activity downloads, bearhugs, and rubber chickens are just a part o f their growing arsenal for sustainability.
