records.script: This team's robot knew exactly where it was going here in Hartford. Cardinal directions and multiple cameras to see the field and game pieces allowed smooth and quick operation. Operation as smooth and quick as this proved to the judges that this robot had MOJO.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's unique gripper really stood out to the judges. When this team needed an automated pickup they tested multiple design solutions. Turns out all they needed was a piece of floss. Congratulations to Team 3146.

One word to describe this team is “Enthusiastic”. With this team learning is an expectation, and everyone has a chance to lead. Dreaming about ways to engage the community, exploring new opportunities for development, and aspiring to get the younger generation involved, this team understands and celebrates the mission of FIRST.

How do you define / measure impact? This team is a poster child for humility. There efforts are continuous demonstrate that even small asteroids can have a large impact. They operate so far under the radar that no one knows where they are, but they sure make a splash. Their international outreach is such a success that the school system created special curriculum so the entire school could benefit from the outreach. They are the I in I-Labs This is not just a team they are a Tsunami.

This team's engineering really impressed the judges. With swerve drive, a super arm and multiple autonomous routes this robot was ready for battle. It's ability to consistently perform on the field made them a knight in shining armor for any alliance.

When other teams sent out an SOS, this team heeded the call. Their members are always happy to help other FIRST teams so much so that they are frequently seen in other teams pits more than their own. On and off the field, they are Ram-positive.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team was very wise with their theming choices and thoroughly impressed the judges. From head to toe to their robot and pits, this team's theming has even charged up their batteries. With their "owl"-encompassing aesthetics this team's imagery has them flying forward above the rest.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: No, this Mercedes of robots was not built in Germany. It was "Made in the USA". This robot's robust and elegant design takes advantage of nu,erous advanced technology and is wired for success. Climbing to success, this robot is not "boar"ing at all.

With a clear aim for their robot in 1's and 0's this team took complicated concepts and took the competition by storm. From linear interpolations to advanced feedback loops, this team saw a birdseye view to success. This year many robots swerve, but a select few soared.
This team's resilience has paid off with astronomic growth. Their dedication to engagement at all levels just blew the judges away. Although this team is on vacation, they're not "dragon" their feet.

Top to bottom this team carefully designed their robot with quality in mind. With multiple versions of their lift and gripper, their final robot is both robust and good-looking. From machining frame members to powder coating their final design, these pirates floated to the top of the class.
This team celebrates the little things, even if it's just movement. Their enthusiasm is infectious, and can be felt through the whole competition. So let out a howl, 'cause here comes the Huskies!

Sparkly in both their robot and personalities, this team enthusiasm is infectious. From their appearance on the field, to their robot, and put design this team celebrates the individuals behind the robot. Spirit is in their blood.

This team has a solid business plan to fund their vision of the future. These money magament masters ensure FIRST can be for anuone. When it comes to this team, it's family, school, robotics, forever.

To the untrained eye, it appeared to be slight of hand. On one hand, the robot gathered the pieces, with the other hand it positioned the pieces for transport and placement. This robots’ strong sensor package enabled it to score in all autonomous categories. The eyes of this robot guided itself to just the right location for gathering pieces during play. It wasn’t slight of hand, but it certainly looked like magic.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The team being recognized for the Creativity Award was definitely the “cream of the crop.” While many teams planned to avoid failures, this team created failures, pushing the team to quickly respond to any situation. Once the competition began, it was easy as pie!

Why do FIRST? Why bring FIRST into the community? This team has integrated the values of FIRST into their community through their volunteering and community outreach. This Team infects their community with their understanding and enthusiasm for FIRST and has seamlessly woven FIRST into the school and community. Small Team. Big impact. In their words… Do better through engineering.

In order to succeed, we must first believe that we can. -Believe in yourself -Believe in your friends -Believe in your mission In their words…. “Energy flows through a circuit, but only if that circuit is connected properly. Likewise, knowledge can flow if those within it support the flow.” So what if they are girls- they are going to change the world anyway.

This team carefully planned and placed every piece of their robot. Their analysis, custom designs, and cleverly engineered rotating tower ensure smooth operation on the field. This team clearly practices engineering and showed excellent competitive cooperation.
You name a level of FIRST, this team is there. Hosting events, mentoring, STEM advocacy, outreach, both local and global. Would Woody be inspired by their wave of inspiration? Absolutely! To the Max.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This Hartford Native team won over the judge's hearts with their outstanding visual presentation. We give them the orange peel of approval.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Good design requires a team to go all in, even when they are not dealt the best cards. This teams’ design and modern lines gave balance to form, function, and aesthetics. In fact, we might say they pulled a full house, Aces High.

Bob the Builder couldn’t have done a better job of designing and hand building this control station. The modular design allowed this team to adapt to any challenge. The unique driver display provided the driver excellent vision. The control layout of this robot turned it into a feline predator on the field.

Every once in a while, a team's spark lights up the whole room! As a small but August team, these participants made the most of every interaction, impressing all of the judges! We just know that your spark is on the way to a full flame, and choose to recognize you for your perseverance and can-do attitude.

This team planned to build a robust robot from the start. An array of sensors helped this robot navigate the field. Material choice and crumple zones ensured continued operation when the going got tough. Gale force winds couldn’t keep this robot down.
Out of our rookie teams, this team impressed the judges with their commitment to FIRST and its values. This team was selected because of its enthusiasm towards learning and developing as a team.

This team demonstrates the drive to nurture STEM and robotics in their community. Instilling a robotics presence in their school, they have big dreams to further their school’s science curriculum. It would not be a shock to see this team achieve great things in the future.

This year's team stood out to the judges for their commitment and community outreach to help mentor and fundraise for FLL programs and your efforts to partner and build relationships with other FRC teams to further the reach of FIRST Robotics. Your team spirit truly shined through your support of teamwork and partnerships! You exemplify the passion of what makes FIRST team successful, and your enthusiasm is infectious!
This team has a clear approach to achieving the team's goals toward operating and improving. Their commitment to continuous development rammed over the competition.

records.script: This team has a robot consistently able to navigate across the field, and complete multiple objectives during the autonomous period. This Robot can sense its surroundings, auto-orient objects, autonomously race to scoring position, and prove that even the most mysterious ecosystems can produce extraordinary innovators. Let's celebrate the team that has risen from the bog, capturing our admiration with their swamp-tastic abilities!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Creative risk entails RUNNING WILD in the design space. Compact gears and motors ensure a RAPID GALLOP in competition. This team’s risky small design manages to be as STRONG AS A STALLION.

This team counted notch by notch and link by link in designing their elevator to be above the field. As they were faced with many engineering obstacles, they balanced on the edge by digging in their claws.
This team is on a roll. They make sure all teams have the tools for success. If you need help, this team is ready to Ninjassist.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has an out of this world aesthetic, from their machine to pits to students. Across Orlando Regional’s rocky competitive terrain, this mega awesome team earns a cosmic oration for providing interstellar Martian visuals to us all!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team ROLLS over any obstacle, by resisting complexity. Their passive intake acquires and orients the game objects. From there, a unique air-powered gripper grabs both the cubes and cones to score. They’re CHARGING up the GRID by harnessing the power of the sun.
Innovation is about the SPEED of change, while control is about the POWER in the world. … But real control systems cook up more than SPEED and POWER, they have tasty MANEUVERABILITY.
This teams' overall execution on and off the field, and spirited development tools, were PIVOTal to their success. This team has been charged up for longer than just this year.
This team RIPS through it’s checklist to ensure pre and post-match success. They surf up-and-down with scoring across the grid at the flip of a wrist.

This team has worked with their community leaders to HIGHLIGHT the benefits of STEM Robotics. They’re highly visible in their community working day and night. More than just education, they have put their skills to work, building a device to clean up seaweed and trash that drifts to their shores.

This team is dedicated to spreading the mission of FIRST. From hosting kickoff to facilitating workshops, including here at the Orlando Regional, this team has extended their many legs far and wide. The minority majority team spins up summer camps and science nights reaching 24,000 attendees and their global outreach has resonated as far as South America, Europe, and Africa - making the world their web. Next Saturday, March 25th, the state of California will be celebrating STEM robotics Observance Day, thanks to your friendly neighborhood robotics team.

This team has spellbound us all with their magical talents. They've conjured up success by combining the mystique of sorcery with the wisdom of scholars. Let's give a round of applause to the team that has cast a spell on our hearts with their mesmerizing performance!
This team is nothing short of a chaotic spectacle! They’re known to bring a bit of disorder and pandemonium to the field. Congrats to the team that has “wreaked havoc” on our hearts!
This team brightens the field with their infectious enthusiasm, raucous spirit, and their use of imaginative lighting. Proving to us that Yes,…… WE CAN HEAR YOU
This team has swung into successful sustainable practices, navigating a dense thicket of challenges. Roar your approval and unleash untamed applause for Jungle Robotics.
This team took this year’s theme to heart by leveraging their “potential.” Using voltage to help guide their robot to navigate the grid. This team climbed their way to success like a prey animal.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When the call of the wild comes, critters come to the rescue. But when push comes to shove, they’re always there. And the bottom line is they always get the crumbs.
This team traveled here from afar. Their requirement-forward process brought them to a versatile and effective design. While this team rose to the top, the award will travel down under.

This amazing team only brought a few members here. 60% of the girls joined the team this year. Their cultural hats made the judges cheer. As they brought women in technology and their country to the first atmosphere.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: They might disappear into the background but they’re recognized in their community. This young team inspired us with their hard headed determination. These well trained canines use their creature muscles to button up their team image.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Like their robot this team is very bright. Their elegant approach to their arm and intake is a highlight. This team is a force in fuchsia, a rumble in rose, a bot in blush, I pinky promise

When navigating the darkness of the field this team helped light the way. With multiple programming loops, they were able to find their way like a guardian angel. If all else fails, they would enable their “gig-mundus mode”
When they hear of a need, this team starts up their STARTS up their ENGINES. They were here early helping the competition and helping other teams take flight. Their bumpers were a thing of delight.

With a strong attention to detail this team assembled a robot incorporating lessons from past challenges. Clean electrical layout, custom assembly jigs and tools, and torqued fasteners. This was no accident. The symmetry of their robot sets them up to soar.

Every week they track OVER THE TOWN and treat students with stem programs. Trekking OVER THE TOWN with inspirational treats, and creates breakthroughs as they innovate. This isn’t a mind trick, this IS the team you are looking for .

This team assists f.i.r.s.t. teams near and far, is VISIBLE at public event throughout the year, and developed an innovative approach to REDUCE TEAM DUES. They achieved a 500% INCREASE in recruitment and a significant expansion of their social media outreach. When they aren’t building BUMPERS, you may see their crate rolling around to add the finishing touches to a SOUTHERN MEAL... 5816 GRA-V

Although this is their first event ever in FRC, this team has already taken massive strides to make it loud since first competing in the FIRST Global Challenge. They impressed the judges with their work to securing fund and steam up all 10 districts in their country with outreach.

Learning how to create sales pitches, this team worked with their school board to secure funding to migrate from FTC to FRC. The collaboration of 4 schools and the growth of individual students’ skills and confidence on the team was inspirational.

This team’s excitement is contagious both in their community and the stands. They have infected over 90 events with their enthusiasm and reached tens of thousands of people with their Robots on the Road initiative.
This brightly colored team has come to the judge’s attention because of their delicious plans for the future. Stand back while they sizzle and pop, the judges are sure they’ll never stop.

Their outstanding achievement in developing and refining their robot's autonomous programming demonstrates exceptional technical expertise and innovative thinking. In addition, their precise and strategic decision-making on the field earned this team the Autonomous Award.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Creativity is the essence of all Roboticists, so what makes this team special? Their use of a standard tool as a key part of their machine has ratcheted up their performance by at least eight times. In addition, their self-balancing strategy contributed points to their alliances.

They roamed the vast expanse of the mid-western plains in search of a solution, focusing on the simplicity of design to elevate its reliability and performance. Simulations to CAD to robot design, their whole herd exemplified Excellence in Engineering

This team truly embodies the spirit of Gracious Professionalism, demonstrating exceptional sportsmanship, kindness, and Professionalism throughout the competition. Their remarkable dedication to helping others, both within and outside their team, has helped start and mentor over three teams competing this weekend, a testament to their outstanding leadership and commitment to FIRST values. A well-deserved recognition as a leader in this category.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team soared above others with its integrated cohesive model and branding. Like a bolt of lightning, it leaves a glowing mark.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: If there was one team that was hard for the Judges to corral in the pits, it may have been because of the artistry of their engineering. The Industrial Design award recognizes the aesthetics of a machine and how well it cannot be wrangled by its competitors on the field. Even though they did not bring Bill Preston and Ted Theodore Logan to this event, we recognize the Wyld Stallyns for their ID skills. Be excellent to each other. And rock on, Dudes.

This team's controls are anything but canned. Their fun and colorful design’s Sleekness Provides Amazing Maneuverability. Their controller is incredible on its own; and even more so in that it is custom developed rather than off the shelf with easy-to-use controls and macro commands wrapped to single buttons reminiscent of an old arcade game. This team’s efforts prove they are no fake meat, they send the mass message to all that they are a role model for innovation in control.

This team's ingenuity and resourcefulness under challenging circumstances have earned them the "MacGyver Award." Despite cutting parts from their robot to make it fit size requirements, they found creative solutions, using the scraps to hold the batteries, and even asking another team for plexiglass to mount them. Their software also impressed the judges, showcasing their adaptability and problem-solving skills. A man, a plan, a canal.

This team showed up as a strong contender in the early competitive season. Between a well-executed design considering tradeoffs and potential failures, a redundancy that supported their longevity on-field, and high quality in every aspect of their engineering and build. Opponents tremble when these “Terrible Towel” holders finally “steel” the win.

This team is a group of inspiring and agile engineers. Their robot is a beacon of inspiration on and off the field – incorporating unique engineering design components while resembling an element of the FIRST logo. These warriors reach out to the community to inspire future engineers. Examples include running summer camps for FLL teams, designing a unique game for special needs kids, and starting “bring your rep to FIRST day”. This team helps any teams that need an ‘ASSIST’ and continues to make a ‘DIFFY’ ’ in its impact on the community.

This team does more than tighten NUTS and BOLTS with a WRENCH. When not competing, they’re teaching code, donating food, repairing bikes, or earning scholarships. You may think they’re DIRTY, but they are leaders in GOOD HYGENE.
This team is already reflecting and looking forward to tomorrow. They're learning from others while building on their brand. We're glad they're here . . . Stay golden!

Jumping with rare enthusiasm into the FIRST competition ensures this team will not be endangered. This team demonstrates a unified spirit within their team, across their community, and beyond. As a team, everything they do displays energy, whether in appearance or interactions in and outside the competition. This group es un equipo bacana.

This team was one of the few who continued to reinforce their team during COVID by adding both members and sponsors, despite losing a key mentor… twice. They run their team like a small business, with clear organizational roles, professional-level marketing and outreach plans, and excellent financial discipline. This team has definitely been able to sustain its 9 lives.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: While they excel at Autonomy, their mascot exudes friendliness and their match play exemplifies teamwork. Success during the 15 seconds is followed up by outstanding performance through to the end. The Manatees are consistently Energized from start to finish.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Some teams say they speed their way through the matches. This team says they bicycled their way through.. Nobody denies that fact that they CHARGED their way to a creative victory. Congrats, 4189 Chargers!

Inspirational in every aspect, this team exemplifies the mission of FIRST Robotics. From outreach to engineering, their work week doesn’t stop on Fridays as they use the full week to mentor and raise awareness of STEM to all. Their year doesn’t start with the reveal in January, but is a year round to challenge others with Destination Engineering.

Like the “Mind Stone” this team passes along wisdom and knowledge through their extensive mentoring program to numerous FTC and FLL teams. They also have a robot that can throw you a bone or a ball to make your day to raise awareness for abandoned pets on where to stay. Like Johnny Appleseed this team is spreading the message of FIRST both far and wide. In addition to increasing girl participation in engineering programs through STEM events they also found the time to provide food and clothing to 500 refugees and clean up some county parks as well. They like to say, “in unison” Plant A Seed Grow A Tree,” congratulations 7451.

records.teamName: Career Blazer Robotics - The Fighting Mongooses
records.script: The engineering design process starts with the brainstorming of ideas and strategies followed by design and implementation to achieve a solution to a problem. This team met this challenge with belt tracks for traction giving them a firm grip at endgame and mobility during game play. With a bright Career in their future, just watch these Blazers charge up on the field!

Look for this mighty team to lend support in more than three ways. From safety and collaborations to serving their community, their outreach efforts demonstrate how they put others before themselves. We are blessed with their Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has taken us on a journey to the stars. From the day before competition until their last game, we were mesmerized by the neon lights that left the competition in awe. Their stellar integration of their team and machine has awarded them the Imagery Award.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Elegant, efficient and practical, this robot never quits The judges really loved their design, even in the pits When it comes to style, simplicity and process, this team really has the form This award goes to this blazing team, the amazing Firestorm!

Controlling the robot is one of the most important parts of this competition. There are many robots controlled with joysticks here today, But only one has a whole kinematic library backing it’s operation. Congratulations, 6887 Catabots!

An assembly of students from all over Georgia. This team exemplifies the ability to overcome differences in language, customs, and distances. Through shuttles and Ubers this team managed to bring a skeleton crew to compete with the self proclaimed “most annoying robot on the field”, which isn’t bad for a crew of three. The Judges are proud to present the award for Most Annoying Robot to Team 8577.

A robot skillfully built with Quality and strength so it can withstand the weighty clashes of the opposing alliances. It will not falter as it climbs the rugged mountainside of a competition like a mountain goat. Wobbles will survive!

Out of the chute this team ground out a robust and well tuned robot. This team relied on the efficiency of 3D printing its own parts and parts for other teams. Building outreach over the summer will continue the spirit seen for large teams to teams of 5!

Their team spirit fills the coliseum. Not only do they exemplify being a unified team, they excite their allies and others with their fun-loving attitude, supportiveness, and appearance. Ask nicely and you might get a neo motor when you need it the most. Their enthusiasm even makes the competition want to shout “lets go black and gold”.

Passing knowledge down from senior to freshmen is an important part of sustaining a team This team keeps an excellent formal corporate structure, while doing a good job at maintaining their sponsorships One last thing is certain, nobody ever accuses them of being a grouch!

This team has been a “Flame” dominating on the field with their impressive design and remarkable execution. Their robot, a true “Gear” mastermind was a sight to behold with its striking combination of Red and black. Hailing from Suwannee, they have proven their “wood-bot” is an autonomous technological marvel.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: In the arena of robotics, a team stands tall, armed with the strength and valor reminiscent of ancient warriors. Their innovative spirit shines through as they've engineered a robot arm that defies convention by swinging from the top, earning admiration from all who witness its prowess. With great honor, we bestow the Creativity award upon the fierce and ingenious FIRST robotics team 5109, the Gladiators, for their triumphant display of engineering excellence and originality!

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: To this team, FIRST means making engineering attainable and seeing how technology changes their world. This district wide team has created team building activities that have developed their greatest strength, collaboration. Always energized, this team doesn’t blush (or turn pink) at the prospect of a challenge! The Rookie All Star goes to 9260 Built 4 Bibb.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This all-star team brings energy to their community and this event. With a strategy of building partnerships through family members and even cold-calling local businesses, there is nothing lukewarm about their successes on and off the field. The judges see something strong brewing with this cohesive community team.

This team has been a shining star in the world of robotics since their inception in 2009 in Marietta. This team designed a “canbot” that is a technological masterpiece. Their robot featuring a mesmerizing “bubbles” of blue and red was a true standout this year.

This large team exemplifies gracious professionalism by hosting and supporting multiple events for FLL, FTC and FRC. Their outreach even extended to collecting food for the “Souper Bowl of Caring.” Don’t let the horns fool you, there’s nothing devilish about their commitment to opening their doors for all FIRST Teams.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's Imagery encompasses all aspects of visual representation for the robotics team, from the design of the robot itself to the overall esthetics of the team's branding and marketing materials. The team takes great pride in maintaining a clean and organized space that reflects their dedication to excellence both on and off the competition field. Delivering their robot with Woodie and Dean by their side, this team rolls out of their garage ready for competition.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Attention to detail and a sleek, uncluttered robot are the results of a well executed design process. A sprocket driven arm, LED indicators, pneumatic brakes and auto align are just some of the features that sets this robot out in front. You don’t have to be a villain” or “green” with envy to appreciate this team’s effort.

Amidst the sea of robotic brilliance, a team burns bright with a passion for innovation, casting an orange glow on their journey to success. Fueled by the mastery of sensors, they have forged new pathways for others to follow. It is with fiery enthusiasm that we present the Innovation in Control award to 6829, Ignite, for fanning the flames of progress and steering their robotic masterpiece with unparalleled precision!

We would like to recognize a team that harks back to the golden age of computing. Through their innovative STEM for stem program, they've developed new algorithms by implementing a four-step outreach plan and establishing a sanctuary for learning with their STEM gym. We proudly reboot our admiration for the resourceful FIRST robotics team 6919, the Commodores, as we present them with the Judges award for their exceptional dedication to advancing STEM education and outreach! Congratulations 6919 for the Judges STEM Growth Award.

In the realm of robotics, a team emerges, boasting a name that echoes their burning dedication to engineering perfection. Their keen attention to detail, combined with the skilled use of carbon fiber and custom gears, has forged a robotic masterpiece that leaves all in awe. It is with immense admiration that we present the Quality award to the globally-minded and meticulous FIRST robotics team 1414, I.H.O.T, for their unwavering commitment to engineering excellence and world-class innovation!

In our midst, a team soars with the grace and tenacity of a powerful bird of prey, their noble colors and unwavering determination a testament to their lofty aspirations. This exceptional group has been dedicated to designing accessible interfaces for special needs, inspiring inclusion and making a profound impact through their showcase events. With great pride, we announce the well-deserved recipients of the Engineering Inspiration Award – the indomitable, skyward-bound Team 4112, EagleBots!

Gather round, folks for tonight we celebrate a team that has blazed new trails and headed due west, leaving a colorful wake of innovation and inspiration. This rural group of pioneers has spurred a STEMpede, galloping towards a brighter future by hosting STEM nights at the community center and engaging the state legislature to champion their cause. It is with great pride and admiration that we present the engineering Inspiration Award to Team 8575, the Due Westerners for their unwavering commitment to making the world of STEM accessible to all.

This bold team is committed to the motto: “bring STEM to them.” A strong vision with focus on measurables and securing grants has helped them build strong relationships in their community. They are surging to making a more equitable FIRST with multiple ambassador robots, G4 FIRST Lego League class packs, and a STEM trailer headed to rural areas with a variety of activities. They have an “eye” of bringing winds of change to their backyard and beyond.

Imagine a team of passionate students promoting FIRST through multiple advocacy initiatives and partnerships with a variety of organizations. They host multiple events as they seek to grow roots in their community. This green minded team has a network of 20 FIRS elementary and middle school teams. They are ready to assemble their “tree of mentorship” to be a force of change.

It’s not easy being green, but this team sure makes it look fun! This group of outstanding students has come together to create awesome robots, fostering a sense of unity and camaraderie that leaves a lasting impression. We are thrilled to present the Team Spirit Award to the ever-enthusiastic Team 832, the one and only O.S.C.A.R!

records.teamName: Career Blazer Robotics - The Fighting Mongooses
records.script: Behold, a team that has proven to be more than just fierce fighters, they embody a spirit of tenacity, collaboration, and community! They fight for inclusivity and embrace cooperation, blazing careers for their members and without collecting dues. It is with great enthusiasm that we present the Team Sustainability award to a team that ensures their long-term sustainability via recruiting members and sponsors through tenacious and fierce investment in their community, team 5900, the Fighting Mongooses!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.teamName: Career Blazer Robotics - The Fighting Mongooses

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: This team makes autonomous and play action look easy with a well-designed arm and control system. But control systems are hard, and it takes a skillful integration of motors, software, sensors and computer aided design. Here in Gwinnett you can go East, West, or south, but going North will find this team achieving success on the field.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: A practical and functional intake feeder gives this team a competitive advantage on the field. Out of the box thinking, brain storming, finding the unique approach are all qualities for a creative robot feature. From design to implementation, this Team's "mechanism" is a real asset on the field.

This team and their cheerful sponsor have been stalwart supporters of their local FIRST community and Georgia FIRST for more than a decade. Their dedication to STEM education and their tireless efforts to promote the values of FIRST have truly captured our hearts. Over the past year this team has inspired countless young people through their organization of robotics camps, STEM nights, and the expansion of their recruiting efforts to the band, humanities classes and the DECA club.

This team is equalizing the access to STEM by building connections in the digital world and empowering everyone. They are showing their metal on the climb to the top of the mountain where they are dancing with the BEARS!

This team came down from Mount Olympus to show their engineering skills. Their robot thundered across the playing field with incredible speed. Their dedication to excellence for engineering is truly inspiring, we are excited to see what those Titans can do this season.

This award is given to a team which is wide awake when it comes to identifying and addressing areas for STEM growth and support, both in and outside their school. They have taken the bull by the horns to lead efforts in multi-team collaboration, created programs focused on supporting young women as they get involved in STEM, and helped several teams get their robot running at this event.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Their Robot and team are inspired by vibrant and colorful flowers bringing a touch of summer to the competition. Their robotic movements resemble a hula dance and we could not forget about their love for cats, incorporating a wild element in all of their moves.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team show exceptional design and engineering skills much like the pioneers of the sky! Their sleek and compact rocket inspired robot impressed judges and spectators alike. Their dedication to industrial design is truly inspiring and we can't wait to see what they will do next. Perhaps build their own space shuttle?

Their use of machine principles and innovative approach to controls make them true pioneers in robotics. Their robot moved across the playing field with the precision and grace of a feline's paw. Their innovation in controls make them the king in the field much like the lion in the jungle.

This team's innovative use of scrap metal and old robots in their designs captured our attention, demonstrating their commitment to sustainability and resourcefulness. Despite facing budget constraints they found creative ways to lower club dues, reduce the budget for their robot, and grow their team. Join us in congratulating the winner of the Judges' Lean Machine Award.

This team has a "Fiery" passion for workmanship and robustness. They are at the helm operating a machine that withstands the rigors of the competition. Do not get too close to them with a spark or a flame because their passion for Quality will surely "Ignite!"

This team has some amazing sponsors. They also do outreach events to teach your girls programming and inspire them to pursue STEM careers. They have a fun and creative name that reflects their passion for robotics and their team spirit. This Rookie All Star Team has a call for you - Get Into Robotics Ladies!

They "Stimulate" inspiration with their commitment to science and technology. Thier mentors have been a booster, guiding them through challenges and helping them "Brew" a successful robot. They may be rookies but their love for robotics is like a strong cup of coffee!

This team cheers from the stands like they did for maximus. They rise like a "Creek" after the storm. They face challenges and obstacles but like a "Creek" carving its path they forge ahead with determination and resilience. This is like the definition of a true Gladiator.

This team has competed in FRC during the past 20 years. They promote STEAM learning through robotics and support the international baccalaureate program. By encouraging self-accountability and responsibility among team members, they prepared a fundraising strategy for success in their personal and professional lives.

This team embodied consistent, reliable and high performance autonomous operations that enabled a significant reduction of cycle times. As a team, they redesigned a major subsystem 3 times to meet their exacting standards. Keeping with the grand tradition of the last of the five Space Shuttles, this award goes to the creators of “Endeavor,” the RoboLions of Suwannee.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The Creativity Award recognizes a team that has taken innovation to the next level. This team literally incorporated very thoughtful elements and 3d printed many pieces of their robot. They incorporated cutting-edge technology into their design to create a truly unique and effective robot that even went so far as to reinvent the wheel by 3D printing them. Congratulations to Team 2415, the Wiredcats!

This team has shown exceptional dedication and innovation in their approach to problem-solving, and their commitment to inspiring others is truly inspiring. Their outreach showcases their team to their school, invites the student body to come learn about FIRST during their free period, and makes robotics more accessible for all. Congratulations to Team 4112, the Eagle Bots!

This team “cultivates” STEM in their community through effective outreach and mentoring including STEM camps and hosting both FLL and FTC competitions. They have “Four-Seen” the need to feed a hunger for learning and are generating a lot of buzz in the FIRST community. They are busy as a bee to “feed the valley” turning a food desert into an oasis to promote both health and science.

Shows not only Excellence in Engineering, but also works hard to be a pathway for the next generation of FIRST Robotics FRC Champions. Elegantly skilled at applying linear algebraic concepts to ensure “up” is always up and “down” is always down on the field of play. Believing in the power of 21 since 2006, this award goes to the creators of “Blackjack”.

The gracious professionalism award recognizes a team that embodies the true spirit of FIRST Robotics. Throughout the competition, their helpfulness and kindness were mentioned by several other teams, and their dedication to supporting other teams in their community is an inspiration to us all. They'll always greet you with a big smile behind their sunglasses - you OTTO know who we're talking about. Congratulations Team 1746, OTTO!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has a unified look across their pit, bot, and uniform. This “system of parts” operates with everyone engaged and working together. From their FLL days to building in redundancies to prevent mistakes, this team and their shipping Jimmy robot are making metro Atlanta proud.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The Industrial Design Award is given to a robot that is a stunning example of how form, function, and aesthetics can be seamlessly integrated into one cohesive unit. It's clear that this team has put in countless hours of hard work and dedication into every aspect of their design, and one could hear their unique arm mechanism on the competition field as they lit up the competition. Congratulations Team 1414, IHOT!

This team had a very innovative approach to the design of their mechanical and electrical components. The speed, agility, and incredible elevator system makes their machine a force to be reckoned with. This team has been on fire the entire event burning up the field with the power of HELIOS.

This team’s little bot moves fast, defending their goal and scoring cubes. They keep moving, pushing, scoring, going, and going. Just like the Trojans of yesterday, this team and their Beta Gama has shown us constantly pursing the win is possible! The Judges Relentless Pursuit Award goes to Team 4240, TroTek Warriors.

This team’s bot is solid and tough which matches the hardworking attitude of their team. Quality gods would be proud of their performance and organized pit. Watch out when you see their gear-themed rambot coming your way.

The Rookie Inspiration Award honors team that has truly made a mark in their debut season. From day one, they have shown remarkable determination, grit, and a never-give-up attitude that is an inspiration to us all. This team is proud to play like girls, and they're inviting every young lady to get into robotics. Congratulations Team 9057, G.I.R.L.!

The team spirit award is given to a team that cheers on their team, and lets you make no mistake about who they are and who they're rooting for. Throughout the competition, they have been the loudest and most enthusiastic supporters. They could be seen in the stands performing perfect pirouettes in their matching tutus. Congratulations to Team 6925, WA Robotics!

This team has an amazing approach to developing sustainability for not only their program but the industry of robotics as a whole. As a team, they have tirelessly supported and encouraged youth in their community to participate in the world of competitive robotics. Their efforts to build FLL and FTC teams that bring young girls into this field demonstrates the relentless tenacity of a mighty storm pouring down to prepare us for new life coming in the next season.

records.script: Their robot ran well on its own on every try. They had multiple autonomous modes they could change on the fly. Their autonomous operation was sky high!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This spirited team has a unique style, sailing west to Hawaii took them a while. Although their elevator looks like Swiss cheese, their claw grabs with surgical ease. The intentional design is simple and robust, for them the Creativity Award is a must.

This team demonstrated a stellar engineering design process through the art of simplicity. They exuded confidence in skiing their engineering process and demonstrated documentation to showcase their development journey and their professional approach to the overall design and engineering process.
This team fosters an inclusive community of sharing tools, ideas, and facilities with teams near and far. The judges decided to crown this team with the gracious professionalism award.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Fasten your seatbelts as we celebrate this team’s visual appearance and design prowess. Their flawless execution enabled them to stand proud with feathers fluffed in triumph. They stood out from the crowd and impressed the judges, proving that sometimes, success can truly be a serendipitous event. Congratulations Team 6704, MidPacific Owls.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Results from another regional has given this team new hot thoughts. When traveling with a suitcase robot, shipping is no issue. This robot’s compact design combines form, function and aesthetics making it the industrial dream.
This team’s innovative use of computer vision modeled in AI was unique. Their use of gyro sensors definitely put them on the right level. The command of their controls was top tier.

This team has shown overall excellence in building not only robots but also an island-wide ‘ohana. Their reach extends from the east side to the west side, bringing inspiration for STEM, a passion for learning, and the smell of coffee wherever they go. Congratulations, Team number 2465

This team achieved excellence, both in their machine attributes and in the machine's performance. It's low center of gravity and steel belly withstood the rigor of competition and enabled them to zero in on the targets.

As a result of their strong community interest and accomplished returning alumni, this team has garnered worldwide attention and accolades for their robotics program and unquenchable team enthusiasm. Congratulations, Team number 6909

The Hawaii Regional First Impact award has been claimed by a team that radiates the aloha spirit and embodies the essence of island innovation. We consider them "All Stars" and their Special Projects bring practical solutions to their community while also raising funds for their program. Their outstanding teamwork, technical prowess, and commitment to making a difference have earned them this well deserved victory. With the heart, soul, and passion of a true Hawaiian, this team, has harnessed the power of technology to create something truly remarkable not only for the local community but for regions abroad. We are honored to congratulate this team on their incredible achievement and know that their success will continue to inspire and uplift Hawaii for years to come. Congratulations Team 359, The Hawaiian Kids!

With the power of four, this team is a FIRST Impact team in the making. This team's growing outreach program and use of pneumatics blows the judges away. All the way from the Windward side, Team 9019 earns the Rookie All Star Award.

Starting from scratch and cooking up a storm, this team was able to construct a robot with limited resources. Using their different perspectives of engineering, this team has a sweet recipe for inspiration. The rookie inspiration award goes to Team 9012.

records.teamName: Our Lady of Providence Dream League
records.script: Despite wearing blue, this team was anything but, bringing their positive energy to the rest of the stadium. With cute headbands and a lot of girl power, these dreamers from overseas have gone BANANAS for team spirit.

This team has been successful in sustaining their program by focusing on developing their academies and outreach initiatives. Striving for the summit, they have become a model of excellence. By remaining committed to their values, they are developing a generation of socially conscientious students who will responsibly guide the community to pursue excellence in technology. Congratulations Team 3880, TikiTechs.
There once was a robot so clever, who could auto stack cubes like nobody ever. With "corn on the claw" in a cone shaped hat, this team knew they would succeed in the field forever.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team doggedly hung on and swarmed with their unique design. They mitigated risk and tried something new. They showed ggrrrreat creativity.

You may not see this team at first, but when they strafe, you will be amazed. Resin and tube to be precise, is what this team designed. With robust engineering, this team delivered a robot that can stick to the charge station.

When this team came crashing into a fellow bot. They didn't leave them out cold. Instead they rebuilt them better, stronger, returning their thunder. This team with a cold name gave a warm embrace to the rookies. Hailing from the north and demonstrating Gracious Professionalism on and off the filed is Team 5690 SubZero Robotics.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: A good theme is long lasting and easily recognized. You can't miss this team with their original outfits and history. With their robot chariot, they ride to victory.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: One robot brought music to the judge's ears. Each instrument was thoughtfully implemented in their design. This droid has conquered the Industrial Design Award.

When the controls are out of tune, the music is discord. Overcome chaos with tuning to win an award. It's not APRIL yet, but the results soon draw neigh. With redundant controllers it's as easy as PI.

Pulling together and working in sync throughout the community. This team welcomes everyone - filling brains, bellies and souls, while branching out with nurturing opportunities through diversity, equity and inclusion.
This team bonded together both current and alumni when the challenge came down. They're all for one and one for all quality.

This team has a tiny name, but they make a big impact, reaching thousands of people with dozens of outreach camps. They are TV and YouTube stars that inspire students to experiment at home. This team has addressed a large group of teachers to educate them on how to teach STEM to STEM students.

This team truly embodies the spirit of FIRST, fostering a fun and innovative learning environment within their community. Their dedication to STEM for ALL is unmatched, demonstrated by their incredible outreach efforts including their summer camp in partnership with a Boys and Girls Club. This team is proof that there are no SHORTCUTS when it comes to supporting FIRST.
When lofty goals lie ahead, this team rises to the test. They look far and wide to make parts and will not rest. These towering new comers strive to be the best.
In this Valley, all is peasant and happy. 32 young students in their rookie summer camp is pretty snappy. Having already won an award in week 2 is quite dappy.
This mighty team sure impressed the judges with their spirit. Between their pom pom waving and enthusiastic cheering, they sure stood out. This team proved they were the greatest slugs of all.

When sight is needed, this committee provides guidance to light the way for the future. They are paving the way for their team and the future of robotics. Getting official support will help their vision be clear.

This team's "Vision" of high scores in Autonomous is a reality. With high-speed custom vision processing, combined with odometry and gyros, this machine's auto performance stands out from the rest of field. I if you missed seeing this in action, give it "one second" and a feeling of WOW will pass through you. Congratulations team 6036, Peninsula Robotics.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's creative approach to placing game pieces caught the eyes of the judges. So much so the judges coined a nickname for it, the pancake flipper. This unique design stood out like a lone wolf. Congratulations Team 3859 Wolfpack Robotics

With a fail fast, fail cheap, agile approach to engineering, the result did not FRY up. iterating a design with simplicity in mind is no small potatoes. This year Excellence in engineering award goes to 2122 Team Tators.

records.teamName: Victorian Engineered Robotic Nation or V.E.R.N.
records.script: This team was often mentioned by others when asked "who has helped you?" They actively look for opportunities to help, knowing that they will learn just as much as those they help. Their reputation soars after every community outreach, event and practice collaboration. Congratulations to Team 5461, V.E.R.N.!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's image has risen within the pit, attire, mascot and machine. No amount of water can douse their enthusiasm. Get ready to rise. Congratulations team 5480. FYRE

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Does spending time fixing your bot between matches make you " Crabby"? Not this team. Their Robot is designed for high reliability and fast repair with redundant systems and swapable pars. All of this means this team does not need to "Fiddle" around in the pits.

This teams Innovation in Controls held their gameplay dominance together like glue. With an offset approach to computational image processing this granted them an additional virtual view in the field. Striking forth to impress the judges our winner of the Innovation in control award, Team 114 Eagle Strike.

This team was a serious contender for almost every award. The judges we're all in awe of your amazing robot and amazed by your impressive team members. For these reasons the judges felt like you slid above the rest. When you come down please bring your siblings in stem. Congratulations Team 115. MVRT
This team lies submerged, ready to Strike. Their strength and agility enables them to dominate the waters. They are the Queen's of the river. Congratulations, Tean 1700 Gatorbotics.

It's one thing to inspire your teammates, school mates, school faculty, but having your entire community supporting you deserves praise. Especially when you're from a community of farmers. Since this is your town's team this is your town's award. Congrats and celebrate with a parade down Broadway Ave Team 6358 Buhleon Operators

This team set out on a quest to have an impact beyond themselves They dug deep even during challenging times And with their full armament they successfully spread FIRST and SETM across the globe. Congratulations Team 3256 WarriorBorgs

This team might be small and new but their passion for FIRST is evident. Whether it is being in STEM parades or connecting to students via schools and homeschool networks, this team is absolutely going to grow! They love the cooperation and gracious professionalism they have seen demonstrated towards them and soon, this team will be in a position to do that to others. We cannot wait to see this team grow a presence up north! Congratulations to Team 9044, the TeraViks!

Being a rookie team in this competition can be scary especially during your first competition. This team seemingly came out of nowhere; you would've thought they had been competing for years. Their demonstration of the FIRST Core Values have inspired us to believe that anything is possible, even for a team in a TOWN in the MIDDLE of the Valley. Congratulations Team 9314 Middleton High School Berserkers

This team enthusiasm for FIRST is not limited to the competition. They are the " Teacher of Teachers" The need of the community motivates and inspirer's every team member. Their spirt can be felt throughout the native American community.

This team created an offseason program for introducing new students to robotics, not just locally, but statewide. They designed and hosted their own unique competitions for 11 teams in the community. The judges are "Amped" to announce this year's team sustainability. Congratulations team 3243 Ampers.

This team traveled a vast distance and reached out for a strong Autonomous performance. Their fan cooled robot stayed cool under pressure and is snow big deal in their country. Make no Gnomes about it, Congratulations to Team...

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has traveled far to celebrate creativity that enhances their strategy of play. They are light on their feet enabling them to drive to a strong performance. But they put their feet down to stabilize their place on the charging station to win!

This team dominated the field when it came to showing their calculations and design progress. From long machining hours to going as far as predicting some elements needed for this year's challenge. With their multi-stage intake and scoring mechanism, this team definitely PWNed the competition.

Soaring from great heights, this team has energized many teams within Chicago. This team exemplifies the principles of FIRST core values by mentoring, building, and sharing resources. Working together both on and off the playing field with Gracious Professionalism, this award goes to Team ...

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Think Pink! This team's outstanding visual of team and machine makes an original statement. As part of the Chicago Robotics Alliance, they support the community and share resources. This is Top Secret and Classified, but we'll tell you this award goes to Team 8122 ...

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team is a well balanced team like GM Products with an exemplary robot design that is a well oiled machine on the Charged Up playing field. The entire process from the design, control, safety, and very polished multi-colored robot was very well designed. Lets congratulate this team that knows how to tame the wild.

This team had unique and brightly printed 3D parts and tracked data on the field "on the fly". They are all about the data coming back to their pit for a match review deep dive into controls. Help us give a shout out or a big old "howl" to Team ...

This bright and cheerful team has worked hard bridging cultures across nation. With sword and shield, they drive peace through action with STEM. Let's all kneel to the Chicago Knights as they receive the Judges' Award.

The quality of this robot impressed the Judges with its easy change out of components. This robot lit up the way by incorporating LED status lights that shined out for all to see. Bear with us, as this team doesn't Byte.
This team really knows how to pack it all in and spread their wings. Their inclusivity across regions is an inspiration. It is a delight to have them as part of the FIRST family!

Whereas this team has made an impact to the local FIRST community of teams through their commitment to assisting and creating FRC, FTC, and FLL teams. Whereas this team's outreach spans their local, regional, and national community. Whereas their enthusiastic trio of presenters delivered calculated, precise, and adaptive prompts that meshed together their team's spirit and outstanding community reach. Whereas "Chuck" and "Garrett's Friends" have touched people of all ages. This year's Midwest Regional Impact Award Winner is Team ...
Trucking from the cornfield to the big city. This team is cultivating STEM education with endless enthusiasm. They arrived as rookies and their potential is Limitless.
From day one, this team really took to the stands. No one can catch up to their spirit. You could say, they knew how to muster the crowd. Welcome to the wiener's circle Team ...
Against all odds, this streak has been gathering in the jungle. This team is making all the right moves to nurture the next generation. Bringing the cubs to drink from their river of STEM.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: Like a retriever this team follows the scent. They pursue their goal whether near or far with great consistency and high performance. THIS IS THE WAY to build a great robot.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team designed their robot for versatility from conception. Their dual sided intake and scoring arm allows this team to stay completive. With a flip of their WRIST, the judges were ALERTED to their creativity.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award

records.script: This team’s vibrant theme is shown throughout its design. With their gas shock arm, they stabilized themselves in the judge’s minds. Taking a BYTE out of the field components and the competition.
This team is all of the RAGE! Their efforts supporting throughout the FIRST community are exemplary. Always able to cheer other teams up when they are feeling BLUE!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: You know this team when see them, from their bot, to their pits. Their theme and image are saturated in all they do. With party LEDs and speed, they light up the field with a PURPLE hue.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team demonstrated exceptional design, starting from kickoff with their design matrix prioritizing desired features while weighing cost, feasibility, and strategy. Developing a unique and effective claw allowed them to pick up cones in positions that other teams would pass on. The WRIST has taken the GUESSWORK out of their performance!

This team is on a planned path for greatness. Even with great triumphs and difficulties, the students took the opportunity to refine their arm design with a multitude of innovative controls. If it wasn’t for their temperature sensor, we’d say this team is on FIRE!!

This hardworking team leads themselves with minimal supervision. They are still able to clean up and recycle with limited resources and opportunities. Please give them THUNDEROUS applause for the judge’s BETTY Award.

The judges were RIVETED by this team when it came to talking about the quality of their robot. Their concept of design is seen throughout their robot and on the playing field. This robot lives up to the moto: “They are impossible to Kill”!!

With a focus of inspiring STEM instead of sports, STEAM is their future. From closet, to roaming room, to now a MAKER SPACE. To Columbia Club advocacy and the McCoy Panel Future of youth discussion. Go Baby Go!

Assisting many FIRST teams across the pipeline, this team is driven to support the MISSION of FIRST. It takes a lot to donate so many parts and materials to other FIRST teams, almost enough money to form another FRC team… which they also did. This team’s presentation was incredible in person, just as strong as their essay was on PENN and paper.
After a very tough year, this team stuck with each other. Bringing their community together with home cooked meals. This team is a close family of BEASTLY spirit.
This team is prepared for ANY risk they have or will encounter. Diversity and inclusion ROBOBOOSTS the culture of this team. Every ANGLE formed the frame for sustaining the CUBE.
This robot was a true MARVEL of technology. Lightning fast, with flawless maneuverability and great failure recovery mechanisms make it stand out.. They really BLUE away the competition.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team discovered in competition that their robot did not meet their performance objectives. With a strategic redesign their robot was reborn with significantly more capability. In less than TWO WEEKS, they created a BEAST of a robot.
This team puts their all into preparing the youth of our nation. This CAT is always on the prowl. They BITE hard and bleed PURPLE.
This team has had HOWLING success promoting STEM in their varied outreach programs.. They actually enjoy being in the DOGHOUSE We look forward to seeing wherever the ROAD takes you!.

This ANIMAL of a team really flies on the field, but the don’t need wings.. With CAT-like precision, they show off the results of a great engineering process and excellent technical approach. Watching how they score showed us that it’s really all in the WRIST.

This team shared resources and helped multiple teams this weekend. They made sure that both them and their clone maintained reliability. This team is on a CRUSADE to spread Gracious Professionalism far and wide.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is very AWARE of how they look to those around them. Keep an eye on these BOLTS, as they seem to be a force of nature. Get ready to hear a Dinos RAR (RAAAAR).

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team had a really FLY design. The robot demonstrated elegant design that also incorporates style, form, and function. The way this team performs is like SNAKES on a PLANE.
This unique robot’s ability to understand the STATE of things, helps keep them in control. Through sensors, indications, and automation, nothing was going to UNDO this decision for the judges..

This team lights a fire behind them. Their actions carve a path and ignite the futures of those in their local community. We would be amiss to not recognize the diligence of this team to not only do their homework, but also make a new friend every day. Winning the Outstanding Community Involvement Award

They can take a hit and keep on GROWLING. With the plethora of spare parts and their reinforced arm, they can hold up to the rigors of competition. With how durable this robot is, you might think the CLAWS were made of ADAMANTIUM.

This team was strong and proud, which made them stand out in the crowd. Their mascot grabbed much attention, motivating themselves and others was their mission. When they cheered in the audience, no one had to wonder, everyone heard this team’s THUNDER.
This RED team has down a long winding road. The plan to level their roller coaster brought new members into their DOGHOUSE. We hope to see these loose cannons for years to come.

This team's swerve control could be written up in a white paper. With multiple autonomous routines that were impressive and worked flawlessly. Their planned paths and waypoints show remarkable PRECISION.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team knew that creativity really counted. They used a herculean effort to build a well-balanced robot. Bring out your go pro, this should go on your you tube channel.

This team works to make an impact on and off the field. They don't just build robots, they're helping build a better community. Blazing a trail for future generations to be part of a more diverse FIRST.

This Indiana team displays excellence in all aspects of the FIRST mission. Their efforts to make robotics available to everyone in their community and continued additions of new teams, while sustaining existing teams, are incredible. Our /investigation/ has found that this team continues to make a lasting impact on current and future members, which results in a dedicated alumni group that make FIRST a lifelong endeavor. The source of their spark is definitely not TOP SECRET!
This team summarizes their engineering processes in a notebook. Their 150-member team utilizes student leadership to address robot design and improvements. Bringing the lightning to Indiana.

When other teams need help, this team is always ready to lend a paw. No one is a lone wolf when they are around; offering advice, materials, work space, and building assistance. With WOLF-ER-INE by their side, this team rises to the top of the pack.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: After arriving through a snowstorm, this team gives us a glimpse of spring. Wherever this team goes, you'll see sprouts of green. It makes sense since this team's mascot eats bamboo.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: No matter where you look, this team has killer designs. From their rocker arms to their swappable manipulator, the judges renamed this team DESIGN-o-BYTE.
This team planned their path throughout the competition. Impressing judges and hounding them with their extensive controls. They flew through the field using their watch tower.

The More Than Robots Award This team has many pieces moving strategically to achieve their goals. Capturing the imagination of novices and grand masters with their outreach they have leapt beyond these four walls and are our knights in shining armor.

Quality was forefront for this team from their summer roundtable to their completed robot. This team's wiring was clean and their welds were smooth as silk. Build robustly, they could be hit by and ELK and remain in TIP TOP SHAPE.
This team has sharp robot instruction, and enthusiasm that is a cut above. Slicing and dicing their way through their rookie season, we have high expectation for this new groups of techies.

This rookie team was charged up on the competition field and electric in the stands, successfully completing a strong circuit in just their first year. We're excited to see how they transform the future.
This team wowed us with their fiery spirit. In their pits they're on their couch but in the stands they're on their feet. They should take PRIDE in this accomplishment.
This team came ready to compete and were dressed for success. Their robot is not their only treasure, ask them about their wares. They ARRRR ready to keep their team sailing for many years to come.

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team impressed with their focus on consistent, high point acquirement during the autonomous period. Keeping a tight grip on every cube, with their auto-stow arm, they excelled with their automatic actions. These troopers are suPURDUEper cone scoopers!

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Thinking outside the box comes with risk, but good planning, strong teamwork, and perseverance can bring ideas to life. Sometimes you have to innovate without having all the right angles. These squares take creativity to the next level.

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team worked hard to spread the NEWS about FIRST robotics through many channels. Their efforts in community outreach really BLUE us away. They have been inspiring us for 25 years!

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team opens their borders to teams near and far. Using mixed media they spread the message of FIRST. This team is always working to expand their family. From outreach to coffee this team will keep you alert!

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.script: It's definitely not a secret when this team storms onto the field. Their process was able to identify all of the key aspects that make this machine simple, robust, and elegant. Inside and out....of this world.

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team is well known for assisting throughout their community. They definitely RED the manuals and helped produce the section on the best use of bumpers. They take PRIDE as they lend a helping hand.

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From the pits to their robot, and don't forget their swag, This team selected everything with PRECISION. This choice was not a GUESS.

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team has proven that "simple is better". With a design that is elegant and efficient, with them it is no cat and mouse game. They will not be afraid to show you the PANTHER pride.

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.script: Being in control requires lightning precision. This team doggedly chased down every situation. The blue and gold pressed all the right buttons.

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team understands the importance of making robotics for everyone. This team has demonstrated exemplary performance, organization, teamwork, and all around good design. This team has added the HEAT to the competition. Winning the Robots are for Everyone Award.

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team took last years robot bugs as a focus for their design. They worked together to build a robot that was not only indestructible, but also aesthetically pleasing. They have proven that it is impossible to kill "LA CUCARACHA".

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team has stepped up to the challenge and made a legendary drive. With their perseverance they have ironed out all the wrinkles. Look out for this conqueror.

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.script: If you didn't hear this team during the matches, you were not really here. This team supported not just their team, but all teams. Lead by the King in his Castle.

records.eventName: FIN District Princeton Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team takes a lot of PRIDE in making their team last. Their innovative strategy to prepare students and hold them accountable is enough to make anyone feel warm and fuzzy. This team is sure to have a lasting DYNASTY.
This team knew how to press all the right buttons. They demonstrated control, innovation and efficiency when operating their robot. Even when things get SQUISHY, this team has CAT like reflexes.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has an EYE for functional and aesthetic solutions. Failure fears them because they do not CRUMPLE under pressure. We ENVIED their DEVILISH design.

This team excels at educating their community about STEAM and the FIRST Mission. Through creative engineering projects they're preparing younger generations to solve the diverse problems of the future. They shine at ALERTING their community about the BUCKETS of fun you can have in the FIRST program.

This team makes sparks fly in their community by providing opportunities for stem for all age levels. Their gallantry knows no bounds planning for multiple years of success. Castling their KING with the ROOK will also help to ensure their sustainability for the future.

When it comes to designing a robot, this team was practical and precise. They COMPOUNDED their ideas, BRACED their robot for stability, and never QUIVERED when it came to engineering solutions. There is no GUESSING about who has shown Excellence in Engineering.
From local to international, this team is quick to assist. Over Zoom or zooming in person, this team is GEARED towards helping others. Don’t get it PHYXT, this team exudes Gracious Professionalism

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From the stands to the pits, this team is sure to catch your eye. With colors that can be seen from light years away. This team’s aesthetics are “out of this world”.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's design was the HIGHLIGHT of our day. They really flipped the game on its head and took a bite outta the competition.
This team was a shining star on and off the field. Every team said they helped MEOW-t. With their small robot strategy, they pounced on the competition.

This team successfully integrated new to them technology and designs into their robot. Swerving away from CROWNS and BERRIES, this team is not afraid to take risks. From melting bits to bumping fists, this team is a little WRECKLESS.
This team slowed to a crawl and was able to walk away again. With Quality documentation and custom parts. They couldn't be crushed like a bug.

This team gathered a feather for their cap at this competition. Their passion, excitement and practical design is a great demonstration of their KRAFT. Don't say this team SLICES the macaroni and cheese.

This team is sure to have caught you attention with their battler cries this weekend. From their enthusiasm to their image this team can inspire any King's court. Their spirit 'tis but a fraction of what makes this team stand out.

Organization and accuracy are a top priority of this team. With their in-depth risk analysis and documentation, they are sure to leave behind a LEGACY for future generations. If they ever get caught in the CROSSHAIRS of hardship, they have no reason to worry.
