records.script: This team’s robot’s consistent auto cube placement helped set them apart. Their range-of-motion helped them reach goals, both in front and behind them. The automated turret of this purple team made the judges’ heads spin.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team looked for unique ways to approach the games’ challenges. They knew that manipulating game pieces wass a complex task… so they became “one” with the robot. They designed and fabricated a very unique “hand controller.”

Is it getting warm in here? This team incorporated the engineering design process including CAD first followed by iterative prototyping and F.M.E.A. strength analysis. Although they are used to the cold, they have been burning it up on the field.

This team sharply embodies not just gracious professionalism, but every FIRST core values their use of active teaching methods ensures that STEM and core values are for everyone in every activity. This team’s GP made the judges say “yippee!” (but softly)

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Just like their robot’s namesake, this team brings a lot of energy to the competition. Stand back and let this team glow! They melted down a lot of orange and green filament, combining function and visual appeal.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team examined all sides of design by flipping between prototypes. This high performing robot is fast, elegant, and modular. Galloping to the charging station this robot comes in “best in show.”

This team’s complex robot aligned to score cones and cubes with ease. Their robot automatically balances on the charge station like an acrobat. The well curated control of this rocky mountain robot helped them raid the competition.

TOGETHER, the judges are happy to present this award for growing through inclusion. PROMOTING inclusion is not just a core value to this team, but a way of breaking barriers. SUCCESS through unity TIPS the scales, allowing them to plant the seeds of future growth.

Not even a demolition derby will get the best of this team. Their focus on robustness, redundancy and workmanship has produced a bot that can withstand the rigors of competition. Quality is leading them on the path to success.
This team has a MISSION to prove that FIRST is more than robots. They TAKE FLIGHT to encourage inclusion and innovation. They respond to their CALL SIGN to ROPE every kid in Kansas into FIRST.

Einstein once said, “There is a driving force more POWERFUL than steam, electricity and atomic energy: the WILL.” This team has a structured onboarding plan, making sure their new members are NEVER in the DARK. Working with other FIRST teams during the offseason has helped this team SPARK interest in others. Their strong CONNECTIONS have CHARGED UP the underserved and underrepresented populations in their area, over seas, and even UNDER SEAS! Reaching students through the entire FIRST family of programs, this team’s STRONG WILL has helped them achieve their ENERGETIC goal - LIGHTING UP ROBOTICS, LIGHTING UP THE WORLD!

The team inspired their judges with their efforts to ensure growth in the coming years. Their inclusion and collaboration show that they know FIRST is “more than robots.” Their burning passion for FIRST may have started from a single spark but is already spreading.

records.teamName: The FBI - FIRST Bots of Independence
records.script: While we were busy investigating the team that was most deserving, this team was first to arrive with their game face on. Even the feds would agree that fom head to they’re suited for this award.
This team sailed here across a sea of corn with a little dog at the helm. Have no fear, if you need a custom tee shirt they can deliver with a BAMM.

Dependability is key for this team. Their robot excelled in consistency on the field. Not only was it fast, but its ability to score not once, not twice, but three times before ending its 15 second autonomous journey on the top! This team deserves a shout out…

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Despite the obstacles, this team has reached new heights. They flipped the odds in their favor with a creative intake arm scoring at every level. Their speed and agility allowed them to BUST past the competition!

This team’s approach to attacking the game looks like a page out of an engineering handbook. Their clean strategy led to the creation of a custom, compact gearbox. It extended throughout the modular and easy to repair design. This balanced approach helped them take the advantage during their siege of the field.

The judges were bowled over by all the positive feedback from others about this team throughout the competition. From helping teams pass inspection to loaning out parts, tools, and even people, this team’s overall good sportsmanship washes over the other teams both on and off the deck. This team goes FULL STEAM AHEAD when helping to get others into SHIPSHAPE for the competition!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team immediately caught the judge’s eyes with their bright and colorful theme. The Robot was sleek, clean, and like a member of the team proudly wearing its t-shirt! Their pit area was organized and filled with team members burning with passion for FIRST! This team constantly invites new students to blaze a new trail, joining their efforts to promote STEM and “Spread the Wildfire”.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team was very intentional with the design of every component of their robot. Each module fit together with precision to create a compact functional design that would pivot in a pinch. It’s clean lines and paint scheme would make Ferrari jealous. By failing forward this team was able to breakaway from the pack.

This team bulldozed the judges with a highly precise bot. Having an informative and useful light display for requesting specific game elements from its human field players. This self- diagnosing robot also lets its humans know when it has a problem. It has truly blown the judges away with an innovative communication matrix. This team simply cannot be diffused.

The judges were impressed with this Team’s efforts to build an inclusive program within their community. They recognize that FIRST is more than just robots. They inspire others through student shadowing programs and public speaking workshops and provide a program where all can feel included. This Team gives each member the opportunity to find the Chaos within themselves

This robot impressed the judges with its exceptional craftsmanship and clean design which includes an elegant compound elevator, reinforced architecture, and clean wiring scheme. With built in redundancy and a solid design it can easily adapt to the field of play. The union of multiple elements POWERED this team throughout the competition.

This team has touched every aspect of FIRST, from inspiration to impact, demonstrating their passion for STEM. They increased their Team diversity to exceed that of their school and earned the respect of the local medical community by applying their skills to improve quality of life for patients with special needs. This purple wave extends beyond just local shores and inspires around the world.

The team that impressed the judges this year provides a pipeline for team sustainability. Focusing on growing exploration and interest in ALL STEM related careers, they have the support of businesses in their community and understand that advanced degrees are great, but trades are critical in the sustainability of the community. It is important to the team that students on every level, freshman to seniors, are involved in their presentation and community outreach efforts. They repeatedly engage areas throughout their state that are lacking active STEM programs. Eagerly seeking to increase communication with diverse populations by learning new languages and making use of them in recruiting and outreach efforts is a sure…SIGN that your team is doing something right. The judges found this team’s outreach and ability to build relationships both in their local community and statewide is truly PHENOMENAL!

In no time at all, this team has managed to shine like the brightest star. They took the initiative to turn their passion into action, making them a FUR-midable team. With gratitude and pride, they take challenges one step at a time while making sure that everyone’s voice is heard. This in-BEAR-ably talented team knows what FIRST is all about.

From a tiny spark has burst a mighty flame. Born from the vision of a single student, this rookie team is leading their school and community to embrace the mission and principles of FIRST while igniting a renewed commitment to STEM. They have big plans both as individuals…career planning and visions of entrepreneurship, and for their team…designing technical improvements for their robot, planning summer programs, and setting up future teams for success. By putting all of their heads together…this team will not be deterred by challenges and are ready for whatever their future may hold!

This Team’s enthusiasm for FIRST is infectious, both on and off the field. Standing up for STEM they convinced their school to give their robotics team a sporting chance! They pass out their love of STEM at both FIRST and non-FIRST events infecting others with their STEM spirit. Some may say their passion for FIRST is scary, but they would call it WILD!

This team functions like a well-oiled machine. Their finely tuned business plan includes strategic elements that ensures their sustainability including year round trainings for their team and community, volunteering at a variety of events, and providing outreach programs for students young and old. They provide a safe space for everyone to engage and learn new skills. Students are inspired to attend their school specifically for the robotics program but they learn so much more than just the technical. Like they always say “Victory goes beyond winning.”
With its amazing show of colors, this robot requires very little help. With its robust vision system no game piece was left out. They might be an outlier but they are fully in the game.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team fused a classic mechanism and new manufacturing practices to develop a unique and functional design. They visually showed their iterations and demonstrated passion on how this feature gave them a competitive advantage. Picking up cones where others couldn't. They are leading on the field in ground breaking technology.

*To the tune of 'Eye of the Tiger' by Survivor* This team caught the eye of the judges with the thrill of their fight! They rose up to the challenge of Charged Up! Led by Steminists they took to the field all the way from Ipswitch Mass!

Today’s winner takes the spirit of the impact award to heart, reaching out to many schools beyond their own, promoting both the FIRST core values and the importance of STEM education. The team is impressive on the competition field each year, but their extensive outreach efforts both locally and globally stand out equally. Their involvement in lower-income communities have given countless young students access to FIRST programs they may not have otherwise. This includes funding and mentoring 12 FLL teams and 14 FTC teams. Through their sponsors, this team is able to give schools they work with access to resources like 3D printers and CAD software to enhance student learning. Their global efforts include providing FLL curriculum to underprivileged communities in Southeast Asia. Most recently, the team has supported indigenous and homeless populations through the donation of household goods and clothing, as well as a mentor traveling with a medical mission to support this vulnerable population. This team embodies the notion that our differences should not divide us. Rather those differences make this team stronger. Every member of this team feels included and is actively involved in its success. They have become a hub, or ***NUcleus*** if you will, through which students from all over the greater Boston area and beyond can learn and experience FIRST.
This team demonstrated a thorough understanding of the design process from beginning to end. They are a bright shinning example of elegant design. They are a champion of excellence in engineering.

The Judges, the Queue staff, and the Pit all agree that this team is the gold standard. From their eagerness to talk to other teams, their work with the NEXUS Alliance, and their dedication to bringing the LGBTQ community to STEM, it is clear to SEA that this team stands out.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Scientists and Engineers love outside-the-box aesthetic and a machine that's outstanding. What links this team and their robot is their *meticulous* standard branding. Such as orange belts, pit, zip ties, and colorful hoodies that left the judges with no misunderstanding.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team is geared towards success with their design principles. Their robots A-frame robot embodies efficient functionality. After winning this award, you'll be sure to find them at the nearest crepe café.

While other teams might have this "peace" of hardware, this team "operates" it with precision. The crowd sees this team while their robot see the field. Their use of vision based positioning made their operation a success.

This team strives to ensure that all team members are able to participate regardless of means. They were able to succinctly explain their growth in fundraising, from writing grant applications to having local companies pledge their support as they progress through the competition levels. They are ready to *soar* for years to come.
Keeping a machine requires attention to details. Like the jolly big guy, this team also wear red. This team made a list and checked it twice, every match.

The vibrant enthusiasm of this team will Fluff up everyone's spirit. Their energy was tangible and *trans-ported* the judges to their happy place. They have so much team spirit it will make your eyes wiggle.

Our judges were ultra impressed by this teams ability to manage and sustain their numbers and business. They popped up out of Wellesley like a pack of violets and have spread their roots to ensure they are around for years to come.
Harnessing the power of mathematics to teach their robot operate A strong understanding of Technical Jargon was required To Judge this award. Though they worked hard, they didn't have to travel far.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's strategy is to zoom across the open range devouring cubes. They gallop back and launch them into their corral. Leaving the open range desolate of cubes for their opponent. Because of this creative grace play......

This team has been committed to FIRST year round. They've steadily doubled their funding for the past few years and their recruiting efforts are not just focused on engineers. They regularly participate in a city fair and also spread a message against violence showing how much they truly care.

This team sponsored STEM days throughout the pandemic. They also go to their senior center showing residents how advances in technology can improve their lives. The team meets with their representatives to push through bills for funding assistance to robotics teams across the state. They also attend local family festivals to spread the word of FIRST. On top of everything else, this team works with students at the Center for Applied Behavioral Instructions to spread the message of FIRST in an inclusive environment.

This robot climbed into the engineering spotlight with its balance between form & function. Not one members of the team left our judged "boar-ed" while describing their engineering design process. The judges see engineering excellence "wired" into their plans and designs.

Communication, Collaboration, Contribution and Confidence; these are the qualities of effective leaders that the judges recognized in this years winners of the Gracious Professionalism Award. Their record for collaboration was unmatched amongst their peers and they SPIN FIRST's core values throughout their behavior on and off the playing field.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s impressive color coordinated robot, attire and even their cart are sure to draw attention out on the field. They certainly were heard cheering loud and proud like busy bees in the stands.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot's intricate articulate telescoping arm, 3D carbon fiber gear and elegant intake makes it a smooth and efficient cube and cone moving machine. Its ability to auto balance quickly on the charging station allows it to score until the end. Its ability to link 25 times in a row makes this robot stand out among the rest.

Pivot, pivot, swerve! Rotate, pitch and turn! Overdrive a Neo Watch that sucker burn But focus on the cardinal points to guide the lessons learned. A pigeon 2 to level out and stabilize so well The control of this bot is all "W" It really is no "L"
With a strong showing out from the gate This flock displayed excellent documentation and theming. From the Live Free or Die state - they rose from the ashes.

Clean, sleek and polished. These are just a few keywords to describe the winning build for the quality award. Like a new set of skins, this robot had exceptional blueprinting, incredible fabrication, and pristine precision. This team navigated mountains of obstacles and developed a work of art.

This team is a rookie in regard to participation in FRC but as a group of students from public, private and home schools, they are fully involved with the FRC programs. They are actively recruiting new members, exhibiting their robot at rotary functions and christmas shows. They understand the FIRST mission and are determined to win future events.

The team started not to long, long ago from a town far, far away..... They are not only true to their colors but its core values - that their team is made of anyone who is interested regardless of their limitations.

This team doesn't take next year for granted. They tireless fundraise to make membership accessible to any and everyone. Their recruiting efforts will definitely help their team Persevere for many years.

This team has a rigorous design process that creates harmony between hardware and software. They crafted an autonomous that enabled them to successfully score in all 3 ways. This team displayed excellence in their flexibility as they had multiple different autonomous modes based on the alliance. When this team is on the field and winding up, look out!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team came together to test their metal on the charge station; they didn’t spin their wheels but found instinctive balance. Mother nature could never match the evolution of this cat’s claws. These ferrous felines truly earned their stripes.

This team has made a large splash teaching the next generation of innovators. Their community has advanced respect and appreciation for engineering by making a diverse space where everyone can learn and grow together. Through global outreach, team training, and establishing FLL teams, they are inspiring STEAM in many ways! They’ve created quite a storm globally dedicating themselves to spreading the mission of FIRST.

This team’s impact is an inspiration to all. Not only is their impact felt all around New England, but all around the globe. In their own school district they helped create several new STEM-based classes with new Science and Engineering staff; a district-wide FIRST pipeline that includes FLL Explore, FLL Challenge, FTC, and FRC teams that they support; a new Innovation Lab; and a STEM program for students with disabilities. Right here in New England, they have worked tirelessly to make FIRST programs available to all – from starting new teams in towns with no FIRST programs, to mentoring and supporting several other FIRST teams. This team has also responded to national and global concerns by sending FLL kits to regions impacted by hurricanes and providing clean water to war-ravaged Ukraine. This team has even extended their mission all the way to the Massachusetts State House with their student-written and diligently supported Robotics Bill to fund, expand, and sustain all teams in Massachusetts. No challenge is too ALIEN to this team…

This team went through a complete rebuild, but you would never know it from the professionalism of its design and build process. The robot impressed in form and function, from sprocket penetrating wiring, to ship-shape electronics layout, and elegant manipulator. Their dedication, spirit, and democratic teamwork, make this team from the north a force to be reckoned. Go pink power!

What they lack in the size of their team, they make up for in the size of their character. Everything was open for asking, as bolts, bodies, and behavior, all were graciously given. While their shaker wooden furniture style robot design was superb, their team disrupted foundational concepts of competition and team to truly demonstrated coopertition.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is a vision in blue, through and through. Their references may be older than their team members, but they wear their hats better than the Dread Pirate Roberts! Thematically, it can be said that the team delivered R-O-U-S, or Robots of Unusual Size, as you wish. With true love, the judges present this award to team 1729, team inconceivable

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: In this robot the object retrieval flows and the visual aids show. The ‘bot and driver adapt to each target through great visual displays that would stand out on the savannah. With great integration of driver and ‘bot, at the touch of a button they go any way.
This team skillfully integrates ballet-like motion into their robot. They also collect data for neural network training. As a bonus, they show their tie-dye team colors for a successful boot up.

This team has contained chaos. They’ve prevented pandemonium with robot analysis, clean wiring, and strict safety. With them, you are protected from mayhem. The Judges Award for Containment goes to Mayhem Robotics!
From the broad swing of their sturdy arm, To standard training for the gray shirts, High quality shows even in the organization of their button box.

The judges eyed this team because of their spirit of enthusiasm for all. Their spirit is visible in their t-shirts, booth, robot, team banner and hats. Their googling eyes are set beyond this Competition on to Community.

This self-funded team has an outstanding grasp on business and project management. Available to anyone willing to join, they also support over 30 FLL programs. With diligent documentation, responsible budget planning, and great sponsor relations, it was easy to “grant” their perseverant sustainability efforts this award. Feel “free to join” us on the field,

This team worked to make small chanages to make a big impact in order to perform consistently in autonomous. They were able to adapt to the needs of their alliances by selecting an effective autonomous routine. Sinking their claws deep into the competition their performance was purrr-fect. The winner of this ward is team 1699 the Robocats.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The creativity award is given to a team that has really raised the bar. This team impressed the judges by creating their own custom lathed lead screw for a consistent and controlled arm movement. The winner of the creativity award is team 467 the Colonials.

Where does Inspiration come from? You start them young in multiple FLL teams. You then run a camp with FTC. You embrace the local Makerspace. You reach into the community and team up with a church youth group. They reach out to new students with Come learn night! Students teaching students is how his team rolls. In their words…This is where Steam happens…. The winner of the Engineering Inspiration Award is Team 2370 the iBots

Where does the biggest impact come from? It’s not about team size. It’s not about having the winning robot. It’s about heart. It’s about sharing. It’s about building for the future. It’s about inspiring. This team’s work is under the radar. No bragging, No bluster. They are fun, collaborative, hardworking and inclusive. They have solid FLL mentoring. They are a founding member of the NEXUS alliance. They hold a very successful Women in Stem conference. This year the biggest impact comes from the smallest state. In their words… We are Pioneers, Volunteers, Engineers and Gongoliers.

This team's use of CAD got them off to a strong start. Their 2D trials guided them to a viable solution. Their use of sheet metal has made them a force to be reckoned with. The winner of this award is team 178, the 2nd law enforcers.

This team demonstrated the FIRST core values both on and off the field. They work together with other teams even through difficult situations. It takes guts to stand up for another team at the risk of your own, but these brave warriors didn't hesitate when a mistake had been made. "Owl" of the volunteers had good things to say about this team. The winner of this award is team 3182 Athena's Warriors.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's imagery is sky high. Their cohesive and attractive design included all of their team members, their pit, and their robot. This team scaled the peak to soar above the rest. The winner of this award is team 7153 Aetos Dios.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The team that is winning this award designed a robot with many custom elements. All the elements were integrated into a clean design which performed well on the field, was good looking, and rock solid. The winner of the industrial design award is team 195 the CyberKnights.

Taking full advantage of commercially available products this team was magic in motion as they moved around the field. Whether driver controlled or autonomous they always seemed to know where they were. The winner of this award is team 1071 Team Max.

A second year team with a sense of community, they are finding their way. Their passion for outreach and engineering caught the judge's eye. Using their skills that they have developed in FIRST, they are making a difference one wheelchair at a time. We would trust their path finding skills any day. The winner of this award is 8709 Pathfinder Tech.

This team designed a solid machine. They rode to the rescue with 3D printed parts. Their creative tensioning cam and cube-shooting intake kept their robot marching along. The winner of this award is team 1740 Cyber Colonels.

One word to describe this team is flexible; starting with only one student and a parent who wanted more FIRST teams in their area. Like a strong breeze this team blew the judges away with their passion for FIRST and it is clear are an Impact team in the making. It is never a stormy day with this team around. The winner of this award is team 9096 Bad Weather.

This team's enthusiasm is definitely unmatched. They're a unified front and always prepared to meet you with a smile. When they're on the field, the crowd is all a Buzz. The winner of this award is team 175 Buzz Robotics.

This team has built a rock solid foundation. They have a strong future that's all planned out. They'll be around for a LONG time. They plan to build and train an army of engineers to save the world! The winner of this award is 7127 LongMetal.

With autonomous mode, each team looks to make the most of their 15 seconds, 1 cube, 2 cones, maybe a charge...the options are truly endless. This team took it further by keeping their eyes on autonomous success using the field tags to their advantage both in the physical and digital world, while helping the rest of the community relish in their success. With 112 autonomous modes, full game collision avoidance, sensor placement and a full match autonomous assist, this team glided into the heart of the judges. Team 6328 doesn't just have a mechanical advantage they have an autonomous one.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team was one of the few with a turret system to give them azimuth control. They intentionally slammed into the station backwall to locate their intended target. They had a north extending arm for cubes and cones and a south cube collector for two targets on each pass.

Focused on fostering an appreciation for STEAM in others, this team is here to stay in their community. Their razor-sharp passion for maintaining a positive relationship and sharing FIRST with their teammates, sponsors, school, and town is clear. From running school and town-based demos to hosting FLL minicourses at their local library, one might say this team ROCKS “Chic in STEM.”

The judges had so much to say about this team and the incredible work that they do. In the off-season, this team runs a successful summer camp, and as the school year starts, they host a robotics open house in the fall. This team is actively fund-raising to support their robot and travels. Increasing the number of females in STEM and partnering with the local Girl Scout troops fuels this team to success. You may recognize the standout outfits and socks of their pit crew, keeping them on track.

This team’s robust knowledge of their robot stood above the others. From their extremely organized electrical panel to their easily fixable aspects, they are one of a kind! Plus, their robot and team has been in a commercial that has aired all over the country!

This team demonstrates gracious professionalism in all that they do. From partnering with teams in the pre-season and build-season, to supporting teams at events by sharing whatever is needed, this teams fly above the rest. This team even shares scouting data, so all teams at the event are set-up for success. There's no mistaking the shine in the sky when this team is around.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Their pit will take your breath away. Their presence is felt to the depths of your soul. Edgar Allen Poe would be proud. Quoth the Judges,”truly inspirational”.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team was justifiably proud of their design and manufacturing process with a first-year swerve drive and much of their robot built with 3D printed parts. They swerve. They telescope. They pivot. They SCORE! They combined beauty and elegance into a an incredibly robust design that is reliable, serviceable, and modular. It’s clear that they spent a lot of TIME on their hourglass plate.
With their innovative libraries to support custom configs for efficient articulation. The robot provides a wide range of feedback to the team. The end result is a robot that roars upon the field.

This team’s robot and community contributions wormed their way into many of the judge’s conversations. Their local outreach has been scaled up to provide a STEAM resource that spreads the principles of FIRST worldwide. When it comes to inspiring others, this team is truly cooking up a storm.
This robot is protected with custom CNC machined components. Its electronics are impervious to everything except a lightning strike. The winner of the Quality award crushes the competition!

Breezing their way in from out of nowhere. Charged Up to create a new team. Hacking their way to collecting donors, mentor, members and space. Though their logo may be cloudy their future is looking bright.

This team shows spirit through their multiple team chants, well decorated pit, and newly founded mascot. Proudly showing "determination" in the heat of competition, it shows in their logo and buttons, in the stands, as well as in their team animation. Incorporating the spirit of this season’s theme into their overall team appearance, as they cheer in the stands, their cone and cube hats are enjoyed by everyone around them.

This team is superb at involving its small community up north. They overcame mountainous highs and lows in other competitions. And they are a bright green jewel that knows inclusion and outreach keep the team Robust.
This robot grew in size on the field; and during autonomous, many points they did yield. Their balance on the charging station was smooth and sound; Their magic schoolbus really goes round and round.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Beware to not underestimate this bot from its size; because for it's creative design it has won a prize. One small roll for this bot is a large leap for their team; for they got many points with boxes and cones on a beam. This robot was quite the beast - it can be crowned a King; Their unique approach was truly amazing!

This team's Project Plans were critical to the success of their outreach. Their commitment to educating new members and K-12 was a "WISH" come true for their community at large. This team shows everyone there is nothing "HAUNTED" about STEM.

The judges really enjoyed this team's interactive presentation as an entertaining and effective way of covering many of the key points of the team's activities. For both rookies and veterans, this team offers introductions and briefings on the full spectrum of FIRST activities, including finance, marketing, and communications, as well as the critical elements of the STEM disciplines. The judges were impressed with their efforts to partner not only with sponsors and teams, but also educational organizations that spread the mission of FIRST and spark an early interest in STEM in children. This team is a true community leader in opening the doors to STEM involvement with the inclusive nature of their outreach, including hosting events for students at Title I schools and writing an engineering-themed picture book that was translated into Spanish. The judges were impressed that the team carried out their 2022 plan to start a podcast and how they have used this platform to interview professionals, alumni, and other teams. This was a team that did so much it might make you crazy, and that may be why they call themselves RoboLoCo.

This team zooms across the field in a flash of yellow. Their excellent material selection made their robot lighter, stiffer and stronger. With a bit of “physical therapy” they trained their robot to excel at this year’s game.
Watching this team on and off the floor was riveting. They bolted to the scene to help any team in need. The Judges were charmed by this team’s Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: While other teams search for a visual pleasing appearance, the powerful asthetics of this team rose above. They attractively integrated their imagery into their technology and their “merch”. This team's branding shows the Phoenix rises again.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: All good things come in threes; in this case - elegance, simplicity and functionality. This team stormed the arena and quickly “rose” above the competition. This robust and strong robot is a real gladiator.
This all black robot was hunting for victory. They SHOCKED the Judges with their modeling and simulation. Their smooth collision free operation helped them to SOAR above the competition.

This team impressed the Judges with their tenacious spirit. They soared over challenges with their scrappy resourcefulness, hand crafting their own components and expanding their knowledge. These BIRDS are doing the impossible.
With a swarm of busy workers, this team displayed exemplary craftsmanship. They were buzzing with mechanical and electrical designs. For this team, Quality is a hive mentality!

This team impressed judges with a great imagination, determination and has a wrangler in the East. Their traveling roadshow at malls and fairs showcased their enthusiasm and even helped grow their team mentorship. Their spirit for STEM shines bright at the Shore.

Recruiting from local middle schools and school club events, this team develops an environment of inclusivity and a culture of respect to promote the teams objectives. They embodied the ideas of sustainability and risk management in every decision they make. Their electrifying spirit towards their future came through in their training plan and documentation.

This team roars through the autonomous phase of every match. They scored multiple cones in the top row and engaged on the charging station frequently. This team definitely made Timon and Pumbaa proud.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: There is a storm brewing in the creative and unique features of the design of this team's robot. Their flash of light from a local city contributed to their success in this competition. This group has banded together to enhance the charm of their robot in the strategy of play.

The judges are crazy about this team's numerous outreach events in their communities. Their influence is anything but sour as they inspire their competition and students in STEM. As Buzz would say, their impact goes "to Infinity and Beyond!"

This is a team that truly embodies the mission of FIRST. Through their mentoring and outreach efforts, including engineering camps and volunteering with community organizations, this team enthusiastically promotes STEM, robotics, and FIRST. This team is definitely in motion… a gear in motion… with sustained commitment to increasing awareness of STEM, they make a tremendous impact in their community while having fun along the way.
This team could work for Hasselhoff. Their story is a shining example of engineering excellence. Who invited this team to joust?

The judges were impressed by this team's willingness to travel to support a rookie team at an event that they were not competing in. They went above and beyond to share their expertise and materials with an new team. This team took pains to ensure that rookives would not experience the woe of the vanquished.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has a consistent and vibrant theme throughout all of its gear. Their herpetological robot similarly followed the theme. The persistence of orange was not an irrational choice.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: A machine fit for a king. A simple, elegant design elevating to the highest level. They make visiting teams red with envy.
This team eight up the competition. Their robot demonstrated great mobility and an innovative arm control mechanism. In the coliseum of robot competition, these gladiators excelled.
This team's communication is out of this world. They had several initiatives that emphasized leadership development. The judges were particularly impressed with this team's book clubs for team leads.
Hiding on a peninsula in Maryland, this team swims the high seas. Outstanding layout of their electro-mechanical systems led to robust design. Their robot made alphabet soup of the competition.

These young cubs impressed the judges with their fierce spirit and enthusiasm. They built a team from the ground up with unflagging determination and grit. Their feline bot showed cat-like agility as it roared across the field.

These enthusiastic flyers have gone to newer heights to passionately motivate the competition. They have soared above the rest with their ability to power up the crowd. This nest squawks with spirit and will always be Proud Of You!

This team clearly evaluates their mission to effectively transform their community. They strategically provide STEM opportunities to younger students. By their efforts, "Ah ha!" echoes throughout the mountains.

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: This team SHINES above the rest, demonstrating a BRILLIANT strategy that dictates design. With innovative sensing and gyro balancing they MINED a strong victory, CUTTING above the rest, congratulations team 4362 The Gems!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: They DISARMED the competition with a creative approach that removed an arm and is self-described as a 'forklift on a tractor', congratulations on the creativity team 6618 WARHBOTS!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: We are over the moon to announce this team that is self-STEERing and student-led, who didn't chicken out or horse around with their no-bull attitude when the STEAKS are high, congratulations team 5050 Cowtown Robotics!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: This is a young team coming to life over the past few years. Though little known just a few short years ago, they have made themselves known in their community by mentoring other local FLL and FTC teams and sharing their workspace. This rapidly growing team has POWERED up their efforts to increase their girl team members from just under 5% to 30% in just a few years. The team has an objective to show that robots are not just for boys; you can see it as half of their team has girls in leadership positions. They are PLUGGED into their community by partnering with their local food bank packaging over 5 tons of food for the needy, participating in the first PPE challenge during the pandemic, providing handmade blankets for the needy and shocking kids with their haunted trailer. This has brought a lot of local media attention in the local newspaper and in a Channel 7 TV segment showing their efforts to spread the FIRST message. We credit them for their assistance with the local community by working in summer camps to provide awareness to youths, participating in Girls Teach Girls to Code event and mentoring sixteen FLL and FTC teams. At home, they are working with the school administration to improve STEM offerings in the curriculum and are reaching out to the community in both English and Arabic. In addition, they are starting an initiative to establish FIRST teams in Lebanon. CHARGING forward they are spreading the message of FIRST locally and around the world.

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: This team STORMED the competition by having a lot of innovation in their sliding super structure and creative interchangeable grippers. Their robot forecasted clear signs that it would funnel away the win. Congratulations team 5090 TorqueNados!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: On this St. Patrick's Day weekend, the Irish tradition of hospitality was everywhere but one team's generosity of spirit stood out. For maintaining their toothy grin even while other teams were chewing up some of their time and resources, the award goes to team 7660 The Byting Irish!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: For their branding, name, design, and STRING of success, we celebrate their commitment to student leadership with enthusiasm and pride, Gerald23's team can definitely HACK it, congratulations team 6528 Terror Bytes!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Variety, versatility, and victory describes this team, with a sleek and simple design they SHIPPED out their opponents, all others gave up the GHOST before the mighty 3656 Dreadbots!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: To the team with all the charge, clawing their way through build and design excellence in robotics controls, we offer our SWARM congratulations to team 33 Killer Bees!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: A very hardworking team who dovetails FTC design into FRC Inspiration, a self-made 3D design befitting a RISING STAR who is right on TRACK, congratulations team 8423 Next Express.

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: After their EPIC voyage through rigorous robotic quality, they impressed with a rolling wheel design and multiple ways to score when even HECTOR could fall, congratulations team 3668 TroBots!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: Forging ahead into NEW TERRITORY they are doing everything they can to build a bright future in robotics, congratulations team 9226 GR Pioneers!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: This team ELECTRIFIES. They have the VIBE. Got those GOOGLY eyes, striking like a lightning bolt. Congratulations team 9182 Tech Tribe!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: Let's get a big cheer going for this team for their originality in design and logo, a student-led level of creativity in team cohesion, we CAN let you do that Dave, congratulations team 3604 Goon Squad!

records.eventName: FIM District Belleville Event presented by Belleville Yacht Club
records.script: With a TUNNEL vision focus on growth, longevity, sponsors, diversity, and mentorship, they are ON TRACK and full steam ahead, 1023 Bedford Express!

records.eventName: FIRST in Michigan State Championship presented by DTE Foundation
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award

records.eventName: FIRST in Michigan State Championship presented by DTE Foundation
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: Distance brought this nuclear team closer, and they were able to fuse together a crew which ignited interest and excitement. They engaged in advocacy outreach with STEM Saturdays, bumper construction workshops with clinics planned on CAD design, public speaking, and bridge design. They maintain a website that shares lessons learned. Their YouTube channel has garnered 5000 views. Two towns, two programming languages, 1 rubber ducky. The judges expect this team to continue to be a strong advocate for FIRST for many years to come. Congratulations, Team 9312, NERD Spark from Albion

records.eventName: FIRST in Michigan State Championship presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: This team BLEW the judges away with their integrated FIRST feeder programs, mentoring, 21 FLL and 6 FTC teams. With measurable outreach that impacted 14,000 people in the last year, they are STORMING through barriers to make their FIRST programs more accessible to the community. This team RED the criteria and they check all the boxes. Congratulations, Team 3875, Red Storm Robotics from Kentwood

records.eventName: FIRST in Michigan State Championship presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: This team is committed to providing a space to maximize access to FIRST programs for all students through their D, E, and I efforts. They are ADVOCATES for STEM funding at the local, state, FEDERAL, and international levels. They HAMMER down and continue to start and mentor teams across the SPECTRUM of FIRST. Whether they’re sharing LEGOs with toddlers or seniors, this team can be WITNESSED building relationships with all those around them to spread the message of FIRST. By developing their own leaders through their leadership retreat these AGENTS OF CHANGE are able to broaden their outreach programs, even reaching south of the border. Their impact is obvious, although these SPECIAL AGENTS worked undercover. CASE CLOSED! Qualifying for the Houston Championship is: Team 201, The Feds from Rochester

records.eventName: FIRST in Michigan State Championship presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: While this team has been around awhile, they continue to find ways to spread the mission of FIRST. They have established clear goals for the future. This team really BONDED with their school and community. This team understands ADVOCACY and has created a measurable impact on our state and nation by lobbying their representatives and members of Congress. This team has expanded their sub-teams to support Business and Analytics. Through the team’s career series on YouTube, they have expanded their reach and shared their expertise. This team quickly SWAM to the top of the pool! Qualifying for the Houston Championship is: Team 226, the Hammerheads from Troy

records.eventName: FIRST in Michigan State Championship presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: This team is composed of bright and motivated students who have a passion for STEM and the drive to make a difference in their communities. One of this team's core values is sustainability, and they take pride in their comprehensive sustainability plan. Through this plan, they have BONDED with other teams, sharing their knowledge and resources to help create a more sustainable world. They believe that small actions can have a significant impact, and they strive to inspire others to take action and make a difference. Advocating for STEM is also a critical part of this team's mission. They are proud to have had the opportunity to speak at local, state, and national levels to secure funding for STEM programs.
