Without them the event we would not hold -------- Although in school, they are not currently enrolled! This year's Judges Award goes TO THE JUDGES! (PAUSE - GIGGLE - Dramatic pause....) OK! Since we can't award ourselves - we were impressed with this team's wealth of solar power energy and neon visibility. We couldn't pick just one award possibility! The Judge's Award goes Team 5534 - the Onaway Onabots.

records.eventName: FIM District Escanaba Event presented by Highline Fast
records.script: You did not have us DECEIVED! Your robust bot could survive a smack into a concrete wall! Congrats Team 4392 The Deceivers!

records.eventName: FIM District Escanaba Event presented by Highline Fast
records.script: The Rookie All-Star award goes to a top performer who chiseled their way into the top 10. They support FIRSTs mission of inspiring and recruiting in the name of science, technology, and engineering. This team outperformed their own expectations and struck like a panther when given the opportunity. This years Rookie All-Star award goes to the Chassel Panthers!

records.eventName: FIM District Escanaba Event presented by Highline Fast
records.script: The Rookie Inspiration award goes to a team that has made a comeback and has inspired courage despite their size. Like a trout in a river they remained calm and just kept swimming their way south of the branch. This team inspires science and tech by hosting Sunday Funday in the name of science for their community. This years recipient of the Rookie Inspiration award are the Pantherbots!

records.eventName: FIM District Escanaba Event presented by Highline Fast
records.script: When the gears bind and slip, this team worked together without a blip. Their spirit knows no bounds, these robos cheer a thunderous sound. Bringing us home in orange and black, congratulate as the Team Spirit Award goes to 3602 - the Escanaba Robomos

records.eventName: FIM District Escanaba Event presented by Highline Fast
records.script: This team 'cashed' in on their electric '22 season. They established an ecosystem for new members and a lightening bright future. Congrats to team 5505 the V2 - Volts Squared.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.script: This robot blazed through the field as though sent by the gods. Scoring seemed automatic no matter where they started, and finishing was always balanced.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Gearing up can get very creative. This team definitely got the scoop and wanted to convey the news.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.script: This team is on fire Every week they inspire new engineers

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.script: This team's success is no mystery, their story for first impact is no yarn. Through involvement in community and school this team has an unwavering dedication to First.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.script: This team is never off but always on and up to speed. Their robots engineering excelled to their advantage.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.script: These cryptic creatures are always chasing opportunities to help others. Their reputation for gracious giving in the pits is recognized by their peers.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This noble creature shines bright through the night. From the Knight in the stands to the bot on the field, they inspire.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team strives for great strength and achievement. Striking a balance of form and function from a northern design.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.script: With an eye like a gem, this contestant seemed part animal and part machine. They used their vision to guide their mission.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.script: Their team model and culture makes everyone feel at home. Their inclusion and unity means they are anything but rogue.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.script: Undaunted by being small, the bear is in the details. Their energy and their excitement revealed their potential.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.script: Everyone reaches for the sky This team is demostrating it is on the right path for success

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.script: These sleuths are always looking to catch you in the act. They show team spirit to peers one trophy at a time.

records.eventName: FIM District Calvin University Event presented by Amway
records.script: You have to sail to new horizons to find what you need. This team created the critical mass to succeed.

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: To consistently place a cube or get to charge, this team made sure to "Land" in the right spot. They didn't get twisted, but stayed aligned each time. Congratulations to team #4422, Twisted Angels!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Strength and flexibility are core fiber to this team. Moving items were not lost in a whirlwind of complexity, but held together in 3D. Congratulations to team #5090, TorqueNados!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: This teams dark name may be misleading... They created a "key" to engineering passion... With 3D printed key chains with QR codes helping them ascend to win the Engineering Inspiration Award. Congratulations to team #4381, Twisted Devils!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: No local stops for this team. They are too busy riding the rails to state capital, when not helping international teams give a big steam whistle for the Bedford Express. Congratulations to team #1023, Bedford Express!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: This team has many hands in the design process and uses the skills and talents of all their members. They demonstrated their innovations both on and off the ground. Continue to use your tentacles to problem solve mechanical issues. Congratulations to team #8373, The Flying Octopi!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: When other teams faced a problem, this team helped them drive straight to a solution. They directed their energy throughout the pits, and became a force for good, helping teams find solutions that worked. Their great energy is the vector to the Gracious Professionalism Award. Congratulations to team #2611, Jacktown Vectors!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Harnessing the power of this schools mascot, this team soared. Matching robot and team provides a lasting image as they FLY. The winner of the imagery award will not be Draggin you down. Congratulations to team #302, The Dragons!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's robot was, ON BALANCE, an excellent example of industrial design. To stay ahead of the competition, they could always hit another GEAR, taking them to the highest SINGLE POINT. Congratulations to team #5066, Singularity!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: This team was uncanny in the design of their control system, allowing them to soar on the field. Their cyborg-like control panel is all buttoned up. Congratulations to team #2834, Bionic Black Hawks!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: This team won the judges award over with their unique design solutions and TOWERING team enthusiasm. Their tech allowed them to swerve the competition in the HEAT of the battle and their potential is SKY-HIGH. Congratulations to team #4453, The Red Hot Chili Bots!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: This teams robot is strong, not getting pushed around with assistance from carbon fiber. This strong carbon fiber robot doesn't get pushed around. The sturdy and robust design, as well as their shielding and "oversized tires," keep the robot in the battle. These warriors lit up the field, and fought until the end. Congratulations to team #2832, The Livonia Warriors!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: This team showed their spark to the judges. A community team who works six days a week. These nerds are a standout group. Congratulations to team #9312, Nerd Spark!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: This young teamis already taking flight. They are soaring inspiration to younger students. Congratulations to this fantastic team, team #9209, Fantastic Falcons!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: We are lucky to have this spirited team with us this year. Their enthusiasm, outfits, dancing, cheering and overall energy is infectious, they took a byte out of the competition. This unmatched sprit is why this shamrock wearing team is the winner of the Team Spirit Award. Congratulations to team #7660, The Byting Irish!

records.eventName: FIM District Jackson Event presented by Consumers Energy Foundation
records.script: They have gone above and beyond to recruit new students and electrified six new FLL teams. Through journaling and training, they build future leaders. Dollars and cents from NASA is only the beginning to sustain their robotics program. Congratulations to team #7166, Red Thunder Robotics!

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: Their robot has evolved from “bare bones” to a self-guided juggernaut. They use the gyro to sense their way on the field, and perfectly drop cones and climb the charging station. With a strong autonomous operation . . .

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This robot always plays a strong hand. Their ace is the unique paddle wheel intake that collects every trick along the way. The “king” is auto orientation.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: These cats Inspire our next generation of engineers. During the summer they spend 7 weeks running FLL and FTC camps. They sparked 8 new FLL teams over the last two years and influenced their school’s career tech curriculum using FIRST principles. They make choosing a career in engineering the cat’s MEOW!

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: This team is geared up for success in the foreseeable future. They took a step back, evaluated their involvement in all levels in FIRST as a result. They fabricated a plan to create a year-round development cycle for the teams they support and mentor. This resulted in a 79% participation increase from 2021 to 2022. Their students logged 1200 FTC and FLL volunteer hours and they host workshops and provide resources to many teams. In 2022 they were able to land an opportunity to meet with congressman Dan Kildee to advocate for FIRST in their community. This team is a world class team from a small town.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: This team’s robot is compact, clean, and aesthetically pleasing. Their telescoping arm design can extend quickly and pickup both cones and cubes. Installing the wiring on the inside of the arm allowed them to take a beating during competition, and keep on “trucking”.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: Just like titanium, this team is strong, durable and light. But it doesn’t just prowl and growl with the toughest competitors in THIS field. When FIRST teams in Pakistan and Israel reached out for assistance to build and program their robots, this team lent helping paws, providing information and guidance and answering questions.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When it comes to navigating the obstacles to success, this team steers, accelerates and avoids hazards automatically. With their prominent yellow and purple team colors adorning their robot, uniforms and neatly organized pit, there’s no way you could miss this team.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Fast retrieval & deployment without a flaw, using a telescopic arm and rotating claw, their spaceship is setup for fast and smooth operations. Industrial design is mastered by Goodrich Martians.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: This team’s shockingly innovative performance can best be measured in VOLTS. With many meneuvers at the press of a button, switches to adjust to the object, and autobalancing they were in total control.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: This team is an animal on and off the field. They adapted to resource limitations, made the most of their environment, and demonstrated ingenuity in overall design. This team was as busy as a beaver, and is being awarded the Judge’s Award for “Smart Engineering”.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: This team’s foresight helped them expect the unexpected. They prevented both mechanical and electrical failures with 3D printed parts to add stability, lexan panels and guards, and a pneumatics management system. We see BIG success in this team’s future.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: Like a STAR, this new team is bright and all fired up! They blaze a red path with spirited leadership. They will wake you up like a Pie in the Face!

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: This new team Flies across the field and pushes to score points. In the face of many challenges, it practices patience and provides defensive support to alliance partners. The team exhibits a Hawk-eyed focus to “get it done”.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: These bot builders collect points with enthusiasm. Their spirit is evident in the pit and in the stands! They support our military with gift baskets while on deployment. These Warriors are exploding with Spirit here and in their community.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #2 presented by Ford
records.script: This team’s roles and tasks are well defined and precisely measured in terms of Gannt charts. Their ingredients are well measured and mixed together at just the right time. This team doesn’t fight but figures out a way to infinitely split the Pi.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.script: It is better than a Tesla with no one on board. Nobody wants a wild robot roaming around. They didn’t throw PIXIE dust, but put their PIXIE camera in just the right spot.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The WIND was clearly LIFTING this team up. And giving them a GRIP on the problem. Their BUTTERFLY drive is what blew everyone away.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.script: There’s no need to be BLUE about this team’s STEM initiatives in their community. From summer camps to younger robotics teams there’s not just ONE thing this team does to promote engineering. With the future in their hands, we’re all glad they’re OUR NEXT ENGINEERS.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.teamName: Code Red Robotics the Stray Dogs
records.script: This team seems like they are really with the PROGRAM! Their approach to inspire the NEXT GENERATION of STEM superstars has built better people! DEW to their community outreach, everyone is seeing RED!

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.script: This team was able to deliver on all aspects of the machine including the design, machining, and fabrication of most of their parts. This team has an excellent HAND OFF with their dual-gripper system. They’re STRONG ARMING the competition with their impressive telescopic extension.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.script: The volunteer staff as a whole took note of this team's eagerness to take CONTROL of helping teams. When duty called, this team saw the RED light and jumped to action. The judges FREAKED out when they heard of this team's willingness to help all bots pass inspection.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s TECHNO theme spans from their robot to their pits. And the FRUITS of their labor really show in their cohesive brand. They’ve CAPTURED the judges’ attention, like a queen captures a knight, these blue & green TROJANS wowed us with their presentation.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This tidy and robust robot is a MAGNITUDE above the rest. Despite COLOSSAL PAIN with their claw redesign, this team has a rugged design in both their robot and LABVIEW DASHBOARDS.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.script: Swerving left and then to the right, this robot is always under control. A TWIST OF THE WRIST brings the robot closer to the goal. This team is DIALED into an INTERPLANETARY win.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.script: “The Jack of All Trades is Master of None, but often is better than Master of One”. This team made us Judges AFRAID that none of our choices would ever be made. For excellent performance across award categories,

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.script: This robot is very robust and LIGHTS things up. This team really makes the arena SHAKE. They left no QUESTION as to their dependability.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.script: This team came in FLAMIN’ HOT in their rookie season. With the support of their small community behind them, this team has left their mark. These terrific technicians are the talk of the town: T-TOWN to be specific.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.script: This rookie team might be small but they really stepped up to this year’s challenge by SWERVING through the competition. Adjusting on the FLY, this group took notes and made changes. This teams really shows what it’s like to A-SPIRES to greatness.

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.script: This team’s enthusiasm surrounding their pits and the event has judges TIED UP. They demonstrate an A to Z understanding of first and share that excitement with all. Their enthusiasm has the judges yelling YEEHAW!

records.eventName: FIM District Kentwood Event presented by Dematic
records.script: Team sustainability starts with a communication method that STICKS. This team made sure their students’ interest stays RED-HOT - building two separate robots. Watch out! This team is COOKIN’ up a sustainability STORM!

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: With their dual limelight setup, this team always knows its robot’s coordinates as it moves between zones. Match-to-match, their robot plots out a multidimensional array that tells it exactly where to strike. When it comes to their competition, lightning definitely strikes twice.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team really branched out with their ergonomically mounted controls board. Their unique inclusion of a ‘Butterfly-Drive’ allows them to gallop past the competition. This team got all charged up while under pressure. They are everyone’s favorite Pony for creativity, allowing them and their raffle-winners to take home the bacon.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: This team has gone above and beyond in their outreach efforts, from hosting paw-some events to mentoring other teams. They have truly embodied the spirit of FIRST Robotics. Their passion for outreach is claw-some, and their innovative approach to problem-solving is purr-fectly impressive. Their enthusiasm for robotics is fur-real and their hard work and dedication have inspired others in the community to chase their own tails of success. Congratulations to this team for their outstanding achievements, and we look froward to seeing their continued success in the future.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: With their laser-focused approach to orbiting the world of STEM, this team has become a role model in the field of robotics. Not only do they excel in their robotic endeavors, but they also place a significant emphasis on community outreach and advocacy programs. By assisting other FRC teams in weekly conferences, and mentoring FLL and FTC teams, this team has inspired countless individuals. Their commitment to giving back to their community is just one of the many reasons why they have become a shining example of what it means to be a FIRST team. Their accomplishments have been nothing short of stellar as they have fused together a team that orbits above the competition. This team has shown a level of dedication and perseverance that has propelled them to great heights, just like atoms.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: This team followed a track of engineering processes that led them to emphasize a solid drive train. They added wheels to their robot’s engine to keep it stable at the station. Their long chain-driven arm can grab both cones & cubes, and utilizes gravity to index the game piece for scoring. The functional design of their bungee-cord arm tensioning system shows that their problem-solving skills keeps them on the rails to success.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: This team scored on the ice and on the race track. Their collaboration with other teams exemplifies the principles of gracious professionalism. They truly embody and share their passion for Technology, Engineering, Science, Leadership, and Academics through everything they do.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s brand was creative and witty! Their cohesive spirit was seen in their pit, and throughout their entire team. Not all heroes wear capes, but these winners of imagery do.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team works to keep their design simple, efficient, and practical. They had a fiendish focus on component replaceability during the build out. Their robots’ functional layout, aesthetic, and simplicity show a devilish attention to detail.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: This team’s control systems showed both out-of-the-box and “in” the box thinking. They carefully watched their presets to ensure successful game piece placement. In a sea of teams with similar controllers, this team’s purpose-built control box pulled them onto the shores of success.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: Today, the judges have defined this as the Dependability award. A robot that has truly been the paw-fect example of reliability and consistency! With flawless execution and a consistent performance that would make even the Chicago Cubs jealous, this team has truly set the bar high for dependability in the world of robotics.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: This team is lightyears ahead with their automated scoring camera system. They flipped the script a week before the competition to rise to the occasion. This team’s telescoping arm helps them access distant planets. Red-rover Red-rover, send More Martians over.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: This team is planting the seeds for an Impact in FIRST. This team reached out to the community to form an all-rookie team in 6 weeks. They chopped through all their challenges to win a Rookie All-Star Award.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: This EVERY-bot might look like every other bot, but this 7-student team showed up daily to the Kettering FIRST Coliseum to build it, propelling their team to a new standard.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: You have to tip your hats to this team’s enthusiasm. This team’s spirit flowed through their members to their mentors, sponsors, parents, home town and the FIRST community. This team doesn’t need any additional power since they are already fully charged.

records.eventName: FIM District Kettering University Event #1 presented by Ford
records.script: Even though our winners have only been around for 2-years, they have demonstrated exceptional mentorship and opportunities for their students. They developed heroic practices and a solid business plan to help them on their journey. Their dedication to Argo-nomic and sustainable practices with their sponsors has earned them the golden screwdriver. Let’s give a round of applause to our heroes!

This team was able to TWIST and shout at the start of each match. Cube placement and balance on the charging station were achieved with three-point precision like the tines of a pitch fork. That noise in your ear is the Twisted Devils.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When it comes to creativity this team can’t be touched. Cylinders, switches, motors galore, this design can catch your eye and put some spring in your step. These players can really hammer down on snappy ways to used stored energy, MC Hammers.

This team has their whole community enthusiastically SWIMMING in sync. They inspire learning in their FTC and FLL affiliates to support long-term success. They’re great pit-partners, just avoid them at the BEACH! Team 4956 RoboSharks Qualifying to compete for the Engineering Inspiration Award at the District Championship is: RoboSharks.

This team seeks to inspire students in STEM and leadership all before their morning BREW. They BROADCAST the news of their accomplishments on radio, TV, and internet, too! Because of the impact of the FIRST program, they’ve created a STORM of interest in their community and in their school. But no RED flags here, because they have all the right tools, Red Storm.

Performing and scoring well above the mean. They redefined design by committee incorporating elements from all of the team. Designing, Learning and Adapting carries them to Olympus and beyond. The captain is pleased and so should Team Average Joes.

This team makes sportsmanship and working together CENTRAL to their values. Lending a hand and lifting up others FIRST and for at least a hundred years. This team had an impressive impact in this “Century” Team 21st Century Cyber Bearcats!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This teams quack and pink passion extends from their goosey fashion. This team gets all sweetened up by their Charlie inspired robot. Coordinated and sharp this team is DOWN with style, Q-Branch Robotics.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team elevated cubes and cones to challenging heights. Their lightweight and strong design utilizing aircraft grade materials allowed them to strike a balance of need. This team’s design was a show of Force, team Stryke Force.

This Team consistently looks before they leap with mathematical precision. Using feed-back they were always calculating their next jump. Their latest leap has them firmly on the winners pad, Frog Force.

The FIM Lakeview #2 Judges Award is being given to a team that showed Honor, Strength, Ambition and Cleverness. They learned that glory is not always found in having what you want but succeeding with what you have. In battle, they respected their opponents and more experienced teams alike and were always ready to lend their hand to others. From the land of ice and snow the Valhalla Nation.

This team found the Midas touch for quality design. No other robot looks like it, no other robot lasts like it. Quality planning from start to finish produced RIVETING performances on the field. They won’t lose their heads, as they RAM their way to victory. Team RoboRams.

This team can be seen blazing across the night sky, and will return again and again. They are made bright by the power of their sponsors and their drive. They may be rookies, but that comet streaking past is a sign of promise.

This team was king of the jungle when it came to energy, motivation and perseverance. Overcoming limited resources and the usual robot modifications on the fly, they still roar with respect and appreciation for everything FIRST. There’s nothing cowardly about this rookie team, the Newaygo Lions.

While small in number now, this team has shown how mighty they can be. Meshing together to make their presence known, they show it’s cool to be a gearhead. From the mountain tops to the valley below, RV Gearheads.

This team has been able to grow and sustain by wrangling in new team members, mentors and corporate support. They developed a business plan to help them keep focus on lassoing in the tasks for the current year helping to meet timelines and looking to the horizon for future planning. This team is just as much at home at FIRST as on the range, the RoboRangers.

records.eventName: FIM District Lakeview Event #1 presented by Parker-Hannifin
records.script: With four different modes to choose from, and a “LIGHTENED” 3d PURPLE printed arm, this team consistently demonstrated autonomous mode performance. During one match, with the JACKED up difficultly of an opponent laying across their charging station, this robot proved their success with a gyro, and VECTOR math.

records.eventName: FIM District Lakeview Event #1 presented by Parker-Hannifin
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team lived up to their name by bringing more than just a little creativity and elegance in their design. Their 3D printed claw was a masterpiece of simplicity and effectiveness that left the judges amazed. There’s ALLOTTA more than just robots on this team.

records.eventName: FIM District Lakeview Event #1 presented by Parker-Hannifin
records.script: This DIVERSE team used the offseason to organize several community outreach events. The were the IGNITION source that inspired sponsors, recruits and fellow teams to engineering excellence Their commitment to the FIRST mission never WAIVERED.

records.eventName: FIM District Lakeview Event #1 presented by Parker-Hannifin
records.script: It’s a jungle out there! You need to be above the competition to see the challenges ahead. Expanding STEM and FIRST by mentoring teams in CAD and Programming outside of Michigan. Or, hosting district events, scout camps, and helping kids with disabilities in Michigan This team is showing far and wide it is more than just a Robot.

records.eventName: FIM District Lakeview Event #1 presented by Parker-Hannifin
records.script: These cool Cats are Facing the competition with an innovative design, professional development process, and a wired attitude. If you are in Kalamazoo and need excellent engineering advice, look no further than the Wired Cats.

records.eventName: FIM District Lakeview Event #1 presented by Parker-Hannifin
records.script: This team exudes positivity and enthusiasm for FIRST. They have used their experience and know how to plant new teams and they often leave the confines of their own ENCLOSURE to go collaborate with the other ANIMALS. Their mantra of “fail fast, fail frequently but always fail forward” embodies the spirit of perseverance critical to success in First. We think this award will perfectly adorn the walls of their ZOO.

records.eventName: FIM District Lakeview Event #1 presented by Parker-Hannifin
FIM District Lakeview Event #1 presented by Parker-Hannifin
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This robot and team were visually STUNNING. In another world some would say that they were MOST EXCELLENT! Respect these MOUNTIES from the NORTHWEST. PARTY ON WAYNE!

Every team this year was charged up, but this team was electric. They bring their own brand of power to 'robots in the park' and relay for life. Their strike has impact around the globe. Congratulations to team #862, Lightning Robotics
This teams excellence in tech BARKS back at the competition. No bot can put this team on a leash. Congratulations to team #3707, The Technodogs

This team doesn't hesitate to swoop in for those in need. Their roost is a beacon of positivity for those around them. This is the wind beneath these eagles wings. Congratulations to team #3568, RoboEagles

Like VIKINGS set forth to discover new lands. This team takes PRIDE in recruiting students with diverse talents. Looking to advance science and technology in the state capital area. Congratulations to team #9241, EV Robotics
You've heard their spirited battle cry, you've seen their purple pride, you know these proud warriors have a spirit you can't deny. Congratulations to team #1076, Pi Hi Samurai
Right side up or upside down, this team is in it for the long-haul. These bulldogs are achieving their mission like the boss. Congratulations to team #5509, Like a Boss

records.script: Trying to balance on the charging station can make your robot “Rocky” or tippy. This team consistently scored well in their automation round with a “one, two punch” on cone placement and charging. They never “Threw in the towel” and finished with a high score “Before the Final Bell”.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Albert Einstein once said “Creativity is seeing what others see and thinking what no one else thought” This team uniquely thought of balancing the robot with “crab walk” technique. The pick and place of the objects was very impressive. The robot was sturdy, well-built, and maneuvered smoothly around.

This team courageously took up the torch to lead their area in STEM learning. They spread the teachings of FIRST and STEM through events that reach their school, other FIRST organizations, and communities statewide. They “Bravely” lead the way in advancing respect and appreciation for engineering.

The pandemic didn’t slow this team down. From starting a Girls Coding Club and a school therapy dog program to petitioning their school board to get Narcan in school buildings and planning a new STEM Center for their community, this team initiated numerous programs in recent years. This “Empire” is taking over the FIRST galaxy.

Much like Smaug hoarded Durin’s riches, this team grabbed points and laid waste to the competition. This team’s engineering soared and they were breathing fire with their technical descriptions. Their iterative approach and multiple grip designs made them fast, robust, precise, and decisive.

Working together and building relations is straight and consistent, not like the “hills” from where this team originates. They help so many teams succeed, not even allowing boundaries or borders to hold them back. This team is “adamant” about holding up to all that makes up Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team stood head and “neck” above the competition by embracing the look of their robot and adopting a zoological theme. With this team you don’t have to travel to “Madagascar” to find your safari guide.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team used a detailed process to design and construct a clean and functional robot worthy of industry. They double and even “triple” checked their design drawings as they developed their robot. On the field this team was “Red”-dy for any challenge.

This team may know about the “Loons” but their attention to keeping their robot in bounds means they are serious about their craft. Onboard sensors and controls helped the driver find their way which made for great “chemistry” between human and machine. It helps to maximize your innovation if you want to lead “The Charge.”

The Small But Mighty Award Although small, this team has “demon”-strated might and courage through tough times. Their “youthful” smiles and can-do attitude show their positive and competitive spirit. By demonstrating exceptional teamwork and unrelenting their drive to succeed, these brave “Bounty Hunters” accomplished their mission and canned our Judge’s award.

This team looked to technology, history, and even mythology for their inspiration. Built to compete and beautifully well documented, their QFD, “Quality, Function, and Deployment” analysis made our checklist. The Kirin, a creature of renewal, grace, and prosperity was the “Bravest Toaster” in this competition.

As a rookie team, they “soared” high in their first “flight.” Part of what makes this group All Stars is how they didn’t let anything “ruffle their feathers.” While they are new to the flock, their commitment to simplicity and their enthusiasm make them great examples of what the future of FIRST looks like.

These newbies quickly reached out to give people a helping hand…or at least a thumb. A budding love of robots grew from a microtronics class and sent these students on a quest to compete. Learning as a team and having a great time will inspire them for years to come.
The members of this team are “Kings” and “Queens” of FIRST spirit. They were the “Ace” in the stands for excitement. This team’s success is “In the Cards.”

You may have heard it through the “pipeline” that this team has the “horsepower” to compete for years to come. They have “corralled” students to their program through their camps and mentoring. They have taken up the “reins” of sustainability.

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: This machine flies around the field…..With 11 encoders and a gyro, they score a cone and balance on the charge station in the blink of an eye Using their industrial inspired arm, they are able to score at any position on the grid with the push of a button Don’t be confused by their imagery, they will STING you during autonomous! Congratulations, Team number 3538 RoboJackets

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team strode into the competition with confidence in their step, ready to break a leg They COUNTERED the game challenge creatively, BALANCING their design with innovation Roll out the red carpet and turn on the spotlight! Congratulations, Team number 7211 Hollywood

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: This team’s mascot may be small in size, but the team is large in character as they inspire others. They have a POSITIVE approach with their community outreach, summer camps and monthly blogs They are a central nucleus in their community promoting STEM locally and nationally Qualifying to compete for the Engineering Inspiration Award at the District Championship is: Team number 245 Adambots

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: When there is a need for help in the FIRST community, you will find this team there Their focus on FIRST sustainability and commitment includes mentoring FLL and FTC teams in their region. They expand FRC by hosting rookie events to enable others to learn and grow. Last fall they increased their IMPACT by hosting an FTC event They participate in outreach on their own and with other FIRST teams During the offseason, they expanded their JUNGLE HABITAT by inviting another high school to come join the fun. This team makes the judges go…… BANANAS!!! Congratulations, Team number 469 Las Guerillas

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: When it comes to engineering, this team knows the formula for excellence A design focused on centralizing their heavy components TANGENT to L.E.D.’s and sensors that let them see what others can’t was the SINE to the judges they had covered all the ANGLES Alert the nerds! Congratulations, Team number 2337 EngiNERDS

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: This team is evolving into community leaders with extensive outreach and partnerships with organizations in their community They gear up to help teams at competitions with creative and effective plans They CRAVE for solutions with their ongoing gracious professionalism…. Congratulations, Team number 2851 Crevolution

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: A unified message begins with a solid foundation of inspired students Stone by stone this team built a cohesive theme from the pit to the robot to the mascot and the school They can handle any siege that challenges their castle Congratulations, Team number 6566 Battering Rams

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team designs with a TOUCH of elegance They FLEW into the competition with a robot that blends functionality with form They reach for opportunity and grasp it in their CLAWS…. “forever more”! Congratulations, Team number 1188 Ravens

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: This team’s robot uses a MONSTROUS array of sensors and controls Their complex code integrates cameras, LIDAR, dual gyroscopes, encoders, and a string POT. P.I.D. control and an efficient autonomous mode decreases their cycle time. This mythical fire breathing team uses great innovation to torch this year’s game! Congratulations, Team number 1684 The Chimeras

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: The JUDGES AWARD for VERSATILITY With an auton for both sides of the charging station and operator control box that will make your eyes spin, this jack of all trades team is not messing around. This team is like an oasis for other teams. They incorporate FRC curriculum in their school and lead outreach activities like Barbecue with Bots This team is so hot they are FROZEN Congratulations, Team number 910 The Foley Freeze.

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: They came out of the TREES shining and bright! Sleek and maintainable with separate energies Quality shines through when this team all ROWs together! Congratulations, Team number 7769 The CREW

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: This rookie team has cooked up a great approach to achieve future goals and tackle technical challenges They spread the FIRST message by sending t-shirts from the capital to friends across the world They are shaking up the competition with their leadership and spirit Qualifying to compete for the Rookie All-Star Award at the District Championship is: Team Number: 9203 Quake

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: This team could be lounging and surfing in their local waters….. But instead they pursue a BURNING passion to improve for the future They have the FIRE to expand FIRST’s mission even with pie in their face! Congratulations, Team number 9237 Swartz Creek Dragonators

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: This team has a spirit that takes flight from school to community They inspire sponsors, their school board and community with a FULL HOUSE of both FTC and FLL teams Its no GAMBLE betting on this team, they are definitely working with a full deck! Congratulations, Team number 3534 House of Cards

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #2 presented by Magna
records.script: This team is a consistent ELEMENT in the competition, with great team spirit and passion for FIRST Using an effective COMPOUND of outreach, mentoring and communications to sustain the mission of FIRST in their team and community This team’s CHEMISTRY puts them on a path to success! Congratulations, Team number 4384 Benzene Bots

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: Staying on time to make their rounds. Delivering once, then twice, and grabbing a third. They keep their engine revving like a HOT ROD.
