records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team starts with a strong arm, delivers with a firm GRIPPER, and finishes with a delicate puff of air, all in the NICK OF TIME. They would make Doc Brown proud!

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: This team nurtures a philosophy of inclusive FIRST experiences and outreach. They Adopt-A-Road, and work with sponsors and international teams. These fighters foster sustainability and diverse technical opportunities for all. And it's a SKIRT, not a KILT!

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: This team can be seen throughout all levels of FIRST. The judges were impressed with their robust efforts toward mentoring, hosting, and reaching a wider, diverse population that may not be familiar with FIRST. They celebrate their successful efforts to expand teams in their home city and were invited to review and comment on planned facilities to support STEM in their community. The recent passing of funding won't give them any reason to COAST, and this will open a SEA of opportunities for them to do even more. This team SCHOOLED the competition with their commitment to making an impact by hosting annual competition and skill building events and introducing STEM to MINNOWS within their community. When found in the wild you'll see them advocating for STEM at conferences and HAMMERING out approaches to increase awareness and funding of STEM. Individually they are a drop of water, together they are an ocean. Congratulations Team 226, the Hammerheads.

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: This team built a new process to save valuable resources. Design twice, approve thrice, build once. They continue to EVOLVE their CREATION.

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: This team practices GP everywhere. They have a FARM system supporting FLL, FTC, and FRC teams. To do all this they have FLOWN THE COOP.

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When this team ROLLS UP to the competition, they are immediately recognizable from the consistency in their uniforms, pit, and robot design. They DIG their CLAWS of branding into the community, spreading awareness and increasing sponsorship. Don't let the cute EARS fool you, their BLUE and GREY ARMOR is tough.

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team used a simple, robust design and student led fabrication to POUNCE on this year's challenge. We were impressed by their focus on continuous improvement, their fast swap batteries, and their commitment to a 5 minute fix for all major systems. To us it's no surprise these CATS brought a fierce BOT to this competition.

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: This team's robot features a complex arm system to COMBAT this year's game. And to control this scoring machine, they BAKED-UP a simple but effective controls box to automate all arm functions. To us, this team's controls were RIGHT ON THE BUTTON.

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: The Judges award for Versatility in FIRST Principles. Like a Swiss army knife, this team has SPLIT utility and excels in all areas of the competition. They are REVOLUTIONARY in how they train their team and include others while their modular robot design TACTICS impressed the judges. Their ability to sustain their ARMY through spreading the FIRST values in so many ways is BANANAS!

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: It's not just one thing that makes a robot great. It takes a powerful combination of student leaders to produce the performance, durability, and capability needed to weather the storm. Their robot enters the competition field with a BANG and a structurally sound honeycomb base. A rock solid, well-designed telescoping arm gives them the reach they need, and hairpins allow for rapid servicing. They leave the field not black and blue, but BLUE and ORANGE.

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: It is no secret that this team made a big SPLASH in their first year of competition with their focus on defense. They have the right MAP to find themselves at the top of the competition with their recruiting efforts and focus on learning and fun. This team's future is as good as GOLD.

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: This rookie team has placed its STAKE in robotics. Creating flyers and word of mouth to share STEM club robotics in their school and community. These TRAILBLAZERS will continue to PIONEER robotics in their school.

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: This team is completely connected to their community from COAST TO COAST. Like the SUN, they turn up the heat to achieve great things. But watch out, alpacas' spit!

records.eventName: FIM District Troy Event #1 presented by Aptiv
records.script: This team has strong BRANCHES to sustain their success. Summer programs support many, many FLL and FTC teams, and they focus on developing future Wonder Women of STEM. They don't get bogged down with BEUROCRACY. They reach out to local authorities to ensure resources for a global connection. Once a CADET, always a CADET!

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.script: Using straight forward timing to independently place objects high, this predator creatively uses modern gryoscopes and Dynamic Speed Control to replicate the balance of a 99 million year old creature. They proved their capability in autonomy as one of the leaders of the pack of veloci-raptors. Congratulations, Team 1711, the Raptors from Traverse City.

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Marching onto the field with a mite-y army and the support of their community, this team’s creative engineering and strong social media presence are two halves of a single unit. Faced with limited resources, this team came up with a creative solution that allows them to collect and place game pieces without time-consuming turns. Sum-ming it up, this team is full of all-stars. Congratulations, Team 2246 the Army of Sum from Johannesburg.

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.script: Plato famously wrote “our need will be the real creator.” For this team, their needs sparked inspiration. Their need for members inspired them to invite two other local schools to join them. Their need for a robot that withstands the rigors of game play inspired them to develop an engineering design process just as robust. They come from a small town, but they have a big impact. The award for Engineering Inspiration goes to Team #3688 Norsemen Robotics! Congratulations, Team number 3688 the Norsemen Robotics from Suttons Bay

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.script: This team makes an outstanding Impact on their community! They bring water to the match to keep team’s fast paces. They serve up Bots and BBQ while shaving cold faces. If you need a cute dog for a day, to help with therapy don’t fret. Just call this Team! Congratulations, Team 910, Foley Freeze, from Madison Heights

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.script: Engineered for reparability, this light weight robot with a low center of gravity flies across the field. This flock reimagined their design process which began with a strategy, and lead to excellent engineering of modules; including drive train, intake, elevator, and claw systems. Their mascot makes a squeaky, high-pitched, klee call, but this robot soars above all. Congratulations, Team 2834 , The Bionic Black Hawks from Bloomfield Hills.

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.script: Whether your team needs ideas, expertise or a little practice these knights are always ready to ride out to help all members of the FRC kingdom. Since 2010, this chivalrous crew has generously responded to many requests AND shared its resources with teams that are new and emerging. Congratulations, Team 3618 the Petoskey Paladins!

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Coming out with both flash and bang, this pack is on the hunt for victory. With fast and fur-rious speed, this Wile E. team has the competition howling. Unofficially sponsored by Acme Corporation. Congratulations, Team 3603 the Cyber Coyotes, from Reed City.

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s limited resources drove a simple focused design that includes high speed and the ability to maneuver cubes and cones down low. They developed their robot to make room for others by hanging on the edge. With industrial reliability, this bot is your best ally. Congratulations, Team 4983 , The IronBots from Mancelona

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.script: This team had several innovative features. From a control panel that can be updated to meet the needs of the operator and each specific competition to a unique counterweight that prevents their claw from taking flight. A refined tunable design wears an orange coat. Congratulations, Team 7160, The O-bots, from Ludington.

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.script: We sea great things happening for this team as they grow their next generation of competitors. From the lakeshore to the woods, this team brings together students of different ages to rise to the challenge of competition. This team wins the Judges Award for Tapping New Potential. Congratulations, Team 5562, The Anchor Bots from Glen Lake.

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.script: Through dogged determination, this team built a robot that wheelie does well on the course. Using requirements-based engineering, the team began their plan by looking at the game and developing a quality strategy. They’re not just lucky leprechauns – Congratulations, Team 3767, Titan Robotics from Traverse City.

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.script: Spearheading STEM at their school, this rookie team is small fry now, but is making a big splash in their first season. Sturgeon forward, this team is learning fast and has plans to engage with their community. With more than 10% of their student body involved, this club is a great catch for their school. Congratulations, Team 9176, The Greenspire Steel Sturgeons from Traverse City.

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.script: Keeping an eye on the bay, the limelight on their bot picks out cones and cubes. This unified team functions like a family and their positive attitude helped propel their team into the upper ranks. Congratulations, Team 7790 Baywatch Robotics from Harbor Springs.

records.eventName: FIM District Traverse City Event presented by "Cone Drive by Timken"
records.script: If your team has caught the fire at a Saturday Game Kickoff or you’ve heard about a marshmallow catapult, you already know why this glowing group will be around for years to come. This team is known throughout the north for increasing First participation with other teams and and within their town. Congratulations, Team 4377, Boyle City Blaze.

These grand students are no strangers to orbiting the sun. This team worked to automate their robot as much as possible, and it really showed in their outstanding autonomous program. Zipping across the field at mach speed, blink and you’ll miss this robot scoring on the grid.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Illuminating the competition with a rainbow tower, this team thinks out of the box. Pieces are placed with the assistance of red and yellow position indicators. Lighting their way to success is team 2054.

This team spreads the love of engineering to all members of its community. From library camp, innovation fairs, and programming camps, they continually build the brains of the next generation of engineers.

Before a team can REALLY shine, there are some things that need to happen. FIRST, they have to inspire kids to love STEM. This team has CHARGED UP STEM interest locally, using multiple power sources. Once interest is GENERATED, they PLUG them into the FIRST community. Lego Leagues are an important branch of the FIRST family and this team has done a great job of connecting them to THIS circuit. This team brings the power of FIRST together by opening their field to others, hosting large events, and CHARGING UP rookie teams in their inaugural season. There is no doubt that this team SHINES LIGHT on FIRST and positively IMPACTS everyone from the youngest kids to the most senior mentors and volunteers. Thank you for turning the LIGHTS ON to create a BRIGHTER future for this organization. Congrats Team 107 R.O.B.O.T.I.C.S!
This team engineered a solid PICKER UPPER and DROPPER OFF-ER With AWESOME PARTS to keep it together- They really showed us the MAGIC!
From cables to wires their humanity stood out, helping others in need this one team had no doubt. Grippingly gracious they found the root cause, congrats team 4967, this one team really stood out

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Not an alien to robotic competitions, this team goes green while getting charged up. Their tie dye shirts even coordinate with their robot. Let’s hear it for our celestial neighbors, the Martians, team 494.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team wowed us with their wildly sophisticated and compact design including beautifully labeled cables! The robot’s intake arm scooped up cones over cubes and delivered them with speedy and sleek grace. This team is dominating its matches with feline scratches!

This team uses their code to deliver the load. These students are out of this world if truth were told! With their amazing mechanization being controlled with outstanding automization the judges were more than sold. Red rover, red rover, more martians come over!

The judges are so excited to present the Judges Award to a team who exemplifies being: S - Strong in their community. A - Always helping kids. F - Finding ways to stay fit. E - Everyone is trained to respond in crisis. T - Tons of student interests represented. and Y - You are constantly finding ways to RESPOND to a wide variety of needs. Our Heart is CODE RED ROBOTICS – THE FIRST RESPONDERS.

It’s been shown that a triangle is the strongest shape. With a professional design process producing a robust robot - there’s no arguing this team has a quality product. This team has red hot scoring abilities that demonstrate their excellent overall design.

This young team of home schoolers with multiple sponsors is well on their way to full charge. Enthusiastically dedicated, they continue to energize their broad base. Soon to be a powerful veteran team – congratulate team 9222.

Drawing from internal inspiration this team flies to the call of FIRST. On the wings of success, they will continue to inspire others in their nest. Their drive to encourage STEM participation makes them the smartest birds in their class. Let’s hear it for team 9248.

This thundering herd is Ram strong with diverse talent. Their all-freshman drive team is enthusiastically lifted by team and fan encouragement and praise. Welding their way to spirited success, congrats team 4855.

In finding their way through the woes of COVID, this team rebuilt, sustained and coded! Alumni guiding, sponsors growing, this bot drove the lot and kept on going. A lot more than just money or a robot, 141 congrats and keep on going.
They made a U-turn to help others in need. And their autonomous mode is graceful indeed. Their code has field mode and they lead the way. Robotics is in their DNA.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This mystery is not hard to glean, Through their poly carb panels so keen. With a singular tram, Recycling’s their jam; We CLAP for the Mystery Machine!

Do not be deceived by a robot so fine. With iterative steps to improve their design. Balanced use of CAD to keep parts level. And laser cutting for precision of metal. AprilTags let them place cubes hands-free. This robot would capture the heart of Wall-E.
Whether in the pits or on the practice field, tools and support this team does share Out of the blue and with good will, Rockford’s bumpers they helped repair

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Though exemplifying a unified aesthetic with a rich history, This team, machine, and pit remain shrouded in mystery, Their dedication to visual imagery leads the pack Secret handshakes, glowing robot, and a team cloaked in black

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: They brought a trimmed machine. Modeled in CAD, an engineering dream. Even the camera field of view gleamed. The HEX became the Industrial Design Team.
It was foretold, a great spartan shall rise within Controlling and protecting cargo with pointed precision Their lineage derives from an ice cold spring with a rachet in hand

records.teamName: Robo Remedy @ Mantiowoc Lutheran High School
records.script: This team carefully documented their design book Their robot was inspired by a common trash hook Their outreach lifts their community to new heights Reaching their neighbors through fairs and STEM nights Collaborating on CAD mode reduces their toil And their energy solution on E-OIL!

Be it cube or cone, we don’t care. Neither one, on the field, we will spare. We came North from “Lake MISH” with the fervent wish. To take “charge” with quality and flair. We begin, to improve on our build. Ideas were spilled. Parts carefully milled. Then Chip was assembled with ultimate care.
Because of their outreach, recruitment, and training, Their passion and commitment to science we can glean. They value diversity and prioritize safety, We all should be inspired by the Green Machine.

When the pandemic hit…some teams were down and out; but this team was out and about. They did not let distance create a wall; and opened their robotics home to all. Their impact on the community was great; when their robot was used to haul freight.

Setting their course North, brought their BOOTY to Duluth. No matter where their sails took them to the field or in the stands, they shared a treasure of enthusiasm When you hear the cheers the tricorns are near with team spirit.

The sharp blade glints in the arena, as this team rallies to battle with heart fierce and strong Through coaching and mentoring, they unite their community with care. Their strategic marketing and social presence, ensure through they will thrive and fare Their sabers are the cutting edge of sustainability!
This team “charged up” with energy from the sun Their programming was second to none This autonomous award is heading southwest to be won

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The battle for this award took perseverance and imagination. This team fights hard for points before finishing on the charge station. For testing using solutions typically reserved for handling hot pots, the creativity award goes to team 6421!

With engineering and design so grand, this team will take the stand. Their engineering process left us in awe, and teamwork is what we saw. A robot that’s simply glorious, let me introduce you to Scorpious.

When other teams were in distress, this team responded with a level of sportsmanship as high as their Hair. Through the riot of other teams panic, a blue streak appeared from the HighFalls with support and spare parts. This team glides with gracious professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From robot to team, the details match a theme They stand out in a crowd and their looks a slam dunk

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Sleekly unique with an up-cycled beak, this team humbly displayed an iron foundation with nimble negotiation skills!
Rarely related to any of the others. This ridiculously rotatable robot is something to regard!
Their school may be small, but their vision is large. Their inclusive culture left us positively charged. Not a lone monarch, more like birds of a feather, Team 3926 shows us we’re stronger together.
This team signaled with their LED lights near the floor Their robot was robust, scoring points galore We want to see this quality robot and red bowties more

This team isn’t afraid to set measurable goals for themselves. They utilize their tools and opportunities to grow and impact the robotics community through inventiveness and commitment to science and technology for future progress. They have vision for the future and their passion for growth in engineering sets the standards for not just “American” but world class excellence in a student driven competitive Robotics program.

-This well rounded team is encouraging STEM experiences to all students at their school -Expanding STEM and FIRST throughout their state. -All team members mentor younger FIRST teams -And their DEI efforts ensure that everyone has a seat at the table -Oh, that was a trip, did you get that BINGO?

This team Roars like a great river whose supporting their leader. They have a “dye” hard energy that is tied with an all inclusive attitude that makes new comers feel welcome. There is no need for a mystical reading to see this team has a high level of positive energy

The team we honor here has shown that they are sustainable for many years. Their influence is far and wide with education, safety, and social media programs they provide. The Ripple has turned into a Wave that even NASA came to Rave.

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: This team used encoders and a gyroscope to score every time in auto. They kept their eyes on the prize, designing an auto sequence that can balance on the charging station or score for mobility. They were truly on fire with their fast, perfectly timed auto sequence. This award goes to Team 2846, FireBears.

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When looking at the game, this team wanted to approach from any direction. They were able to turn the tables and put themselves in a position to succeed. Congratulations to team 2823, The Automatons!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: This team engineered their way to the skies from the meadows. They believe in simple-is-better, but went through rigorous design reviews. This team clinched the Engineering Excellence Award with their claws. Congratulations, Team 2502, Talon Robotics.

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: This team may have redesigned their robot in three days, but they carried a spirit of coopertition and collaboration throughout the months leading up to this weekend. This team wasn’t chilly, but rode the winds of gracious professionalism and paying it forward to a successful competition. Congratulations, Team 2450, Wind Chill!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Looking at this team and their machine, it’s not hard to find the common link. While inspiring inclusivity, one also is reminded that fashion and function can be in sync. This Imagery Award confirms skirts are ok, as long as your leggings (for safety) are pink. Congratulations Team 2177, The Robettes!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Simplified design was the story this year, focused on what they do best. Small and efficient, fast on the blocks, and a design based on rigorous test with LEDs that shine bright from the robot’s brain. The Industrial Design aware goes to the G.E.A.R.s from Blaine!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: This team’s control system features an arm that can reach both in front and back and straight up to balance. When navigating the herd, they made re-orientation look easy, integration of gyros, encoders, limit switches, April tags, and programming set them up for success in the game. The innovation in control award goes to Team 3630, Stampede!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: The ingredients of success include teamwork and a positivity pop! The team has made room for all voices and engaged its successful freshman crop. They have mixed in continual improvement, while having fun, so let the Judges Award drop. Congratulations Team 2549, Millerbots!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: On the shores of Gitchee Gumee, this team was firm and strong. Their process well-defined, which helped them all day long. Running into walls for test, keeping low to the ground, Hiawatha Robolobos showed the highest quality around. Congratulations Team 7258 for the Quality Award!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: This student-driven team is a subscriber to face-to-face communications. Executing a purr-fect mix of summer camps and sponsor visits has brought technology education and awareness to many. It’s plain to see that their inspirational efforts are generating meaningful team growth. Please congratulate Team 4663, Cyber Tigers.

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: Unicorns prance in a tie-dyed frenzy, A STEM home for all, opens doors aplenty. Meals to accommodate, fuel for the brain, NoMythic 2491, where futures are gained. Congratulations Team 2491!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: Getting started is the hardest part. This team built themselves up with support from their community and a vortex of spirit within their team. Automating themselves to victory, congratulations Team 9157, Iconic Polars.

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: A creature has re-emerged from a pile of dust. After four years of hibernation this team’s enthusiasm fed their re-birth. This squad is the manifestation of Team Sprit. Congratulations BEASTBOT, Team 2855.

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: Not just any day is this golden award given. They dig their way through challenging terrain to keep an open path for all. Their strong business plan Brightens their student’s future. Congrats to team 2052, KnightKrawler!

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.script: This team has their autonomous on lock. Using limelight and sensors to get the game pieces on top The use of sensors doesn’t end after the first 15 seconds Instead during teleop you’ll find them using buttons to lead their robot to the right spot.

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: They came from the north from a school with a hyphen, but season progression brought a trouble horizon. When their drive train caused difficulty balancing in place, pneumatic brakes were added to lift it with grace. When alliance partners joined the charge station racket, arm angle adjustment fit like a warm comfy jacket!

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.script: This cube-crushing robot is loaded with creative, functional solutions to challenging problems. It takes, it grips, and it places with grace and reliability. The team followed a model engineering design process with one feature going through 18 iterations to reach the optimum. The result? Engineering that utterly dominates.

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.script: Despite not having a programming mentor, this reptile team’s code-able skills will become that of lore. Coming out of its shell, they generously rewarded other teams with their programming knowledge.

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s bright energy was visible a mile away. The robot and the team illuminated the field, radiated the pits, and everybody else around them. They blended form and function with a robot that reflects the team’s theme. Their comic and tropical energy earns this team the imagery award!

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Equipped with a Team Certified in SolidWorks and water jet technology, this Team Created an elegant functional gantry. They Combined 7 motors with linear bearing, Taking Cost into account. They Creatively struck the balance between from, function, and aesthetics.

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.script: This team used a delicious mathematical constant to position their arm to any point in 3D space. Using live inverse kinematics, vision-calibrated swerve odometry, and inverse multiplexed custom PCB buttons, this team created a lifelike and effective arm….or should I say beak?

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.script: This team has experience the power of FIRST and it shows on the field and in the team. They have a versatile, unique, and high performing robot. This team advances knowledge and respect of robotics in their community. The judges are happy to recognize the hard work of over 2,000 hours this team of five has put inot this season. We’re excited to see where they go next.

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.script: Their bot is robust, And moves with ease, It scores well too With features to please. All thing have a spot Held tightly in place So safe and secure No matter the space The team may be small But they play it straight The quality award Goes to team 3848!

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.script: Community inspiration in STEM is not the only trait in their instruction set. This team synthesized a robotics class, and convinced their school to support their team, with teachers and coaches promoting robotics. Their influence extended beyond the shop, with the team community outreach in local steam festivals and national night out. This team was Dedicated, Nurturing, and Altruistic!

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.script: This Minnesota team is having a great impact on its members, within its school and in the greater community. Being a student-led team, the members organize all activities, from writing grants to mentoring rookies. A major initiative for this team is to ensure their school provides an inclusive environment for everyone. They ran a Diversity in STEM fair in collaboration with other minority organizations within the school, to help address imbalances in the make-up of advanced engineering classes. Coming out of the pandemic they realized that, although their school district had FTC and FRC teams, there was little access to FIRST programs at the elementary level. As a result, they raised some money to start, support and guide 9 FLL teams, and held a practice FLL tournament for 72 teams. Growth of FIRST programs in their school district has been phenomenal. During Covid, the school district only had 32 FIRST team members. It now has around 450. The team pops up everywhere in its community, from weekly community events at a local cinema and leading a STEM exhibition at their annual city festival, to printing and donating over 3000 face shields and ear savers for healthcare workers. They donate 1500 hours of time each year to volunteering in their community. Please join us in congratulating this team that “Looks Inwards to Look Outwards.” In yellow and black, from East Ridge High School in Woodbury Minnesota, it’s the Errors, Team 3130.

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.script: Walk by their booth, and you’ll notice a pattern; This team enthusiastically welcomes you in. They have outreach events in grocery store aisles and frozen lakes, and a positive attitude in the stands and pit. This team provides a plaid display of enthusiasm and spirit for others to emulate.

records.eventName: Minnesota North Star Regional at La Crosse
records.script: This team has a student-led dedicated business team that accomplishes everything from communication to travel arrangements. They developed a pre-season game to build excitement throughout their school. If anyone tries to disparage FIRST, their Talons come out!
This team made the judges’ heads turn with their autonomous quick scoring. They can change their routines with the click of a mouse. They inspire us all with their cement mixer backbone.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's robot was purring like a kitten. They tackled the challenge with their grippy paws. They had tunnel vision for their goals.

This team almost exhausted a suite of analytical tools. They started with time over distance and carried on with spreadsheets. They concluded with a lightweight, fast, and very effective beast of a robot.

This team’s animal mascot is a rallying point. They’ve proven themselves to be screamingly good at outreach in their community. You won’t catch them “playing dead” when it comes to gracious professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team PACKED a centralized theme into their presence this season. Their theme qualified for a full overhaul, reaching their apparel, pit, and robot. The judges would like to wave this team in for a CHECKERED FLAG finish.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This Team’s serve drive helped them avoid CATASTROPHY by evading the competition. An elegant mix of cameras, accelerometers and beam breakers effectively swept game pieces across the field. Departing from their PVC roots, this aluminum robot impressed the judges with their balance between form and function

This team swerves along the path between the substations and the grid. At the push of a button, this Missouri team knows their cardinal directions. They galloped off the starting line in auton to get the “purple sugar cubes”.

The Judges are delighted to present this award for Inclusion in STEM. This GEM of a team cultivates relationships around the world. This inclusive team encourages any CAT to come and play. Robots come second to this team’s friendships.
This team’s robot looks like a sophisticated professional. Their well-built robot’s custom claw is on-target under pressure This boy-band doesn’t grind any gears.
This team isn’t afraid to think INSIDE the box A box they have sent all over the world. This team is MEGA inspirational

These BIRDS of a feather worked together with their local government officials, team sponsors and community partners to raise awareness of FIRST and STEM. Weaving the different strands of FIRST together, this team has launched many new, innovative programs assisting and enabling teams throughout the world. Extending the ROPE, they are working to create new teams across their state and help them SOAR to new heights. The judges couldn’t stop RAVEN about this team!
This new team’s future is bright. Maybe because their STEM kits are SOLAR POWERED. This international team has an international impact across 45 countries.
Our hopes for this team are as high as their team number, because their young members get so much hands-on experience. They may be CUBS but the have the hearts of lions!
These cats really roar. You can hear them in the stands and see them in their school and community. Hip hip hooray! Hip hip hoorah!
This team may be small, but they are mighty. They engaged their community to rally support. This APEX predator is here to stay.

This metal team impressed the judges with their autonomous prowess. Their reliable three piece auto and automated features throughout their robot helped them consistently perform on the field. Using their limelight for vision targeting has helped this team rock to the top of the ranking.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: On kickoff day, this group of students and mentors took a very creative approach to develop their game strategy and learn the ins-and-outs of what it meant to be a competitive force throughout the season. Becoming robots for the day and running a human simulation on their gym floor, this team was able to analyze the game pieces and get a good feel for how the game would flow. This BEARY special group of girls has been nothing short of amazing and impressed the judges with their creativity.

This team used a hot new process to develop a functional and practical element on their robot. They used finite element analysis to lighten an important subassembly while maintaining strength. Keeping the robot light allowed them to play Mach 5 with their hair on fire.

This team was a true ray of light in their community. Their efforts ran the spectrum from delivering flowers to nursing homes to pushing legislators to support STEM education. This team’s focus on outreach is a brilliant example of “Gracious Professionalism”.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Imagine this team coming from the mists of old England. Like a knight of old, this robot continues to compete. Not even a holy hand grenade can stop these killer bunnies.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team roared into the competition with a robot that was ready to rumble. They applied what they learned from previous years to ensure their robot was designed robustly from its arm to its swerve modules. This team’s efficient design has made major “sound waves” in the judging room.

This great team combined multiple elements to build great things including Java and Lava. Detecting tags and tape they can automatically place cubes and cones with the push of a button. You wouldn't expect such innovation from a process a old as combining wildfire and solid rock.

This small school developed their STEM program to fulfill their mission of educating others. Upon obtaining a large technology grant, this innovative group of students spread the wealth by funding multiple teams. This Cardinal team impressed the judges by insisting "We are better together" as "We play with robots".

Their robot knows where to go at the touch of a button. Their multi-pronged approach to design allows them to use both pneumatics and motors to pick up and deliver. The quality of this team’s robot makes them stand out like a stag in the wild.

This team leads the way with their outreach. They are involved at every level of the FIRST ecosystem, from hosting events to training mentors. The judges were impressed with this team's pack of 41 FLL teams.

With the use of summer camps, science activities, and working with younger FIRST students, this team of many colors set the bar high. Their efforts to impact both their local and FIRST communities are not just measured in their total number of events, but in the analytics they collect. Their pipeline strategy starts with the youngest students in FLL Discover and continues after graduation as they work to support alumni across the region to fulfill their mission of engineering engineers.

From the start, this team's goal extended far beyond the playing field. Whether it was to increase STEM participation in their school curriculum or gather sponsor support from their small, supportive community. This WILDLY impressive rookie team has been able to accomplish some great things so far this season.

Sporting the colors of royalty, this team brought their horns from the mountain. Led by their mascot and powered by fans, their spirit was unmatched from the top of the stands. This team's spirit is anything but sheepish.

This team used their quick reflexes to react to the rigid growth of their team. They use FTC and a junior varsity team to ensure their team’s knowledge will be passed down to new students. Planning for sustainable growth will surely help this team avoid “cat”-astrophe.

Many robots start on auto-pilot but not all are consistent on the field. Experience drove this team’s quick build and under control robot. Auto check the high box, this rambunctious robot balances every time.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team demonstrated phenomenal synergy between their components throughout the competition. On the field, they show their true colors with every move. Their robot’s defensive system protects their most valuable component, leaving no need for a guard dog.

Strategy emerged from a blank white board riddles with blue ink and produced a feline like claw for grabbing and placing game elements, “Their robot REAPS the rewards of their planning.” Their robot has the swerve and speed of a cheetah, but with blue shading.”

This team raced to help when it was called for. They were neighborly in helping others. Their paradigm is that the gracious professionalism banner hangs in a school but gracious professionalism lives on in everyone they touch.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team propels themselves into STEAM. They are a Launchpad for lifting off youth into the FIRST family. Their theme, team dynamics, and robot are out of this world.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team created a robot that exemplifies simplified and elegant industrial design. Their machine was well designed and the high quality fabrication had everyone’s eyes on it. Everyone was green with envy on how this robot looked and operated in the chaos on the game field.
This team’s controls are more than just push buttons and potentiometers to create great balance. Crank the controls to ELEVEN. They didn’t just RACHET, they rocked the LIME-LIGHT for great control.

This team and their robot continue to show great enthusiasm on and off the field. Adaptable and goal oriented, they will be a rising star within their community and FIRST family. We expect them to dance their way to new heights.

The judges recognized this team machined one clean machine! They’ve stayed reliable and on path with no need to swerve around the competition. With EVERY-BOT-Y hands on, this team is charged up to fly to MARS!

This Noble & Able team continues to grow exponentially by extending the FIRST community beyond their element. They continue to build diversity in communities’ that are under-represented, such as Neuro-Diverse students, and also grew the team to 50% girls with significant leadership representation. They came from the North to SHINE the BRIGHT LIGHT of FIRST across the globe.

This team strives for environmental sustainability of not only their team, but community and environment as well. Their annual FIRST summer STEM camp consistently converts campers to FIRST members. They’re a real BEAST when it comes to advocating with elected state officials for support of FIRST!!

As the sole rookie team at the St. Louis Regional, the Warsaw Wildbots competed effectively against peer teams at all experience levels. In the face of limited resources, their accomplishments serve as a real inspiration to all of us. We expect them to be a force to reckoned with in the future. The judges were so inspired by this team’s performance on and off the field; they were unanimously selected as ALL-STARS.

While their enthusiasm is extraordinary, it was their infectious spirit that caught the judges’ attention. While this team experienced great loss with the passing of their head coach, Dave Zilz, his legacy lives on in the passion and teamwork displayed within this team, and also throughout the entire St. Louis robotics community.

This team has a robust and well documented record of team and community events. This team engages with their sponsors, their local community and other teams at four dozen events a year. At its CORE this team has a solid team structure and organization that created a cohesive team atmosphere.
