records.script: This team had an electrifying performance that shocked the judges. Their use of odometry, filters, and sharing of code has them charging ahead of the competition. They are certainly the champions of the autonomous section.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team may be climbing to new heights, but they must stay grounded. When the incline is steep, they put their foot down. The well-engineered auxiliary wheels with air brake put their creativity score above the rest.

This hard-charging team rolls out as winners every time they enter the arena. Their innovative use of autonomous robotic coding, with a well thought out solid design and carbon fiber puts them heads and shoulders above the rest.
This team represents the building blocks of FIRST. They even wrote the book on gracious professionalism, with Woody Flowers as a basic element.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team really banded together and is as cool as ice cream. their imagery signifies a new beginning and is as sweet as vanilla, strawberry, and chocolate. Who knew wolverines ate Neapolitan ice cream?

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This incredible team never hides their fantastic capabilities and straightforward functional design. Not one to wander aimlessly...they take the field of play by storm...charting their way to victory.

The double gear drive mounted on the mast head of their bot allowed this team to move from the lower deck to new heights. This team has demonstrated the ability to go where no team has gone before. Their bulldog perseverance helped them drive to successfully innovate a better scoring method.

At FIRST, we know that this program is so much more than robots. This team showed that by going to a match with no robot at all. Their love and dedication to FIRST and STEM in general makes them deserving of this award.

This team's robot exhibits exquisite attention to detail from soup to NUTS. The talk story of their design focuses on solid performance in all aspects of the game. The judges get the feeling that good waves make for quality bots. Aloha to the winners of the Quality Award!

This team's robot is a direct reflection of their ability to revive classes in STEM. Their passion and commitment to education has assisted their diverse school in understanding STEM even when English is not their first language. This second year team will strike a balance to ensure that STEM remains a priority in their community.

The Las Vegas Regional Impact Award winner is a veteran team that continues the achievements of their excellent predecessors. Among their many accomplishments are providing outstanding community outreach with STEM classes including Girls Who Code, sponsoring electronic waste disposal and supporting other FIRST teams. They built sustainability by developing a foundation in FLL and building blocks in STEM education and FTC to create an outstanding FIRST structure.
As rookies, these predators kept their focus on the prize. With their commitment to tech, creativity, and strategy, they built a simple yet fast and functional robot. They must have bionic eyes!
This rookie team calls Nevada their home. With their stellar community support and outreach, they knocked out the competition. This team put the KO in cool!
This team knows the way to our hearts is through our stomachs. Singing their national anthem could LEAF anyone enamored. Such extraordinary team spirit could only be forged through dedication.

This team's recruiting and fundraising efforts have added up to create quite a diverse team. There are plenty of players to divide the work and set into motion a program that will sustain them in the future.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: This team's robot is capable of scoring blocks and cones and then parks on the charging station. Their sophisticated software uses reliable input sensors to allow the robot flawlessly operate autonomously. This school has a long history of science, mathematics, and technology.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: A truly unique intake mechanism that can both pickup and launch cubes or cones, it has proven highly effective and has served them well in competition, come sail away to a land of creative engineering and crazy hairdos. We graciously give the creativity award to The Mohawks, team #329.

There are two criteria to win this award. First, the team must be able to describe their engineering process clearly and succinctly. Second, the team mjust have a design that proves effective in the field of play. This team stood out in both criteria. They stuck their neck out and created a great robot.

This team is quick to deliver a spark among its community. They have generated a program that resulted in building a network of spare parts to be redistributed back to teams on Long Island. This team places the community first and may be in shock after we announce them as winner.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is ready to all outcomes even in case of a spill. Thier robot navigates obstacles and challenges with a happy face while the team cheers with grace.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This winning team impressed the judges with their attention to detail. Every component had a purpose and was colored to match the team's theme. Hofstra may be miles away from Sesame Street but we know where to find the Biggest Bird!

This team's robot easily picked up cones and sped to the high grids. Their control systems allowed the drivers to quickly park on the charge station. This team proved that the south will rise again. The judges debated over this decision while eating big plates over fried rice.

The judges were impressed by a team that bridges multiple schools to broadcast the message of FIRST. They build robots, mentor junior teams, and support their community in creative ways. With help from their sponsors they inject the magic of robots into their community and create real opportunities for growth and change. This team breaks down barriers like the warriors they are.
This team embodied the concept of KISS. With engineered failsafes and controllers to steamline their flight. The quality of their tech would even make Neil Armstrong jealous!

This team practices FIRST core values throughout the year. They actively organize community and international events to spread the word about STEAM. Watch as they fly off to rampage with the other teams.

This team wow’d the judges with the IMPACT they have made in spreading STEM to underserved communities. They have a Reach into both the local and global community. Many of their alumni return as mentors. The team has made connections across the globe to bring STEM Opportunities to those in other countries. The judges don’t want to “Change the Story” and can’t wait to hear the next chapters. Let’s give a loud ROAR and congratulate, Team number 1796 the RoboTigers, from Queens Technical High School.

This team worked tirelessly to bring people from different backgrounds together and to break down cultural barriers. This student-led team, comprised of members from many countries, chose to name themselves after the "root of unity" in mathematics, highlighting the value of inclusion that brought them together for this competition. Congratulations to team 9184, Zeta from Sevenoaks, UK.
This team was brave enough to host and mentor our youth. They impact hundreds by sucking them into their new world in FIRST. They certainly passed the test.
This team has unwavering team spirit and support from each other. They even developed an API that collects match stats as well as predicts matches. Win or lose, you could hear this team roar.

Demonstrating outstanding organization, this team has plans on plans on plans. From a deep recruiting funnel to their budgeting process to team communications, this group turns coordination into a superpower to advance the mission of FIRST. When it comes to sustaining their team, they hit it right on the dot - in particular a green dot sticker.

The first 15 seconds creates heroes. Those that can master binary ones and zeros. This team scores in the grid and demonstrates mobility. Their balancing act is also an impressive ability. They start tele-op with a million volts.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Tasked with coming up with innovative designs, this team understood the gravity of the situation. When an earlier design presented a risk, they pivoted to a creative solution. They put the clamps on cubes, cones, and their competition.

With a focus on design flaws early on This team’s multifunctional rollers left us in awe with their squishy stars and rotating claw They approach their engineering with the precision of a hawk and reached new heights with their carbon fiber arm.

This team’s reach has been felt across 3 continents. They have come together from many communities and the work they do brings together many more. Their passion for robotics and ethos of sharing helped establish multiple FRC teams. This golden team has personified Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Blue and Green lit up the scene All stars for their core values, energy and branding. Our hearts and minds you have tugged, Cheers to the super electrical plug!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team made all the other competitors green with envy. They custom designed and fabricated their parts to create a robot that was a terror in the jungle. From Long Island City, this robot was more mean than pretty, and STEAMed straight ahead to take home this award.

The end of the match is a great struggle. Lots of priorities to balance and juggle. It's an uphill battle and the challenge is to stay in place. This team can do it, but they have a backup just in case. Standing their ground with four pistons on the floor...

The judges want to recognize a team using their robot to put the unity in community They describe their team as family and go out of their way to create opportunity. These warriors, exemplifying robots building scholars, were on a mission to share their interests and skills outside the classroom.

A strong alloy and ally, this team was unstoppable and unbreakable as it soared to the top of the food chain. Their robust machine was designed to plow through the opponents defense without ruffling its feathers throughout the competition.

This team is perched to be a standout for years to come, impressing us with their elegant wire management, gear system, and pneumatics. Their fledgling outreach to their community has hatched support in STEM amongst politicians, including a congressman and a city council speaker. They even take international teams under their wings, incubating organizations in Poland, Netherlands, India, Guyana, and the Philippines. They ascended to new heights logging 1500 volunteer hours and supporting 4 FIRST related events this year.

Focused on creating safe spaces, We know this team is going places Using red hot flames to melt plastic parts, And helping the visually impaired won the judge’s hearts Bringing sustainable resources to help a new village grow, And teaching little kids all they know This team really hit the mark, Congratulations team 5665 Sparc

First of their kind They are not falling far behind Promoting women in STEM there is no end to what this team can do For diversity and your community you are the glue, which is why we see the future in you MecHack you can put this trophy on your rack

They may be new to FRC, but they know their way around NYC. Some say “where there’s a will there’s a way” and here’s the proof. Left without a mentor, funding, and few members, this team got back on track and steamed ahead. Energetic and diverse like its community, they inspire others today. We look forward to where this ride will take them next year!

We tip our hats to this enthusiastic team And although they lover their pajama pants, they certainly weren't sleeping in the stands. These maidens, with their social media saviness Continually exude their infectious spirit all year round with their TikToks that go viral through their school and beyond.

It's really exhilarating when 62.5% of your 16 mentors are Alumni. This team had detailed, documented approaches to fund raising, budgets, recruitment, project management, and quality control. New team members easily plug into their cohesive system for parts, planning, and problem solving. To the team that makes STEM fun for everyone.

(POEM) This team dominates the field, Because these warriors will not yield! In Auto why score one when you can score 2, And balance for the alliance crew! Their consistency has contributed to ranking points And this team livens up the joint!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: (POEM) This robot is very compelling Their main goal is often propelling You can’t hide From this team’s Falcon Pride

This team went from prototype to prototype so they can score from front to back. They ensured every voice was heard from over 100 students. Their engineering review board narrowed down their final design including a virtual sprocket….

Rumors of this team’s good deeds permutated the pits in 4 different ways. Prepared to help others Applying FIRST core values to community needs Witnessed by many other teams Sportsmanship like no other This team has the PAWS all over this award

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team and robot stand out in the field and in the pits. The robot is instantly identifiable by the legendary design. Their imagery is on fire, extending to a pit fitting to any dragon’s lair. You can recognize this team by their distinctive orange and black theme.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team has an outstanding form and function with a ton of artistic flare. With the ability to drive and pickup simultaneously, they scored with time to spare. Weather a cube of a cone, this devilish team performed with debonaire.

This innovation was so new the Judges had to use google to find out what it was. This team discovered how to incorporate AI into the design. They identified objects incorrectly at first, but trained the system to understand what is a cone and what is a cube. The team is planning to utilize the Google Cural to improve their autonomous for the season and future seasons.

With challenges a plenty during lockdown, this team found a way to spread the STEAM message throughout their community. Thousands of small STEM Packages were distributed thru libraries, recreation events and with food distributions reaching many.

This team spent long hours in CAD to get the perfect fit. They even took the time to polish their rivets and powder coat their chassis. From the “t” actuated trapdoor, down to the steel chassis for one of the lowest CG which results in the highest of quality all around.
This team supports the full breath of the FIRST Programs. They explain the Mystery of Science in whatever language you speak. This team will always show up in your community and never GHOST you…
Their advocacy is full STEAM ahead! 95 events is what they led! You can't camouflage their IMPACT They are team 1511 - Rolling Thunder

records.teamName: The Giant Diencephalic BrainSTEM Robotics Team

records.script: This veteran team like many is rebuilding. They are enthusiastic when explaining their build process, robot design and their FIRST experience. Most impressively they have their cheer game down. They cheer on partners, making a larger than life impact in the stands and on the field. You can identify this team by their bright pink outfits and their jubilance. They hail from Pittsford.
This team knows that reaching out to the community is vital. They also know that forging friendships with other teams is the best. This controlled “Mayhem” definitely sustain them in the future.

In autonomous mode, this team always reached for the highest level and found their balance. They demonstrated exceptional precision, accuracy, and consistency throughout the competition. We would give them an A++ for their efforts, but in their language, it would be C++. Congratulations to Team 4122, Ossining O-Bots.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Necessity is the parent of creative invention. This team molded their path to success one star at a time. These spin doctors racked up the points with their innovative design. GRRRREAT congratulations to Team 340, Greater Rochester Robotics.
This team’s robot always extends a hand. Their design efforts turned the tables, and their workmanship keeps things steady. Congratulations to Team 2791, Shaker Robotics.

This team exemplifies the core values of FIRST. Their attitude is extremely positive on and off the field. Collaboration is at the heart of this team’s ethos, assisting other teams at competition and in their home city. Congratulations to Team 4571, Rambots.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team displayed a theme that integrated robot appearance with team costumes. They spread the principles of FIRST, supplying treasures to elementary schools in their territory. This team roams the high seas of competition with flair and swash-buckling style. Congratulations to Team 578, Red Raider Robotics.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This award goes to a robot with a great silhouette. It is sleek, but you can’t see it in the dark. The judges thought their workmanship rocked! Congratulations to Team 144, The R.O.C.K.

This team took control to the highest levels. Innovative design was key to their success. With many views they can handle any ‘red hot’ situation on the field. Congratulations to Team 639, Code Red Robotics.

The judges were very impressed by the number of teams who do great work spreading the message of STEM and FIRST around the world. One team achieved measurable success by providing robot kits and coding lessons to young girls. They were sooooooooooooo impressive that they were recognized by the UN for their efforts in West Kenya. Congratulations to Team 6911, SO BOTZ of Orangeburg, NY.

From the start, this team took the time to develop and iterate on their design. Their intentional process was well documented and described. Their unique take on a virtual component led to a clean, robust, and functional system. The quality award goes to Team 20, The Rocketeers!

Whether at an FRC event or out in the community, this team makes connections with other teams through a strong emphasis on diversity. With many student-led activities, they create noise about the fun and impact of STEAM. Whether from the band shell or the Capital, their deadhead-inspired impact can be heard from miles away. The Engineering Inspiration Award goes to Team 1511, Rolling Thunder

Our Impact Award winner sparks innovation through their outreach and leadership. Their initiatives power the impact of FIRST in their region and beyond. Their leadership is electric, creating strong bonds with many BFFs. As the “joule” of their city, they build the future of FIRST. Congratulations to Team 4930, Electric Mayhem!

This team demonstrated the ultimate in community service. When a natural disaster occurred, this team stopped in the middle of build season to aid their fellow countrymen. Putting their rookie season on hold to help earthquake relief efforts is inspiring. Congratulations to Team 9099, ANKAROB.

This team took the concept of team spirit beyond the playing field. They became a family, making sure that everyone is connected and heard. By setting an example of year-long team spirit, they developed hearts as large as a dinosaur. The award goes to Team 333, MEGALODONS.

This team clearly understands the mission of FIRST. They created an extensive program across their community to recruit future members. Increasing team funding is their cup of tea. They broke the bubble and swooped down on their competition. Congratulations, Team 2601, Steel Hawks!

This team scores cones and blocks … with code like a flying fox This team is able to score points galore with their single arm core These wild horses are in a league of their own placing lots of cones in the zone Congratulations, Team number 2252 The Mavericks

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their creativity is always within an arm’s reach Robot elegance brought by human creativity and mimicry They have independent shoulder, wrist and elbow working in concert to create an elite symphony Reaching out from Warren Ohio Congratulations, Team number 48 Team ELITE

This lean green engineering machine put together a bot that can float like a featherweight, and sting with steel. Their design-ah, is so fine-ah, and has every gear and cable in a line-ah. Three cheers for the Steel Stingers of Medina! Congratulations team 2603 The Steel Stinger.

This team from the north helps Santa’s elves, making more than 400 toys for tots If your robot needs a little help, they will go to battle for you They are a mighty support in the pit, on the field and in life. Congratulations Team number 6421 The WarriorBots

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: There are many colors here at Buckeye Regional, and we know there are many shades of purple When the match is over, their competitors are in the dust bowl We can’t get the image out of our minds of them putting the squeeze on cubes making them WINE Congratulations, Team number 1551 Grapes of Wrath

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This beachcombing team buffaloed the field with their elegant and efficient design Their disciplined engineering process kept it simple, sleek, and quick by minimizing the number of moving parts and complexity The Bison lead the herd in Industrial Design Congratulations Team number 695 Bison Robotics

This team brings a touch of gold, with their innovation in control Their configurable drive control box will really knock your socks off This team really excites us, with their robot named Midas Congratulations Team 3201 Ross Rambotics

This team has battled for years to have a healthy robot in competition and this year everything came together The team scored highly with the judges in numerous categories while their robot also scored highly on the field This team really did gain the UPPER HAND at the Buckeye Regional. Congratulations Team number 6964 The Bear Bots

Their robot is simple, modular, and robust They paid attention to the details, like paint thickness, to design quality into their robot They say they have repairs and spares for everything that moves, but they hardly needed them They kept an eagle eye on quality Congratulations Team number 4028 The Beak Squad

Whether shooting for the stars at NASA events or sharing STEM across the world, this team zooms to promote FRC The ladies “tech” is so “lit”, their impact shines all the way to Africa Inspiring the next generation with their passion for girl-powered engineering, this team’s “magical” spirit is outstanding Congratulations Team number 2399 The Fighting Unicorns

This team has focused on consistent growth, which it has demonstrated through its feeder systems of FIRST Lego League and FIRST Tech Challenge teams. In fact, this team has a significant return of students in future seasons. This team’s commitment to STEM outreach, community involvement, and volunteer activities is unmatched. Founded in 2012, this 80-person team has assisted 5 FRC teams directly, has established 6 FRC team partnerships, and hosted off-season events for FIRST teams throughout the Midwest. Their generosity is highlighted with a fellow FRC team that was struggling to recover after the pandemic. This team provided countless hours of hands-on assistance, parts, mentoring, and even introduced the struggling team to sponsors and corporate suppliers in their network to help get them back on solid ground. Over the past year, this team hosted 40 community events, spreading the mission of FIRST, impacting 26,000 people and is increasing representation of women in STEM through its work with the Society of Women Engineers “SWEnext” project, and with the Girl Scouts. To top it all off, this team delivered 32 Lego kits to kids at Nationwide Children’s Hospital, and their work with Turn for Troops to create writing pens and deliver handwritten notes to veterans on Honor Flights has been regionally recognized. Congratulations etc.

With many teams under the sun, this one shines brightly among the stars A young rural team with a “based” design, who gathered a significant constellation of sponsors They have made one small step for FRC and one giant leap for STEM Congratulations Team number 9075 Lunar Robotics

This new team impressed with their intake They scaled up from tech, and strive to dominate The end of their story is yet to be told, because this team’s future is DIPPED IN GOLD Congratulation Team number 9194, 24 karat; KSS Robotics

Everyone sees this team’s spirit on the field and in the stands in the community, they share that FIRST spirit through working with Habitat for Humanity and the Robot in Three Day project. With those party hats they know that “robots just want to have fun” Congratulations Team 3324 The Metrobots

This student led team will go to the ends of the earth for sponsors With their heavy involvement in FIRST Lego League, they are granting access to STEM for years to come Recruiting and retaining members is easy as pie Congratulations, Team 3814 Pi Robotics

This team navigates their way through mountains that some would consider SMOKY. They have maximized 29 autonomous ways to determine their path and complete their journey. This team is KING of play, whether in the field or heading to PORT.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This little robot delighted the crowd with its UNIQUE approach to scoring. Despite their name, they don’t slip off the charge station! This crew catapulted themselves to winning the Creativity Award.

This team is HARD to beat. When implementing their swerve module, this team steered clear of RUBBLE. Through build logs and iterative design processes, they were able to choose SOLID components to make their design excellent! This team ROCKS!

This team is known near and far as the go-to team in their region for any assistance in all things FIRST. They empathize with the plight of small teams by providing their scouting data, lending tools and parts to competing teams, and even lent their easel to a competing team for a presentation! These giants are stronger than steel!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When it comes to having a charged up zeal...this team has major appeal! Their colorful pit and stellar bot really electrified their alliance partners and the judges. Spawning for the imagery award in 3...2...1...

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Soaring over the field, this team's design was impressive, and their feathers were never ruffled. Once their alliance landed, their unique kickstand helped their "flock" balance. Their low center of gravity did not prevent their industry-ready fabrication from flying high!

This team’s huge passion for innovation controlled their rise to the top! They were able to collaborate using the capabilities of two not-so-distant schools. Their unique control system incorporated Local AI and advanced imagery and data to let their robot rise the top of the hill!

This team demonstrated integrity by not locking the truth in a VAULT. Their Gracious Professionalism showed itself by righting a wrong and accepting responsibility when it might have been easy not to. This team values coopertition as opposed to confrontation as evidenced by their ability to successfully merge two teams.

This team's robot THUNDERS far across the PLAINS of gameplay to score with efficiency. The team doesn't lounge on the BEACH as they complete disciplined checks between matches to ensure that their robot remains robust. They are outstanding in their field with a machine as solid as a buffalo, but make no mistake -- this robot has the quality of a Bison.

This team and their accomplishments are out of this world, but they remain grounded in their commitment to engaging their community. From the valleys to the summits, they inspire students to experience STEM at all ages!

As Lady Gaga sings, "You are giving me a million reasons, about a million reasons." We are selecting this team and we bow down and say… This team helped grow the FIRST community and spread STEM by starting multiple teams and hosting and teaching at several events, engaging tens of thousands in the community and beyond through their outreach efforts, and maintaining strong partnerships with sponsors. This team has shown their metal to be flexible and resilient. The team has matured better than fine wine. The votes are in and the "Ayes" have it. In fact, all three. While BUILDING a lasting legacy where teams can focus on QUALITY over quantity, they make sure to honor their beloved late mentor, Paul George.

This is a team that really understands what FIRST is trying to accomplish, proving that technical stuff is fun, challenging, and offers a future. This team is already recruiting new members from their FTC program. In fact, 100% of their team members are former FTC and understand FIRST core values. This team "busts" the myth that small teams can't compete. Rising up from the ashes at the "speed of sound"....

The enthusiasm of this team caused them to be HIGHLIGHTED by the judges. This team swarms with enthusiasm as they spread the FIRST mission in the stands, the pit, and their community, With lungs of steel, the cheers of this team leave a mark!

This team’s passion for FIRST is evident. The judges agree: Robotics is “so much better than sports.” Their magical plan to recruit and maintain members, mentors, and sponsors has allowed them to diversify and grow. It is no myth that this team’s fighting spirit will sustain them for years to come!

This team was not MAY-HEMMED in by the chaos and confusion. THey determined with STEELY resolve to give their robot an edge without anyone at the controls. For consistently and reliably achieving points on its own,

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s robot is POULTRY in motion. Combining outstanding design and an EGGSPLOSION of creativity, they’ve worked around the CLUCK to build an im-PECK-able machine!

You may not see them coming, but you’ll know they’ve been there. Using a deliberate CAD-first approach, they stalked an elegant robust design with a bite. The award for Excellence in Engineering goes to these silent CATS
Like an ARTIST, this team creates a positive atmosphere both on and off the field. You can rely on this team if you ever lose your paddle while floating the river.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: As the sun sets across the Oklahoma Sky tonight, we are reminded of this team's exceptional visual integration from pit to machine. For this award, they are the absolute OMEGA.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.teamName: F. R. O. G. - FIRST Robotics Organization of Grove
records.script: This amphibian robot hops over the pond of competition!! Their un-FROG-gettable machine is elegance, efficient, practical and has made significant FROG-gress on the field of play. Give a loud croak for this team!
This team has shown us all that they are masters in the sea of mechanization. With precision and control, they sink their competition. All will fear when they release…THE KRAKEN!

This team embraces many aspects of robotics. Team members bring skills from various backgrounds such as Health, CAD Design, culinary arts, graphics design and more. They flew to new heights with recruiting and constantly gave a big ol’ nod to mentor Todd.
This team PURRS quality from the design process to on-field performance. Using a robust 4-bar arm, they C-the-PLUSSES in building the robot and team with this attribute as their guiding principle.

This newly-revived team is, FIRST-of-all, passionate.To them, outreach is a real big deal and they make sure museum-goers see their bot as they go by on their visits. Thousands of people think these POSSUMS are AWESOME ambassadors of FIRST.

And then there was one. A small team can have an oversized impact in the community if it has FAITH and a strong backing. This team has embraced the FIRST challenge of outreach and community involvement for many years by starting programs like: *Assisting start-ups of FRC teams locally and internationally *STEM day outreach for youth and seniors *Hosting in-season events for FLL and FTC and out-of-season for FRC teams *Producing supplies for first responders during the Covid emergency In addition, with the backing of one of their sponsors, they like to do events where there’s some TINKER-ing involved with their SPROCKETS.
This team embraces the latest Technology, but don’t get them confused with that other Institution from back East, as they’re definitely innovative in their own right.

This team has united their community and it shows with everything they do to help others out. This team drips enthusiasm through co-opertition in hosting bot-fests and supporting events both in and out of season. These Lions roar with love for others!

This small-town team has big dreams and a passion for crushing it. These sneaky panthers have clawed their way up the state capital to lobby for the future of STEM. They will leave their mark on the future of FIRST!
This team reaches for the sky when they code, and their programming was miles above the competition and never faltered. Their autonomous performance was simply divine!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team is on the right track and has a load of imagination. Their miniture control system may be small, but packs a big punch while reversing the design process to use natural hand motions. All aboard the Creativity Express!

When the season started this team put their thinking helmets on to set their goals. Using good engineering processes in their design kept them out of the dog-house. Redundancy is good when parked on a hill and you don't want to be knocked off the top!

These cats went out of their way hunting for teams to help throughout the pits. Stealthily donating an arm and autonomous code, they've assisted over a dozen teams throughout the competition. This team has soared graciously above the rest!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.teamName: F. R. O. G. - FIRST Robotics Organization of Grove
records.script: This team turns others GREEN with envy. They look good in any environment, and have the GOLD STARS in the grove!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team harnessed the power of the sun to help wanderers power their communication devices, and sent scouts on perilous missions to other coordinates beyond borders to spy on the "lesser beings". This team designed their own drives and boards to jump ahead of other teams in the race of design, and used Replicant technology to build multiple robots at different coordinates using long-range collaboration. Col. O'Neill would be proud of the work that this team has accomplished in creating their MALP.

With their custom controller and indicator, this team always stays cool under pressure by keeping the whole team informed of their robot's status. With the press of a button, their system can FUSE multiple inputs to forge a path to score. This team is a NUCLEAR powerhouse with a well designed control system!
It was always in the cards for this team. Their coordinated pit, robot and team uniforms were NO JOKE. Let's all go WILD for this team that the Judges deemed winners!

This team's robot design was top-notch, and their team management was simply SPIDER-RIFIC. With their quality control and attention to detail, this team spun a web of success that no other team could match. Though this team may be from the Down Under, their robot quality is sky-high!
This team has demonstrated a well oiled formula for success. Their team continues to UNITE students through FIRST across the globe, and this A-STEAM is an inspiration to all!

This team proves that you don't need an army to succeed and fly high. Indeed this team, despite its mighty accomplishments and successes, cannot fly at all. It's not a stretch, or a "STRITCH", to say that these ostriches are well deserving of this award!

This team rose to the top by quite literally building their robot by hand while graciously engaging peer teams in the pits. This global gold medal team knows how to improvise, adapt and overcome...even with governmental bureaucracy. This team has proven and exemplified the spirit of gracious professionalism, patience and Caribbean culture as they brought honor to their country!

This team comes from a place where the kids still respect the college dean. This team and their energy proves that while football is the roughest sport on campus, robots are cool too. While many on this team wear boots, they are very proud to be Okies from Muskogee!

This team is enthusiastic about spreading the spirit of FIRST throughout the world. Promoting STEM from kids to seniors, this team has impacted hundreds of people throughout their community. This team's enthusiasm and teamwork is critical to the chain of success in promoting FIRST core values!

This team is by no means GREEN at their approach to sustaining success in FIRST. From the network of Alumni across two states, to their unique approach in promoting science and technology in their community, this team has a solid plan for recruiting and retaining students and mentors alike. This HEAVY METAL team constantly keeps its eyes on suststainability!

records.script: This team’s telescoping arm reaches for the moon. The consistent operation of the drivetrain positions them for success. In theory we need drivers, but in autonomous, this robot is in control.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their colony of motors expertly navigates cones, cubes, and charge pads. The unique mix of swerve drives balances functionality and creativity. DAM <pause>, this team can chew through this year’s competition.

This team heats up their community with knowledge. We’re red with excitement over all of the STEM and FIRST appreciation that they’re spreading. To celebrate their hard work at CNE, we are declaring today a Devil Day.

This small but mighty team has weaved an authentic story. Their vision seamlessly integrates FIRST principles with environmental sustainability. This green focused team certainly puts the pedal to the metal to make their Impact.

The reach of their engineering process and design captivates any audience. The judges learned about this season’s continuous improvements and saw multiple green lights. Reaching the top of the ranking is easy for this long-necked robot.

This team was tied up endlessly helping others. While other teams were worried about crossed wires, this team was worried about crossed knots. This year’s award goes to the green team with the running pit crew!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team of fighters use their image for good in supporting rookie teams. We became aware of their presence by an image, and a robot, that belong to no other number. This team looked so good, the judges were worried that they were about to be carried off to Odin’s halls.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Their elegant CAD design was core to the team’s success. The robot always has its precise bearing with accurate control. Its incredible arm can easily pick all the apples in the orchard.

This team drove their robot to collect a large number of Pylons. Through a variety of sensors assisting the driver they Stressed Out their competition. Their robot can see, feel, and hear the arena, stopping them from getting a Blurry Face, and They Don’t Care What You Think.

This team demonstrated their tenacity by rising from the ashes of COVID. Through the active involvement of their entire STEM community, this teams gets things done while inspiring the message of FIRST. They floored us with their impressive girl power.

This team has taken quality to a new telescopic level. The combination of water jets, CNC, and 3D printing for fabrication shows in the individual parts and assembly of their robot. Because of their fabrication process, this team will keep butting heads, with quality improvement as a central theme to their many subsystems.

This team demonstrated great spirit by growing fast and working in a pack. Despite late funding, they sled into the competition with a strong will. Filled with enthusiasm and great defensive play, it’s Huskies all the way!

This team took inclusion and diversity to a global level with representation from 5 countries. They showed how effective recruitment is critical for success and growth of STEM. We are glad to see this 3D-printing club transformed into a competitive FRC team.
The deafening cheers of this team could be heard all over campus. When it came to their spirit and passion, this team didn’t horse around. These Greek warriors surprised us with their enthusiasm.

These knights in sustainable armor are crusading the way to equality in STEM. Empowering their community, and assisting all corners, all while ensuring that the next generation of squires is adequately armored. FIRST sets the bar pretty high, but they just keep giving more, more, and more.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: This team has a well-balanced autonomous mode that can be a ray of sunshine in their alliance. This team can pull a different solution out of their drawer for each situation. Their robot not only looks good on the field, but it can storm through the competition like a raider.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team charged up with green energy to take their creativity in any direction. When placed in a dark situation, they can rely on their solution to not screw up. These knights found an innovative solution to control the kinetics of their game.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: This team is a cut above the rest in their robot build with design and in-house machining. From a long line of winners, this team really has a plan to grow, inspire and recruit the best members. Despite their mascot, this team doesn’t play in the shadows.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: This team has actively supported other robotics teams in their community. When people could not meet inside, they took outreach to the sidewalks. Their colours make you think of sunshine on a rainy day.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: There is nothing contradictory about this team’s excellence. Their advanced skills included simulation and prototyping, resulting in an elegant design. A thorough engineering design process put a wrench in their competition.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: This team always makes room for others, willing to collaborate for the good of all. When other robots find themselves homeless or needing space to grow, the gears of FIRST core values start to turn. With fairness in their hearts, this team shares their bounty.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team caught the judges’ eye with effective aesthetics throughout the competition. Their headgear and signature colour pack a visual sting. It is incredible to see the purple Pokémon “Skorupi” on the field.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team shook the ground but remained stable with each challenge. Elegance was observed in the entire robot, from their multi-axis arm to the gripper. It successfully strikes a balance between functional design and robustness despite their 5th wheel.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: This team was able to overcome the task of controlling their robot without shortcircuiting. Through innovative programming, they were able to decrease cycle time and score points at the push of a button. The robot zips around the field with the best controls of any of the Daves we know.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: This team is passionate about engaging women and younger generations in STEM. Emphasizing quality over quantity, they put a fun spin on a competitive competition. They might be logical, but they will make you Laugh Out Loud.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: This team demonstrated solid construction with exceptional attention to detail. Cutting-edge technologies and innovative features were combined with aesthetic cable wiring. Their design stemmed from various branches of prototypes, resulting in a robot as robust as an oak tree.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: This team made a lot out of a little and more is on the horizon. When they returned from Shad Valley they roared and the pride answered. They may be new, but their pit was more popular than a watering hole on the savannah.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: You can see this team’s well documented journey from little Lego pups to new dogs on the field. They actively sought to better themselves, their team, and prepare the next generation of engineers. After their “best in show” performance, they didn’t just sit pretty, but continued to earn treats from sponsors.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: Every member of this team showed energy that spread like wildfire. After a full restart, this herd emerged unified with a new spirit. The food might have shown up cold, but the team has shown up hot.

records.eventName: ONT District Western University Engineering Event
records.script: This team has figured out how to transfer their knowledge to younger players. They are not afraid to leave their comfort zone. With their plans and practices in place, this team will not strike out anytime soon.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation

Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
