records.script: This team's robot knows its place. Their control was actively aware and updating without user input to ensure their accurate location on the field. Today we will always remember the "titans".

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team recognizes that their robot would not always be dealing with ideal situations. They came up with a unique solution to account for those cones that don't want to be picked up. Don't get caught with your cones laying around with this bot in sight.

This team focuses on "maximizing" outreach in their community. This year, by working directly with teachers and principals, they created an impressive academy for younger students, which incorporated building simple machines into the school curriculum. This team takes technology to the "max" in their community!

This team reached out to over 60 thousand people over the past 3 years. They conducted over 70 outreach events. They "plowed" their way through to rural communities, influencing over 10 thousand. They "merged" their impact across all three levels of FIRST Robotics.

This team zoomed to the forefront of consideration for this award. The way they executed and strategically swerved and adapted to any position of the game pieces set them apart. They demonstrated great CONTROL, and ALTernative approach to play and DELETEd any doubt.

Despite not having a school this year to meet and build in, this team still worked together to be a pillar in their community. They spent many "hours of code" with elementary students. Their outreach is as prominent and apparent as a constellation in the sky.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Other teams may barely notice their license plate number and those big friendly eyes. This team knows how to come out of a long winter hibernation and stand out from the crowd.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team is "Wild About Form Function Layout Elegance and Style". They focused on how efficiency, simplicity, and design can make a successful robot. Fasten your orange belts.

A good control system is like a "handshake" between a computer and a human operator. Not "every bot" has innovated to double up controls and flip your perspective. The advanced control system this team developed was definitely not "worked from iron".

This team demonstrates a safety-first mentality from pit, to people, to the playing field. Their consistency and reliability were noticed by judges and event volunteers alike. You would have to be "Raven"-mad to miss their team spirit.

Robustness starts with a solid frame. This team's cable management and double-lifting mechanisms stood out "brightly". This team "highlighted" an approach to quality that would make professionals "green" with envy.
Their stories are full of passion and inspiration. Thanks to this team, we all understand the importance of "water". When this team "surfaced", their cheers complemented their robot's bite.

This team is flying over the neighborhood looking for team members and sponsors. Through good communication and hands-on training, nobody is left behind. With a raptor-like focus, they are building a sustainable nest for the future.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: This team’s robot, with its autonomous cone and cube handling, is capable of reading QR tags and placing the pieces Just Right. This team overcame its biggest challenge of handing off its play pieces. Working as a team with over 50 students, the Robotics room is better known as Mr Samaroo’s room.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team was able to explain and impress the judges with their creative design process from concept to completion. Always eager to innovate with new ideas, these busy beavers creatively crafted a new power hungry swerve drive.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: Reaching out to the community from grade one up, spreading good will for STEM impressed all of our judges. Safety manuals, process diagrams, and checklist for you and me, oh my!

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: Making an impact with FIRST can be about assembling all the right pieces. This team works hard to make sure no pieces are missing from FIRST. Lots of community building buttoned up the win for this team.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: This team’s claw can do it all!! It can pick the cones and cubes and perfectly place them every time. A ton of engineering technologies are used behind the scenes. Lidar for navigation, Image processing, algorithms running on Raspberry Pi with intense mathematical calculations, and actuated with pneumatics, cables and onboard motors – well orchestrated for the game play at the field.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: Lending a helping hand to a team in need is a gracious and selfless act. Judges noticed and respected one team who helps many others with their “Fix-it” attitude. Their approach is a key contributor to a symbiotic relationship.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is green and can be seen. They sit at the round table with their peers, while their robot moves silky smooth, ascending the field to take the throne as the great one.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s clean, simple, and reliable design starts with the arm and the gripper, then ends with the drivetrain. This team’s robot echoes its namesake, as one of Canada’s toughest flying aces.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: This team’s robot, when retracted, maintains a low center of gravity, allowing for very stable mobility around the field. Their cascade elevator design executes accurately and consistently, with top shelf placement of cones or cubes. Their consistency in their robot control made the opposing alliances green with envy.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: This tiny team showed perseverance and resilience in overcoming challenges in the heart of competition by rebuilding a major component of their robot, resulting in a better design than ever! This team did not give up, brainstormed together, and showed their fighting spirit by delivering an orange wave to the arena. For the judges award for persistence and innovation under pressure...

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: The judges found the winning team’s robot to have an exceptionally clean design with a functional and robust gripper. The members of this team are Rebels WITH a cause - QUALITY.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: This team came prepared with strategies, business plans, and passion from a team of STEM explorers from all around the world. They shared a tremendous vision of building FIRST and STEM communities locally as well as overseas. The judges believe this capable, committed and collegial team will charge up the FIRST rankings for many years to come.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: Starting with a blast, this team effectively recruited members, engaged with their community, and designed a competitive robot, all within a few short months. By running coding events for younger girls in their area, they proved that they won’t leave anyone marooned. Out of the ashes, this team has shown they can rise to the ethos of FIRST robotics.

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: You win some matches. You lose some matches. This team has the vision to do better each time. Always keeping their schoolmates south of the border up-to-date, even when they’re cheering from a distance…

records.eventName: ONT District University of Waterloo Event
records.script: Masterminds on this team have implemented a tremendous framework to build and operate their team over many generations. Tool trainings, team dinners, video tutorials, templates for wiring, sharing tips and tricks, terrific! Like the giants of old, beyond a doubt, this team proved they will be able to sustain far into the future.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.script: This team is a neck above the competition. Zipping ahead of the teams before anyone could touch their controllers. An automatic choice for the autonomous award! Congratulations, Team number 4678, CyberCavs!

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team was wired and provided a strong footing when securing their position on the charging station. The wild nature of this cat anchored their honour of creativity. Congratulations, Team 5885!

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.script: This team is used to breaking barriers working in their community to recruit new members in STEM programs through coding events and shrek the halls at Christmas. Ushering a new DAUN for engineering inspiration. Congratulations, Team number 4617, DAUN!

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.script: They code, they build, they program with care Their robot comes alive, they’ll take it anywhere They’re the STEAM team, they inspire Rebooting, rebuilding, they take it higher This team’s got the skills to make the bots greater They’re robotics masterminds, you could call them a raider Congratulations, team 5024, Raider Robotics!

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.script: This team wasn’t horsing around with their unique and effective intake design. Their out of the box frame design left their stamp on the competition. Stepping into the limelight for the excellence in engineering award with no plans to leave is team 4907, Thunderstamps!

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.script: Although they wanted to take a bite out of the competition, when teams were hungry for help they always delivered. Unlike their prehistoric mascot, this team has stood the test of time. Congratulations, Team number 772 Sabre Bytes Robotics!

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From their team to their robot into the stands they are full of “green” energy and enthusiasm. Don’t be green with envy! Congratulations, Team number 4920, Bell River Boltheads!

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team managed to corral all the elements of an effective design and it showed both on and off the field. They certainly gave the judges a bit of a neigh-sayer moment, but in the end, we couldn't resist the robot's unique charm. With its sturdy build and clever design, it's no wonder Vincent Massey 4903 galloped away with the industrial design award!

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.script: They are a “ruff” competitor that are in “charge” of the field. Their Innovative double pick control put them ahead of the pack. The ability to switch directions like a flick of the tail make this top dog a special breed. Congratulations, Team number 4946, the Alpha Dogs!

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.script: This team is anything but lost. In the last year they grew very quickly, but they are by no means a weed. They’ve inspired the judges to win their award! Congratulations, Team number 8789, The lost 10mm sockets!

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.script: This lightning-fast team impressed the judges with their risk mitigation measures using CAD modelling. They received a “10 out of 10” for their use of 3D printing and extensive spare parts list. Clear the runway; coming in hot for the quality award is team 8081, UMEI Lightning Robotics!

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.script: In the field of metal and wire, their heart shined through. They established family bonds and persevered through challenges. They shifted our paradigm on team spirit. Congratulations, Team number 2198, Paradigm Shift Robotics.

records.eventName: ONT District Windsor Essex Great Lakes Event
records.script: With infinite choices of strengths, they chose three. Organization, Structure, and Methods are three sides of their form. This triangle of strengths will help them with rebuilding a program for “absolute” sustainability. Congratulations, Team number 4308, Absolute Robotics!
Hailing from central Oregon, With a mind of its own. This bot asserted itself by scoring anonymously from every position Leading their alliance to SERT’n victory.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: While you may expect them to clawfor the cubes, Their creative plan shows that’s not what they choose, They use sticky hands to grab onto cones These cans solve the puzzle with a method of their own
This team knows how to PULL THEM IN to STEM programs from all over their community RESISTANCE IS FUTILE.

Impact award winners need to impact a broad swath of their community; Letting the FIRST culture inspire many different groups of people. This team’s annex may be gone, but they are driving all over their community.

This team CONSISTENTLY raced across the field scoring Points for their alliance. Low center of gravity and precise scoring lead their alliance to VICTORY. Out of the VALLEY comes this elegantly designed robot.

This team has gone to the sky and above to support all teams this weekend’s teams by weaving a net of volunteers and resources to enable a successful event. We thank them and their school community for being sky high hosts.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Their mascot is purple with ears. Consistent imagery is outfit, machine and pit. They are surely memorable not just for the squeak.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With their hot organized pit, which is simple yet elegantly designed. They are “WELL POACHED” in all categories with their multifunctonal 3D printed brackets. With thoughtful design intention from beak to block, this team had a well organized robot, with good cable-management proving to be “bug-less”. From lucky talons to sleak LED wings, they are surely to be the Industrial Design leaders in Flght or Grounded throughout life.
This team’s single button control activates deadly aim and comes when just meters away from the goal! Their control schematic confirms their intent to never miss in cone/cube placement!

The Judges call this the “All Around Award.” This team has grown an army of FLL teams. They’ve endured their robot with a mixed media of parts from plastic to metal to wood and they sparked a robotics Revolution in Turkey
This team build a robot that will hold up to anything mother nature can throw at it. It featured clean, well-crafted elements to weather the rigors of the competition.
When we see this team raise their flag Their siren screams lure us all IN It’s hard to not get caught in their NETS
This team has made giant strides in a very short period of time. Their outreach program is second to none. Though their identity is 2B Determined, their ongoing influence is certain.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.script: At the speed of light generated by focused electrons, this bot leveraged April tags to precisely navigate in autonomous mode at extreme speeds capturing points. LED communications, NASA quality software, and expert machine construction were the product of a team with a plan. There were zero errors in this code folks. Get Charged Up with the success of our winner.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's robot boasts a truly creative arm mechanism that impressed us all. With a little bit of twist and a flick of the wrist, this team demonstrated unique creative control that set them apart. With their innovative use of controls and filament, this colony truly created a metal work of art

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.script: This team emerged from the depths in service of those historically "loched" out of robotics We all agree, they've earned *credit* for their extensive outreach across the pond to communities underrepresented in STEM Their monster dedication has earned them the Engineering Inspiration award

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.script: It took a SWARM of MEAN MONSTERS to decide on the FAVORITE for the Impact Award. There were FLYING and FLAMING SPARTANS, CRUSADING through the VALLEY to deliver the decision. And when the STORM had cleared, the winner was still 2B DETERMINED.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.script: They get the RHYTHM of rapid design and don't miss a BEAT with their documentation to the nines. A pipeline for prototyping and communication line, from design through conception, they leave nothing behind........ Especially not their BETA testing.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.script: This team was flying around helping other teams They helped turn down the heat of competition by sharing tools and expertise They are no chickens when it comes to gracious professionalism

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's got ALL the right angles. Taping off the competition from the pits to the stands to the field of play. They've been under construction since 2004, constantly developing their Conrad...pause for effect.....the cone crusher

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team has created a robot that combines efficiency, versatility, and flexibility with expert precision. Their robot's arm moves like a dream, seamlessly transferring cones from the ground to the nodes. With its explosive gearboxes and intricate joints, this robot is one mean machine.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.script: You might recognize this team for their unique echelon assault For brigading a path across the field, planned, programmed and executed at the drop of a cone This team ranked above the rest with little recon to achieve the award for innovation in control

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.script: Dwelling along the Willamette, this team really impressed the judges. They are slashing through diversity to reach out to more of their community. If your robot can speak two languages, porque no los dos. For winning the Dual Immersion Award.....

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.script: When you seek a robot with robust design concept and fabrication, look no further than this team’s bot! They recognized a potential weak point in their robot and used risk mitigation in their design process to allow lesser parts to fail in order to protect the essential rest of the robot! Their entire robot, named after Apophis, the Egyptian God of Chaos, demonstrates exceptional quality in design and workmanship!

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.teamName: SWARM - South and West Albany Robotics Maniacs
records.script: This team takes flight when disturbed. Buzzing around the competition lifting the spirits of their partners. They made this competition a hive away from home.

records.eventName: PNW District Oregon State Fairgrounds Event
records.script: When adversity swells, this team examines its strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats. With Armstrong budgeting and captains training captains, this team turns dark skies blue. Weathering the storm, this team maintains a sustainable future.
This team’s supreme efforts resulted in a perfected recipe for autonomous. Leaving their community behind, they reliably found balance on the charge station after putting their biscuit in the basket.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Others may error when trying to decide between cones or cubes, but this team’s LED signal is sure to be copied. Gracious host and fierce competitor, the creativity award goes to….
They have reached beyond their boundaries to inspire future engineers. This enables their own growth in the field and makes them role models.

From the wilds of the great white north; to the chaos in our halls of democracy; with links to the middle east, Washington and Oregon we’ve searched high and low for the best. And now, we’re no longer meanly hedging our bets, rather we’re burning to swarm our favorite teams with love and adulation. Alas, we can’t, for in the end it’s Confidential.
This team has the design process down in a most shocking way! Clarity in their design process has quantified a tsunami of organizational ideas!
From grammar school through high school this team executes and demonstrates the principals of FIRST throughout their full community.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Without them, the stands would feel bare. Hats off to this team for roaring into the arena with ursine spirit.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Commander of cones and cubes with their tactical design you might miss them as they speed by. Form, function, and aesthetics, this robot certainly stands out in General.
This team’s custom presets make scoring a breeze. They like to Bend the STREAM of Innovation to Control their robot.

We the judges are calling this award “True Grit”. With an all rookie team and rookie mentors they rose above this years challenge. Though their flock is small they can say this award all “Mine, Mine, Mine”!
Like the spring that controls their arm cables, this team is a constant force in PNW robotics. A few broken eggs didn’t stop this team’s robust design from catching fire at Wilsonville.
This team’s friendly spirit resonates with everyone in the vicinity. The strength of their community will hold even through the dog days of summer. Have you seen this dog? You have now!
Friend to many, place for all, sharing not just a “means” to an end. Just ask and you will get an invite to your field away from home.
Their persistent precision during the autonomous period got them noticed. Their balancing act was something dramatic. Our furry friends from down under are out hopping their competition.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: While they spread way out in their community build space, they coded their arm to automatically retract. While we tend to stay away from labels, this team used their label makers to make people laugh. This highly effective catchers mitt, definitely caught this competition off guard.

This team communicates the mission of FIRST through their STEM outreach with FTC and FLL feeder programs. They provide a culture of inspiring the next generation of STEM and engineering professionals by sponsoring boot camps, demos, a brunch and many other activities in their school and community. Their more than 25 year “crusade” to spread the word of FIRST goes beyond the success of their robot and is exceeded by the accomplishments of their students and Alumni!

This team made multiple quests to impact not only their community but people worldwide. Qualifiers and practice events, teaching events and outreach devices, this team does it all. They may be a small team, but their impact is definitely… out of this world.

Like the extension of an arm, they reached their way to the top of the rankings. This team possesses a wildlife essence that resembles a raven, mustang, or goose. The excellence of their robot certainly helped them Stomp their competition like a moose.

For putting the needs of your fellow competitor in front of yours. For jumping in, helping out, and dropping everything to make sure that this other team was able to participate this weekend. You demonstrated to the core what Gracious Professionalism is all about by ensuring Team 8721 could quickly compete.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team heightened design choices to incorporate natural elements. Their imagery extends into the team, fans, and even competitors! You may think they’re goofy, but the judges think they’re GOOSEY. HONK HONK HONK

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team loves to fail fast, learn and iterate. Their strong designs struggled at their first event and they got right to work on the design process, as soon as the drive home. They came into Bensalem with robust and elegant improvements, bringing on effective design together and scoring with a real Robo-force.
This team’s iconic control helped to reduce the stress on their driver. Their push button solution for quick decisions. This stream deck does not let them blend into the background.

Being from the Jersey Shore, they know a sea sponge can soak up 20 times their weight. This team used every opportunity to learn and soak up as much knowledge as they could about FIRST Neither wind, nor rain, nor hail, nor a tornado will knock them down or out of the competition. The Judges Award for the Little engine that could goes to team 8721 DAIS NAID
Their robot is not a federally protected foul A centrally pivoting arm exhibits balance and poise This herd of impetuous ponies exhibit professional engineering pride.

This Rookie team has a growth and business plan that engages their school community with strong parental support, a STEM class, and robotics summer camp. They DOMINATE the competition on and off the field. It’s clear that with their PATH to success they will THRIVE and participate in FIRST into the future.

This budding team faced many challenges but did not let it get them down. Despite hardships, they have continued to be advocates for STEM and FIRST in their school. This team ‘Rose” to the occasion and their perseverance never wilted.
This small team has BIG ENERGY! They gave the competition a JOLT of positivity with their ELECTRIC outlook. They flew in and stole all the THUNDER with their amazing attitude.

This team thrives on their pipeline of new members through FLL and hosting an FLL Qualifier event annually. Their approach to fundraising is clever and follows a trail of 1000 chicken nuggets; acknowledging their sponsers and alumni. In addition to being “Chippy” these Nordic adventurers are sustaining themselves with an aggressive plan to keep their mission of FIRST and survive for many years to come.

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.script: This robot’s autonomous code allows it to balance like an eagle on a branch. Their GitLab organization was simply electric, allowing no bug to escape their talons. Even Chicago winds couldn’t blow their robot off course.

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team could come at a problem from any angle and set themselves up for success. They really set their hooks into the challenge with a novel solution that enabled them to fly through the course. Their success in autonomous and teleoperated was embedded in their circuits.

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.script: This team started this year’s efforts by implementing an “end-to-end” engineering evaluation and “modular prototyping” processes which is odd since they do not seem to “have a cause”. Their defiant nature was shown in how they accepted input and ideas from all students before a design began. Design revisions continued through the season resulting in a highly competitive, modular system. These “rebels” have really “stuck their necks out” to achieve Engineering Excellence.

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.script: Many competitors went out of their way to nominate this proactive team for gracious professionalism. Their entire team seeks out those in need both during the build season and at all of their events to make sure everyone is ready for competition. Much like their namesake, their strong values shine through including a person who stayed late hand-sewing with style, aka the “Bumper Queen”

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.teamName: The Giant Diencephalic BrainSTEM Robotics Team

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team made it to the big dance for the Imagery Award. They’re from rural Pennsylvania and maintained their imagery both on and off the field. Easily one of the most recognizable robots on the field - they continue punching even after the dance is done!

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's robot has a robust design with a low center of gravity They incorporated an impressive array of actuation in their shoulder, elbow, wrist, and finger joints. The judges were green with envy over their three-fingered gripper

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.script: This robot’s trajectory tracking control ensures it can always connect the dots. This team’s unique alert system was absolutely riveting! Their pastel-encoded simulation ensured they could fix the robot before bed time!

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.script: This team stood out to the judges for their unique inspiration and impact both inside and outside their community. They utilized their robotics skills on and off the field. This team reached out locally and globally touched hearts everywhere. They will be sailing to Ecuador to deliver a custom-made & 3D printed hand.

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.script: From their herringbone gears to their use of inverse kinematics and law of cosines mating with the integration of hardware & software allowing this team to produce a reliable and efficient robot. From the town who says, “Ask the man who owns one.” Packard Auto, Warren, Ohio.

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.script: This volunteering-focused team conducts donation drives and a variety of workshops with the most impactful being business, project management, and finance. They have formed several FLL teams and impacted many more through their longest running FLL regional. Their YouTube and Discord community is not cheesy but promotes the essence of their FIRST mission – coopertition.

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.script: In January, this team made sure everyone was ready to kick-off the season in the right direction. Over the course of the year, they offered workshop such as CAD, manufacturing demos, and coding, leading to other teams winning awards. Working with local partners, they raised money for a toy drive to benefit children at a local hospital and were even featured on Telemundo. From the Southern Coast to Kenya, this team advocates for funding for mentors, teachers, and students alike in spreading the message of FIRST. Using their Magnetic personality, this team blasted off into space while ramming through obstacles near and far.

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.script: This new team has already found sponsors and started recruiting for next year. When their robot was getting pushed around, they hit the weight room to bulk up. This school club was so happy to find a warm FIRST welcome, that they didn’t sting.

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.script: The Case for this team is that with limited resources, they have demonstrated remarkable ingenuity to build a competitive, 100% student-built robot. They were inspired to elevate robotics to meet the sport requirement in their school activities. Oh and they traveled to Pennsylvania from the West!

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.script: This team's number was on the prowl around the field. Their enthusiasm could be heard from their shouts in the stands to their partnership in the Pitts. Their team spirit shines bright pink in the FIRST community.

records.eventName: Greater Pittsburgh Regional presented by Argo AI
records.teamName: The Giant Diencephalic BrainSTEM Robotics Team
records.script: Designing a sustainable program is like building a backronym, it takes a clear purpose and attention to detail. Growing it requires inspiration, advanced networking, transferring knowledge, and a lot of hard volunteering. Between their relentless connection-building and their FLL Regional Grand Championship, this team really connects their ideas to their actions.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: This team’s automated arm has moved them up the ranks. It’s balance system lights up the field in an array of colors. This team is always on the hunt.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team showed the judges innovative new uses for string. Pulling the strings taught help both their arm and these pioneering technicians reach high.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: They promote STEM in their diverse team family and they advocate in their county and beyond. They spell out their values and spread them far and wide. We all agree that when it comes to STEM, we want SOUP everywhere!

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: For this award, we focus on the last THREE years of accomplishments. This team identified geographic proximity and scheduling conflicts as the TWO major barriers of getting students to the Events. This title ONE school blew the judges away!

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: This team’s process is quite robust. Iteration has made them upper crust. Their consistent performance is almost crazy. Congratulations team 314, Miss Daisy!

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: This team is there when you need them They’ve got the tools, the skills and the heart. They wear a LOT of hats.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team shows off FIRST values within their pit and within themselves. They each are atoms, special alone, but through their bonds have formed something powerful. They sound demonic, however they’re anything but.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team, a strong flock constantly iterates their design to be better. This year, they soared, swerved and swooped in the pits to make fixes in 8 bolts or less. This team is FLYYYYYYYY

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: With a dominating yellow presence, this team commands control. With their high speeds, agility and precise intake, they made their competitors quake. This team efficiently sabotaged the playing field.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: They are small but mighty on the field and off. They may keep you scoring but you won’t mind because they are nice and so happy to be here. We were impressed by their energy and especially their gracious defense! The judges award for gracious defense goes to Team 9014, Vulcan Mechanics

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: Sometimes you succeed and sometimes you fall. This team’s designers answered the call. Springing forward and standing tall.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: Before this team ever stepped onto the field, they took it upon themselves to create an FLL team. They powered through their successes (PAUSE) and their FAULTS to stand out in their first competition. This team will make the rivals ground Quake in fear in the future to come.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: With a commitment to inclusivity, this team has made an impact. Crashing a gala helped fund their mission Their “Never a Closed Door” policy is helping their team and Community grow.

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: This team has awesome synergy. Their positive energy is contagious. Everyone feels the CHARGE from Team 2722

records.eventName: FMA District Springside Chestnut Hill Academy Event
records.script: This team makes sure their expertise will be top notch for years to come. They teach each other in after school classes, document and test qualifications, and the structure pays off! Wrap your heads around a team that has geared their future to come.

This team used a robust camera system to autonomously navigate and score during both autonomous and teleoperated play. GATHERING data throughout the season allowed them to refine and filter their controls algorihms, interpreting information from 3 cameras at SONIC speed.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Bear with us now, as we share this great news, This team’s robot had a wedge that just couldn’t lose. Their BEAR CLAW was fierce, their approach so clever, In a game of inches, they were as precise as ever. For their innovative style, we must give them their due, The Creativity Award goes to Team 46 82.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award

records.script: This team impressed the judges with a creative focus on their unique game strategy and match simulation, which drove their design process. Their miniscule drive base and efficient game piece transportation makes this robot the ultimate partner on the field. In memory of an impactful mentor, the judges are honored to present the Excellence in Engineering award to the robot MIKE.
This team is helpful in whole and in PART. They have traveled near and far even crossing state lines to help other teams. This 2-state 3-school 4-H club Is the ONE for us.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: TAKING FLIGHT transforms their artistic presentation. FLUTTERING around, this team’s detailed imagery expands to fill the arena. A BUTTERFLY’s wingbeat has caused chaos at this competition.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The king of the castle, this team is smooth like no other. With elegant and compact components, this robot springs to the rescue. With a fast extending arm, their YOSHI tongue is out of the BOT.

This team TAXED the judges’ intellect with their ACRONYMOUS presentation. Their DAC enables turret-like position adjustment, while their AARB enables reliable charge station balancing. We think their name could also stand for Incredible Robot Software.

Building up their community one brick at a time. UNIFYING ROBOTICS and providing for underserved communities. This team never gives kids a normal field trip with their FABulous bus. The Judges present the Magic School Bus award to:

By shifting their focus, this team CHAIN-ged the way they drove their robot. Their robust drivetrain and turret ensure quality motion and action. A sight from the stands, it is clear that this team RAIDed the paint cabinet for black and red.

This team led the EXCHANGE of FIRST core values internationally Thanks to their ADVOCACY every student will have a chance to succeed They TOTE-ALLY deserve this award. You better REACT because their RECIPE FOR SUCCESS deserves a lot of CREDIT.

Covid impacts got their GEARS spinning which resulted in the development of FLL robotics curriculum for the classroom Ambassadors for Unified Robotics they don’t leave anyone out Their focus on diversity, equality, and inclusion really WOWS the judges This team has FORGED a legacy as strong as IRON.

This Rookie team introduced FIRST to their school and recruited a quarter of the school to join them. They also introduced the mayor and Chamber of Commerce to FIRST. These Rookies are also working to BRING BACK THE ENERGY of FLL and FTC to their community.

This spirited team may be small, but they will grab your attention with their ORANGE attire like TENTACLES coming from the DEEP. Whether they are dancing or participating in a parade, they bring with them the spirit of FIRST.

Always a HIGHLIGHT of the competition this team is a FORCE to be reckoned with. Their model for sustainable financial and personnel plans is recognized across the GALAXY Success explodes like a shaken SODA bottle. OHH YUPP

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: De nombreuses équipes FIRST nouvellement formées peuvent retracer leurs débuts à cette équipe. L'équipe a persévéré en apportant sa passion pour FIRST à sa communauté, et à son pays, tout en lançant une solution innovante remarquable pour aider les autres. Cette équipe a mis au point une recette de succès digne du guide Michelin. Le Prix Impacte FIRST est décerné à l’équipe 5553 Robo’Lyon de Neuville-sur-Saône, Rhône, France.

This robot demonstrated consistent, reliable high performance autonomy. It routinely scored multiple pieces and charge station balance. It was also highly allergic to collisions and was obsessed with scoring.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: We all know creativity is key for innovation. One team stood out from the crowd and shifted their ideas to the stars. With an adorable mascot and team determination this group creatively saved many puzzles. Let's hear it for 4048 Red Shift!

This team started and mentors FLL teams and is a founding member of an alliance. They seek to help at athletic events and the athletes return the favor. Leads on this team interview for their positions, just like in the real world. This team is propelled along the canal of life being steered by rowing oars and mentors. Congratulations to the Gongoliers for winning the Engineering Inspiration Award!

This team started and mentors FLL teams and is a founding member of an alliance. They retain approximately 75% of their sponsors each year. As families do, this family eats dinner together. They are looking out for their members by setting and checking on their goals. They post a series of mental health monday's on social media during the build season. Congratulations to the Mechanical Advantage team on winning the FIRST Impact Award!

This team exemplifies what it takes to tackle any problem they face in robot design. Thorough documentation and high attention to an iterative design process is what sets this mean, green machine apart. This bionic group knows how to "aug"ment the strengths of their bot to tackle the challenges at hand.

This team impressed the judges with their demonstration of gracious professionalism. While small in size, this team's collaboration with other teams and dedication to diversity and inclusion is quite large. They truly represent the fundamental aspects of Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team was exceptional in demonstrating FIRST core values and displaying team pride. This team rolls in like a storm with a passion and representation. Everyone take cover as the red storm rolls.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's simple and small design left a "larger than life" presence on the field. With a design from the quantum realm, they fly around the field like a superhero, STRIKING fear into their opponents. Congratulations to Team 78

From creative robot/machine communication to innovative software uniquely designed to ace the game and perfect the control systems in their robot. This small team was able to design a robot with the driver in mind.
They fought the field and their bot won They fought the fire with dominion They fought the school and the kids won They fought the law and the team won.....

Excellent workmanship is a pillar of robustness. This team electrified our judges with their formidable fabrication and pristine paint job. This pack of Raiju (Rye-jew) forged a mystical machine worthy of praise and recognition. Let's hear it for the timberwolves of 1153.

Each year it's harder and harder to enter a FRC competition as a rookie. This team jumped into the fray with a vengeance. After the first week's battle, this team returned to their school and revamped their bot. With this weekends performance it is was easy to award "the oaker association" the rookie inspiration award.

This team with its simplistically designed bot faced many challenges throughout its design build and competition season. As the alarm sounded for each problem the team rallied with spirit and enthusiasm to solve the issue and moving forward for a successful season. This team's spirit was also uplifted with support from their school community and alliance partners. Their spirit is evident and the reason for being award Team Spirit.

Sustaining a team requires time, effort and a whole bunch of determination. This teams values are rooted in their lineage and builds upon their foundation like no other. The hybrid cross between two schools has created a power pride. Let's get a round of applause for the kings of sustainability. Lions and tigers, lets hear it for the Ligers!

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.script: When cones and cubes broke the law, it was time to call in the Sheriff. Using the long arm of the law, this team used its programming and coding to kick cubes and charge up. This robot magically swerves in and takes the top Autonomous award.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Not one to follow others, this robot wins the creativity award for design of their grabber. Using a unique telescoping arm, 6 autonomous variations, combined with a figure 8 chain, this robot is a diamond in the rough winning the Creativity Award.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.script: Due to their efforts they are expanding their whole region. West of the capital, they cowboys and cowgirls continually advocate for FIRST. What will their spark ignite next?!

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.script: This team’s efforts in spreading the FIRST message was demonstrated from their essay to their professional presentation. Teams describe this team as a model of Gracious Professionalism and everything FIRST values and the judges wholeheartedly agreed. This team takes the message of STEM from their backyard and beyond by writing grants to sustain the team, literally and figuratively driving STEM to underserved communities, and finding ways to get STEM in the classroom. This team’s rotational force is rolling the winds of change to their backyard and beyond. They are Category 5.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.script: Whether on top of the world or under the sea, this robot is not crabby. Using a professional design approach to the design process, this robot clawed its way to the top of the Excellence in Engineering Award.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.script: This team rushed out with their spare parts and workforce ready to lend a helping hand. For putting the motion behind Gracious Professionalism, and treating each team as part of their FIRST family. They truly are everyone's Big Brother.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has gone to the next level by rebranding their image. They took flight and not only made FIRST look good but themselves as well. For overcoming all their challenges and rising from the ashes.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team strikes a balance between form, function, and aestheics while creating a robot that can both score and balance on the charging station. Considered a Maverick in the robot arena, this well-designed robot is recognized for its innovative Pizza Pan.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.script: This team doesn’t get all torqued up, they stay in control. They rode their “televator” to the top of the list for the Innovation in Control Award. They continue to reach new heights in all aspects of FIRST.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.script: These students bring grit. Their robot is built like a monster truck. They are the cogs to keeping STEM in their community.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.script: If you’re chillin’ on the sidelines, you might want to get help from this team and robot. Their success will make you green with envy because of the quality of their workmanship. Surviving the rigors of competition has led this robot to be recognized as the Quality Award winner.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.script: They are coding their way through their first season. After debugging all kinds of problems, they are inspired to continue this journey.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.script: This team is fun, playful and respectful. As they slithered their way into the playoffs, they were really able to “Move It”. Their fangs might be small but their spirit is large.

records.eventName: PCH District Anderson Event presented by Magna
records.script: This team is well on their way to soaring above and beyond their own expectations. They took a train the trainer approach with their challenges. Luck will have nothing to do with their future sustainability.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.script: With a streak of black and blue, this team rushed in to drop the cube in the station before parking in autonomous mode. Like their namesake, they took flight into the air, launching over the charging stations to speed across the field. They really "drove it like they stole it."

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: In the FRC joust, this black knight robot used its diamond-plated armor to guard itself from its opponents. Their unique figure eight chain drive with dual motors protected them from burning out too soon. They really assaulted all the other robots in this category.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.script: When this team saw a need for STEM education in under-served communities, they swept in like a storm. Writing grants and bringing robotics kits to schools throughout their region, they made it possible for K thru 8 students in multiple counties and schools to pursue their STEM dreams. When elementary students were in an educational drought, this team brought the wind and rain. This team is truly in a Category of their own.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.script: This community team has evolved through the years into a strong and sustainable program from moving up through FLL, FTC, and now FRC. Their love of FIRST is apparent from their presentation to their pits and they diligently work to spark that love for FIRST with their families, community, and local and state government. There is no trail this team will not ride to bring STEM to their community. These cow pokes are creating a STEMPEDE in the upstate that will inspire future generations.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.script: This team may not be the most flashy but they compensate for that with an effective game plan. This multi school team developed a functional robot with the resources they have available. In a true David and Goliath story, this little robot brought down the giants with a plastic trough.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.script: When other teams are feeling blue, this team steps in to help. They mentor teams, host events, open their workshop, and volunteer their time and expertise to support all three FIRST programs in the heart of our state. These devils truly are angels in disguise.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team “ducked” a bullet to come back, and their light is shining brighter than ever with a cohesive design that encompasses their pit, t-shirts, robot design, and flair. They project a memorable eye-catching brand. This team is a Flash from the past.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Don your finest punk metal attire, bang your head, and join the mosh pit. This robot was able to efficiently intake game pieces and reach this highest levels of competition while providing a robust base for stability. Time really flies when you're cruising around with this Speed Wagon.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.script: With their use of limit switches for their robot's arm, encoders for their motors, and their gyroscope to provide balance, this team was able to steal matches from the competition. While the green of Saint Patrick's day may be over, the green glow from this team grabs your attention 281 days a year. The remaining 84 days are reserved for chillin' like a villain.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.script: This team's enthusiasm for FIRST made them "pretty in pink. Their showy costumes and creative use of videos for hype reels and student training stood out to the judges. Give these "Katz" a fist bump!

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.script: No bull! This robot doesn't follow others. They dominated the field with their Maverick robot. Wanted dead or alive, this team knows how to use their garage to maximize their impact.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.script: This rookie team has cracked the code. Overcoming all obstacles, they are already working on sustaining and supporting the students who will be coming after them. With a parent booster club, a non-profit, and a playbook in hand, these Comets really "tell the tail" of FIRST Robotics.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.script: This team really let us all be "part of their world" this weekend. They "clawed" their way into the hearts of the spectators. We all enjoyed "taking a drive under the sea" with Sebastian.

records.eventName: PCH District Hartsville Event presented by South Carolina Department of Education
records.script: This team has been burning tracks up and down the roads doing robot demos, teaching after school programs, mentoring FLL teams, and hosting cross-program FIRST events. They are a magnet, drawing new members and supporters to their team. They are on fire to keep their pipeline of teams expanding.

This team has consistently scored well in the autonomous period. They can place pieces with a push of a button, have their robot balance on the charger by itself, and auto-detect its position in the field using the April tags. The tribe built in 64 autonomous functions that have shown their merit on the field of battle.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team is getting ahead with a robot colored in red. Aiming their arm precisely with air redundancy is always in care. They winch their claw back, with springs pulling to the end of the track.
This team has impressive all-around skills. Their precise design allowed this team to shift into another gear during the competition. Their success is no secret.

This team is known for their legendary ability to help other teams before they even get back to their pits after matches. As their name implies, they might be perceived to walk on water, but in this case the water is frozen. They are named by many, and have a log to back it up.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team meets in history. Their platform in fantastical, and they incorporate it in everything that they do from their attire to their robot. They don't let steam cloud their vision.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's robot looks more at home in an automated factory. Their use of composites and anodized aluminum with enclosed wiring was functional and aesthetic. Although their robot looked at home, the team was far from home.

This team used a unique fully articulated one-sided arm to dominate the competition. They designed and implemented a fully featured automated multi-button driver control station along with braking servos. And they did it all with not using any pesky cameras.

Cats are known to have nine lives, and this team may have lost one of them in an early match yesterday. But like a cat, they managed to land on their feed and continue to successfully compete. The judges were impressed with their positive attitude, resilience, and creativity.

This team designed a robust, compact robot to withstand the rigors of competition. The utilized orange pi and two camaras to crush the competition. Their unique mix of high ground clearance and low center of gravity allows them to balance with ease.
This team runs like a business. Their inspiration reaches thousands. Their robot might end up full of holes, but they can easily respawn.

Since 2008, this team has demonstrated sustained performance in overcoming economic and geographic barriers promoting STEM awareness in their community. This team is committed to STEM education through teamwork, community involvement, diversity, equity, and inclusion. They established the MIP process to foster student-led design. They have a proven track record of creating leaders and innovators that prepares them for life after MARS.

This team was off to a slow start with the late arrival of their KOP. Once they arrived at the venue, they where blown away by the friendliness and help they received. They ended with a robot that could score and play a mean defensive game.
This team screamed the loudest in the stands. You will definitely see them coming, but don't be afraid. Even though they have many layers, one hex code stands out.
This team's time has come. Let's put this gear in overdrive. There is no stopping them. They have ensured that their clock will be wound in perpetuity.

records.script: This team auto elevated their scores. Their Autonomous functions saw them flying around the field. On Pegasus wings, this team was a scoring machine. Congratulations Team 1745. P-51 Mustangs.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This teams use of reverse air pressure was as creative as it was functional. Their over reaching arm and intuitive design vacuumed up the competition. Congratulations Team 7492. Cavbots

It's a mathematical certainty that this team wouldn't leave us adrift in our quest for inspiration. Their island gantry sits upon a solid foundation. They did not leave the judges cold when they harnessed the power of the sun to fuel their vessels. This team Frosted Out the competition! Congratulations Team 5411. Robo Talons

FIRST can be a place where people grow. This team grew from very little and developed into a family. They are not just an FRC team, they are a FIRST family from beginning to end. When it came down to it, they answered the call of duty and are selfless in their endeavors. They are honorable mercenaries. Congratulations Team 6369, Mercenary Robotics!

This teams robot was as slick as a snake. The student engineers blacked out the competition with their performance and professionalism. Even with outweighing the competition, it still moved like a mamba on the field. Congratulations Team 148. Robowranglers
With this team around, Why worry in the pits? They were always lending helping hands and minds. The most Graciously Professional Team around. Congratulations Team 4153. Project Y

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team bounced into Amarillo. Their bright colored hats point to their destination. Don't be tricked, these kids came to win. Congratulations Team 4063. TriKzR4Kidz

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot swerves around the field, placing game pieces all around. Their sleek black design is speedy and industrial. This team quickly flew to the top of the rankings. Congratulations team 3310. Black Hawk Robotics.
If you want to see the snow, you know where to go. From their exciting designs to their ocean sky shirts, this team proved their knowledge on and off the field. Congratulations Team 4206. RoboVikes

The evidence was clear that this team had a legal strategy for check-mating the competition. May the record reflect, they were selected for the judge's Judgiest award based on their extraordinary leap landing them so far outside the stands, we just had to bear witness. THIS TEAM ABSOLUTELY ROOKED THE COMPETITION! Congratulations Team 6171. Chain Reaction.

If you want your sponsors seen, this team has your machine. Soaring above the competition, this robust robot makes you take notice. Precision of design had them flying to the finish line. Congratulations Team 8874. Cybirds.

This blue-clawed team is an all-star cast of future engineers. Showing incredible potential, we feel they will prosper for years to come. Their robots namesake flew to the stars and we expect to see them there as well. Congratulations Team 9105. TechnoTalons

This teams inspiring outreach tramples the competition. To India and back, this team is passionate about STEM. This Rookie Team is turbo charged with commitment to their community. Congratulations Team 9136. Rampage.
Who had a smile throughout the whole competition? What green team spreads spirit from the pits to their community? This Rookie Team answers the questions! Congratulations Team 9080. Enigma.

This team stands strong against the wind. Holding onto their black hats is a testament to their resilience. Swirling through the pits and the stands, they sustain their western foothold. Congratulations Team 4717. Westerner Robotics

This team electrified the judges with how this team integrated their sensors into their code. It allowed for SHOCKINGLY slick movements around the field and prepared them for any autonomous configurations.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team SHOOK the judges with their unorthodox game piece mechanism. They slithered to the top of the creativi-tree with their simple, but effective cube shooter. We hope they sink their Fangs into this award.

This robotics team is constantly changing and improving processes to make things better. When something breaks, they SPRING into action. This team is full of POTENTIAL ENERGY, and will surprise you with their enthusiasm and love for spreading FIRST to others.

Seven teams committed time to preparing submissions for the Impact Award. They all rose to the challenge of taking on an extra task during the busy build season, and each of these teams showed just how deeply committed FRC participants are to the ideals of FIRST. Although only one team will win the Impact Award, they were all strong contenders who exemplify the passion and dedication that everyone there has for youth robotics. This year’s Impact Award winner wowed the judges with the breadth of their outreach activities. Their efforts include an ORCHARD of initiatives, such as hosting events at Worlds, striving to increase the number of Black students in STEM, teaching young girls about building, and supporting a number of FTC and FLL teams. This SAVVY team has PEARed up with Girl Scouts, FRUITFULLY spread the values of FIRST, and are well pre-PEARed for the future.
This team all in their brains Double jointed arm, don't seem the same Preforming well, and we do know why 'Scuse them while they reach the sky

This team showed exceptional gracious professionalism on the feild and in the pits. They showed PURfect poise and grace while pouring blood, sweat, tears, and parts into helping other teams and the event. You can always count on this team to land on their feet. Give it up for the cat's meow

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team outshined the others with the unity in their designs. They impressed the judges with their ELECTRIFYING artistic creativity and show that art and robotics go SHOCKINGLY well together.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team pounced to the challenge of the Engineering Design process. From the purple hued hills they stealthily captured the judges attention because even Wakanda could have benefitted from this teams curiosity, ingenuity, and passion for design.

This award was a snap to decide once the judges took a crack at it. We were impressed by the PID control of their multi-jointed arm and their simple operator interface. Its superb integration helped the team POP its way to the top of ranks.

The judges decided to give this award to a team who exemplified resourcefulness. This robotics team found cleaver ways to overcome financial challenges they were facing. These "ultra" cool students found innovative ways to make their robot and "ultimately" saw how recycling parts could pay off.

Newly birthed into FIRST Robotics, this team chose to make a simple "robo-bust" design to that was simple to maintain. Controlling their quality with clarity and making them a force to be reckoned with when they charged onto the BoBattlefield.

This team uses summer camps, tours, and booths to educate the public about the FIRST program. They explained that FIRST is not just the robot, but an entire program with many areas for students to engage with. Business, marketing, finances. This team has built more than just a robot to swim through the ocean of competition.

This team makes good use of demos and fairs to get elementary and middle school to become future FRC members. They also communicate that FIRST is not just about the robot and exemplify a fighting spirt.

This team brightened our spirits all confirmation. We could hear them cheering for all teams across the field. They were bursting with excitement when talking to the judges and even taught us their cheer: tik tik BOOM! It's Orange Dynamite

When this team realized the future of their kingdom was in danger they put the callout to their "metal head" friends to join forces. These "knights" have created a longstanding sustainable future for their team.

The judges were impressed by this team’s use of sensors and streamlined processes. From collecting to scoring, this team has a strong grip on automation. We watched their robot play with speed and accuracy, STEELing the show.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This second year team impressed us with a specialized robot that was fun to watch. This bot scored cubes like popcorn popping from the hopper! Their creativity really shines!

This team inspired the judges with their thoughtful approach to removing barriers to FIRST and STEM. They inspire other students, even from a distance. And if you lose your rhythm, this team just might help you rejoin the dance.

This team has had a direct, positive impact on many of the teams at this weekend’s competition and around the world. From focusing on team mental health to designing solutions to help other teams launch their seasons, they’re finding new ways to improve on their impressive foundation!

From their ability to pick-up pieces from two sides to their novel drive train this team had a well thought out design. They have engineered a novel pneumatically-activated brake to hold their robot stable on a shifting platform. The low profile design easily meets the robot’s size limit while reaching any height desired. This team works with a number lower level teams to ensure a steady flow of students with qualified students who are chips off the old block.

Let’s shine a light on a team with an outstanding positive attitude, and initiative to help others. This team, has lent a helping hand to others by jumping to build bumpers for other teams, and helping other teams pass inspection. This teams’ commitment to sportsmanship has been a ray of sunshine the past three days.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Before the dawn of man, an apex predator emerged from the murky depths. Ever elusive, but intelligent, crafty, and … color-coordinated, this creature brought attractiveness in engineering, and outstanding aesthetic integration of the machine and team appearance. Teal. Yellow. Purple…You’ve likely seen this mysterious beast yourself roaming the pits and the field. It’s hard to describe, but impossible to miss!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team utilized an efficient design that was refined through prototyping. Their robot propelled their team HIGH in the ranks. This team showed the POTENTIAL DIFFERENCE a harmonious design can make.

Wait … is that a cube or a cone? Where should it go? Drivers have a lot of decisions to make, and keeping those human players from ‘RAGING’ is a difficult job. The judges were impressed with this team’s simple and elegant sensor-based automation of this work– letting the ‘DROID’ do the work of identifying game pieces and making scoring as easy as a Padre Island breeze.

This team stood out to the judges from the start. From their team aesthetics to their outreach, this team is building a legacy that is morphing their region by sparking an interest in STEM and spreading the spirit of FIRST. Their future is bright…GREEN.

‘Orange’ you glad you met this team? The judges were! This team impressed with their robust design and ‘ready for anything’ approach to sustaining performance. The team passionately explained simple things, like putting washers behind rivets to add strength, and more complicated things, like printing 3D parts on-demand over the Internet. Was it a monster truck? Say it with us – “OH YEAH!!!”

This team’s design process is very advanced for such a young team. The results show in the field of play, and all team members played their part. Don’t get caught in the stampede on their rise to the top!

This rookie team empowers girls to be interested in STEM. This rookie team shows what’s possible when they face challenging situations. We were impressed by their perseverance and grit. So gather your doubloons, and let’s set sail to make waves!
Welcoming all with wings held wide, this team displays blue and yellow unity. The entire team was CHANNELing spirit throughout the competition. You don’t have to try to get VIEW of this team.

How does a team build a robot legacy? Answer: by recruiting ‘legions’ of new members through summer training camps. They overcome all obstacles with a ‘phalanx’ of different solutions – fundraising, passion for STEM, and a deep understanding of FIRST Core Values. If robots existed in ancient Greece, this team of Spartans would dominate with its long-term strategy and sustainable approach.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: This team improved the stability of their robot by virtualizing their elevator structure. Their robot has been a master of balance, even in the fog of competition. The software in this robot smoothly choreographs the motors like a slow dance to a Jimi Hendrix song.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: It's clear that this team has some creative minds! Fitting a square peg in a typically round hole is right in their lane, making their robot much more stable when the chips are down.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: Like a cougar stalking it prey, this team focuses on a big signing day. They know this trail will eventually lead to prosperity. They celebrate the end of their FRC journey by setting their sights on their engineering future.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: This team found innovative ways to stay involved during the pandemic and kept their plans for team sustainability and STEM outreach going despite the challenges of moving many activities to the virtual space. They impressed the judges with their diverse portfolio of activities and their work to take the message of FIRST around the world. The judges are confident that this team’s initiatives are making a real impact in their community that will leave a legacy.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: When presented with a challenge, this team jumped at the opportunity. Whether with legos or wood, they sprang into action and iterated on their journey to become excellent engineers.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: When other teams needed help, this team was ready to engage. They slithered in providing enhanced support to all with load-in on day one and impressed the judges with their GP all weekend!

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The judges' eyes were drawn to some BOLD colors, and this team has them from head to pit and even the WIRING in between. So bob along with us as we celebrate their entrance.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team did not let the fate of the materials used determine their aesthetic and functional design. Their quick “disconnect system” connected them in being competitive thought out the match. This team truly shows that one’s persons’ trash can be another persons’ winning robot.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: A cone in a strange orientation is no problem for this team's auto righting system that always puts it in the right place. They can even fork onto a filled charging station to raise and balance a partner. The innovation that this team showed in their design is clearly out of this world.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: This team has made it their mission to charge ahead, spreading STEM throughout the land. These electric warriors are doing their part to make STEM accessible and inclusive to all!

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: This team's quality had no RESISTANCE. CURRENTLY, they display robustness and workmanship without losing amps. Their reliability CONDUCTED a fierce opponent while staying warm with their beanie.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: This team is one of the newest elements. They are neighborly but not radioactive. This team is blue but definitely not sad. This rookie team is in command of all the stars.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: This team has shown real perseverance this season. Unlike their mascot, this team's not shy nor small, and they glide through the community scoring new members and sponsors along the way.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: Charged up with energy and spirit, their cheers could be heard all over, whether for themselves or someone else. Their energy was nuts, and their team spirit could not be broken.

records.eventName: FIT District Space City @ Clear Lake Event
records.script: This team was on the part to recruit new members to our FIRST community. With summer camps, training programs, & offseason battles, this team came out victorious with sword and shield.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This rookie team stepped up their FIRST game and stepped onto the FRC plate. They have truly raised the bar to achieve a substantial fundraising goal, and have performed well this competition season. As a community team, they have impacted the world already and have been showcased in the Middle East. These rookies have inspired and create a MARVELOUS pipeline program and have continued to inspire in their community.
