records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66
records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This rookie team combined its efforts to star in this FRC season. These rookies really had to learn the ropes quickly, as their robot quickly climbed the ranking mountain. These rookies not only inspire students, but also inspire adults by providing local coach workshops. This team really RAMPED up the competition this year and shined a light on their work.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66
records.script: This team’s commitment to Science and Technology education is the community and their outreach efforts are unparalleled. With their focus on connecting different parts of the community to STEM and advocacy for legislation, this team demonstrated outstanding success and appreciation for engineering.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66
records.script: This team’s respect for engineering is steadfast and applied through the team, school, and community. Whether it’s having kids drive the robot at Robotics Day, moving Girls Forward in STEM, being a TARP mentor, or making it know that every child can do the UN-IMPOSSIBLE in FIRST - this team is an engineering force.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66
records.script: Everything this team does, increases the potential for other teams. By providing resources, materials and mentoring, this team gives everybody the opportunity to learn from them. Their sustainable pipeline is so vast, it is truly out of this world. This team raises the floor for all teams in FIRST, and creates a blueprint to help no matter your starting point. With over 13% percent of this year’s robots using their design, they are the clear winner for this IMPACT award.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66
records.script: Mentoring FLL and FTC keeps this team’s pipeline in check. Their advocacy work not only helped bring up Texas needs, but racked up more STEM opportunities. This team knows no cultural barrier with 14 different languages spoken and equally distribution of leadership across genders, their recipe for inclusion deserves the blue ribbon. By creating their owning winning sauce, this team has soared to new heights with their international outreach. If you’re not careful, this team’s flames with smoke you out.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66
records.script: By growing and sharing valuable skill sets, this team branches out and covers a lot of ground from a clever use of power tools to making a more inclusive community. You can flip through their pages and resource data in multiple languages. If you need a place to practice or need support PEARparing for a competition, their doors are always open. If fundraising is your issue, PEARing with this group will give you tips and tricks to do it yourself. This team inspires individuals to be creative, competent and capable. You can PEAR up with them at their multiple conferences at World Championships.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.script: This team is ALWAYS aware of where they are. Even when they are spinning around and around until their limit switch spring tells them to stop, they won’t get disoriented because they are constantly keeping an eye on the multiple AprilTags. Contributors to multiple open source projects including PathPlanner, this team is applying some forward TORQUE to the public coding community.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s creative solution to limited resources lifted their robot from the SCRAP pile. Using what they had on hand and donated plastic, this team built a triple jointed arm and cable system resembling a steam shovel that enhanced their ability and strategy.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.script: This team’s engineering process included modularity and redundancy with safety coded at set points. This system is designed to optimize the drivers’ performance with a built in PRECISION MODE. The design of this robot allows the drivers and robot to FUSE into each other’s BETTER HALF.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.script: This team exemplified Gracious Professionalism year round. They post detailed guides, help teams at competition, and open their doors to teams in need. The judges were impressed by this team’s ability to ABSORB knowledge and DISPERSE resources to others. The ways this team supports the FIRST community are so vast, they cover the whole SPECTRUM.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This crew sailed to the top of the imagery category with their furry duck-billed mascot leading the way. Their robot danced through the field like its namesake, helmed by a team of plucky pirates waving the Jolly Roger. This rookie team of talented buccaneers are as original and fun as can be.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team took design to the next level with 3D printed parts and an immaculate elevator design. This team runs on a bright journey in the right direction. The team distinguishes themselves from others with energy and their robot’s top VELOCITY.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.script: This team impressed the judges with a root that has over two feet of vertical reach and is nearly untippable with programming to prevent the swerve drive from changing too quickly. Despite their name, this team always puts safety first with an innovative safety mechanism that automatically shuts off motors through a software switch.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.script: This Judges Award for Pioneering goes to this vibrant, welcoming team. Their pioneering story made them march to the top of the list. They are a rising star launching STEM programs in their community. In order to reach for the stars, they built a rocket launcher. WE WANT YOU to give a round of applause for this team.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.script: This team demonstrated quality in every step of their build process. Their elevator and arm design were truly BOLD ideas. They showed that attention to detail and COURAGE pay off.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.script: This team's coaching for FLL has proven successful from high regions to the sea. They go above and beyond to reach across borders through their many exchange students and have developed personal connections across the globe. They prioritize machine uniqueness and simplicity, garnering them attention at STEM showcases and fairs. Just like the clownfish and sea anenome, their students rely on each other to overcome challenges creating a symbiotic relationship.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.script: This purple-clad team was up on their feet cheering loud every chance they got. Their LED lights and cowboy hats caught the judges’ eye, but we were most impressed with their endurance and excitement throughout the competition. We were NUTS about their spirit, and they BOLTED straight to the top of the list.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - APOLLO Division
records.script: You better step in line and walk the walk when this team enters the field. Their dedication to team persistence and inclusion strengthens the UNIT. They make it clear that ORANGE is the new black.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.script: The judges were impressed with this robot that has the vision to know how to get where it’s going. In the autonomous period, this robot has been a formidable NEMESIS. This team proves that great software can be mightier than STEEL.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Lots of robots have pumps that work great and screws to hold everything together. One team uses screws to do the heavy lifting and their pumps PULL YOU IN. Don’t let the pink façade fool you, these LADIES CAN delivery.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.script: This team exemplifies an excellence in engineering that extends beyond the undisputed prowess of their robot. Pristine documentation and organized design principles have allowed them to learn from their past mistakes and RISE FROM THE ASHES every time. With a dedicated focus on fostering manufacturing and machining skills team-wide, they make sure their AXES are always sharpened for battle!

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.script: This team is hidden in the hills and deserts guarding an enchanted secret – buy WHY? Is it the secret of their Christmas enchiladas? No! This team is working on growing a statewide network of existing and new teams through creative networking.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From the stands to the field, this team is as cohesive as they come. Their purple hue can be seen drifting from pit to pit. Don’t let their shirts fool you. It’s not paisley, it’s HAZY.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The team’s industrial design has afforded it unmatched efficiency. Their robot’s ability to multitask lets it SWOOP across the field and score in record time. Leaving other teams in its SHADOW, their competitive design is unmatched.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.script: This team has many different 3D printed parts. Their software progression through custom buttons is no THROWBACK. They’re mechanical progression took the judges BACK TO THE FUTURE as it transitioned between three different intakes.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.script: This blue team with a strong orange FTC program went beyond the binary colors of their team this season. This team shines in all colors ensuring everyone has an opportunity to participate in robotics. This team TURBOCHARGES robotics for all.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.script: After this team followed a carefully refined plan, it’s no accident a complete BLACKOUT occurred. This amazing machine emerged from a cloud of darkness at the pinnacle of the quality pyramid. The ORIGINAL team to BLACKOUT the competition truly stands apart.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.script: This rookie team plays like a seasoned veteran. Maybe they saw the possibilities in a Pixar movie and they went to INFINITY and BEYOND. With a pipeline established to provide infinite resources, they have really hit the MARK.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.script: This special forces unit uses a green beret with a COWBOY flair. You can’t miss this team with their green lights, shoes, shirts, and pit. Their new shop at the elk’s lodge might make other teams GREEN with envy.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship presented by Phillips 66 - MERCURY Division
records.script: Green, black, and sharp as an EAGLE’S eye, this team includes everyone who wants to participate. They created a pipeline to promote female participation in future seasons. Their PIERCING desire to make FIRST accessible to all is a true testament to their love for robotics and inclusivity.

This team elevated their game with autonomous code. They “swerved” across the field, accumulating game pieces and “cubing” the excitement from the opening seconds. The robot masterfully parked itself at the top of the charging station.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This robot could not camouflage its creativity on or off the field. With a unique elevator system and quick release snap-on bumpers, this bot prowls through a jungle of cubes and cones. This teams robot is named after a longtime mentor, “Shad” which this team is truly proud of.

This team had all the “right ingredients” to inspire, teach and empower girls to pursue STEM. With one “Ice scream scoop” at a time, they are expanding FIRST’s mission across the communities. This engineering inspiration award is given to this “well baked, evenly cut team, ‘pepper’ pizza…. Oops…

This team showed judges how much impact a team can do around the community, in the nation, and internationally. They run and host on and off-season competitions across various FIRST programs. The team started, mentored, and/or assisted multiple FLL, FTC, FRC and FIRST Global Teams. This team created STEM programs for women, youth, student athletes, students with disabilities, and student minorities. They bring FIRST to school fairs, city parades, city festivals and even professional sports games. This team shows other FRC teams how to “SOAR” to new heights.
This team came in with a new “spin”. They were able to quickly “Amp-Up” to the challenge. And, the team had no issues “Charging” into the competition.

This team embodies Gracious Professionalism through their commitment to helping others. They “make it loud” by hosting FTC and FLL scrimmages and by hosting an FRC off-season event. They are “Geared” to helping teams with “thundering” passion both during competitions and on baseball fields. When asking other teams who helped them the most, there was only one answer -> the loud and proud TITANS.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: We would like to give this team a big “hand”. With cards and “furry jesters”, they fill up the stands. They sting like a “scorpion”, but look like pros.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This high velocity team impressed the judges with their wholly independent subsystems. They focused on building redundancy and “stinging” the competition with their lightweight robot. Never one to run from a battle, their 4-bar linkages stayed strong through every match.

This team showed incredible implementation of their control systems and produced an autonomous function that would make “Doc Brown” proud. With a pre programmed field map, solid scoring control presets, and "flux capacitor", these time traveling “red camo clad kids” are controlling their destiny and the competition.

This team greatly impressed the judges. They are like a "cobra" in a target rich environment. This team has captured everyone’s attention both on and off the field. The judges named this award the “Bedazzled” Award!

This quality team fought with the integrity and consistency of a fighter pilot. They stayed steady thanks to a hidden steel belly pan. Their simple mechanisms and strong drivers have allowed this team to “fly” through the competition.

To “Infinity and beyond”! Though this team did not have enough space, they took what little they had and expanded the world around them, making room for everyone. They took NASA’s slogan to heart, and for this reason we have selected this team as our Rookie All-Star.

This robot team is out of this world! With their huge presence at this event, we are so glad they came here to inspire us with their “shiny gold”. The judges feel we have not seen the last of this “blue fin”.

This team has a positive attitude and likes to “make it loud”! These warriors attack each match with Gracious Professionalism. Their spirit will spread beyond the East through their robotics hero story book.

Growing younger teams is essential to this team’s sustainability. “Overall”, they are not afraid of long hours or getting their hands dirty. Planting seeds now, these pioneers are watching their crops grow with anticipation for the next generation of inventors.

This team starts the match with an automated routine full of energy. They used programming to augment the human element, allowing their team to really shine on the field. How they use code to FUSE the driver and machine shows the potential automation has to help us reach new heights.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their enthusiasm. They bring form to functionality with their aesthetic 3D printed intake, cleverly reinforced with aluminum stock. Shining brighter than the NEW MEXICO SUN, we know they’ll go far no matter what DIRECTION they take.

This team climbed THE HILL to reach new goals and their success is no SECRET. They show off their robots at sporting events and citywide parades. Still wondering WHY? They also focused their outreach efforts on getting robotics recognized as a statewide sport.

From hosting FTC workshops to founding teams, these students are IGNITING passion for FIRST in their community. They have advocated to their city, state, and national government about their vision for STEM expansion. They are broadening their impact beyond our national borders by CHOPPING down barriers for underfunded students. In their efforts to further the mission of FIRST, they presented to members of the National legislature at the National Advocacy Conference. Their assistance helped in the passing of ESSA IV-A, resulting in 8 million dollars SERVED UP to Texas on a platter. Both in and out of the pit, these grillmasters are cooking up opportunities for everyone.
This team has put their thoughts towards efficient and reliable machine building. The machine was electrified through many iterations, until it was finally CHARGED up to the competition.

This team was not the LONE competitor to come from far away. They have a look and enthusiasm that can’t CAMOUFLAGE their contagious spirit. You will know they are in the house when you hear them shout G.P.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is a FULL HOUSE of represented schools and awesome students. Their robot scores like a stallion and stings like a scorpion. There’s nothing unpredictable about this WILDCARD of a team.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team is an example of practicality and robustness with structural subsystems that can be interchanged, repaired, or completely redesigned and reattached, with only a few bolts. It’s impossible to not hear their rotors roaring from the field.

This team’s robot is so COOL that it leaves a layer of FROST on the field with every match. Their smart robot can sense what game object it’s carrying thanks to their state-of-the-art controls engineering. They impressed the judges with their innovative SHWERVE drive.

This team faced challenge after challenge and never CAVED IN. Their many accomplishments prove that they refused to go into HIBERNATION this winter. Their ideas, teamwork, and ability to adapt and think outside of the box resulted in achievements that one could call RADICAL. These achievements are what earned this team the Judge’s Award for TENACITY.

For this team, a singular event provided the IMPULSE. An unplanned disassembly left a module lying on the horizon. After LAUNCHING their revision, they had a robot that could survive the rigors of competition RE-ENTRY. When it comes to quality, this team has the MISSION under CONTROL.

This team is a model for how to create a riddling robot of no compare. They kept us on our toes with their enthusiasm. They developed their rookie team on a MYSTERIOUS foundation with a their strong partnership efforts. This team may be hard to understand, but not for us Judges.

This rookie team has started an outreach program worthy of veteran status. Their overseas mentorship and FIRST team expansion has been recognized by morning news and gained DIAMOND status. From camps to block coding to FTC kits, this team has laid the foundation for robotics inspiration that can only be described as marvelous.
This team refuses to be just a cog in the machine. Robotics, it seems, is not GREEK to them. This team’s enthusiasm and vibrant style gets us GEARED up for competition.

This team has a well-documented plan for measurable growth and success. Their annual STEM camp and freshman outreach program contributed to fierce and aggressive year-over-year growth for themselves and their community. Webinars, local park events, and homecoming festivals are worthy of a HOWL and set an example for STEM diversity and gender inclusion.

This team is a strong force that goes the distance, even beyond national borders. With their custom vision system and autonomous abilities throughout the match, this team automatically deserves this award.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: To win this award, this team looked back to the days of yore for inspiration. They designed and implemented a legendary tool to allow them to shoot cubes from farther away and still be inside the lines. Whosoever wields this sword is rightfully the winner of creativity!
This team inspired not only younger students through FLL teams but their entire community both in the arena and on the field. From the Big River, we want you!

This team demonstrated their commitment to the FIRST community by hosting 4 FIRST events in just the last 6 months. They advocate for the expansion of robotics programs with their school district by lighting a fuse for funding, recognition, and promotion. In addition, their contributions go beyond STEM education and FIRST, by using their skills and resources to positively impact the environment. Whether mentoring teams, increasing boba awareness, or deploying raccoons on the beach, THE ZEST IS YET TO COME.

This team demonstrated their excellence by a well-documented design process involving the whole team. On their path to the stars, they built a robot that can practically do it all. This redesign not only enabled a strong performance, it put them in another galaxy.

This team demonstrates the spirit FIRST by shining a light on smaller teams. This team's commitment to giving and mentoring reflects the principles of FIRST. So light it up, because this team is electromagnetic!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s imagery SOARED above the competition. Their team’s theme just can’t be beat. Get ready to ruffle your feathers!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: From their articulated arm all the way down to the organized wires and cables, this bright robot demonstrated it all. No one would think this team's robot is a can to kick down the road.

This team has an amazingly agile auton for foiling the competition. They impressed us with their web-based graphical calculator for drawing new auton paths. This is the kind of thinking that can make steel weak.

This team puts high focus on ensuring that every student has the opportunity to engage with STEM and robotics. Through abolishing fees, tracking diversity metrics, and celebrating all contributions, they showed the judges that they highly value authenticity, accessibility, and inclusion.
The judges were impressed with the clean lines on this robot. This robot is built tough and calculated. The tilted elevator extends with direction AND magnitude.
When this team moseyed into the pit, they wrangled their cubes, and they have big plans for the future. Saddle your horses and shake your spurs for these all-star rookies!
This team strikes for their first time this year. They rallied together and gave it their all. Slither over and shake your rattlers for this team!

This team impressed the judges with the passion for STEM and FIRST that was evident in all their interactions. They even took some of their bots to the water with their Sea Perch program! This team drives a bus that is fueled by enthusiasm!

This team embraces a whole community focus for building their legacy. Using student leaders, they have developed a powerful program to build a strategy for longevity. Only a dance floor with flashing lights show more coordination among three different dancers!

This team attacked the field with a strong and "consistent" plan and easily completing three task of scoring, mobility and balancing. Just giving us a small taste of autonomous to be used during the following game play. With a solid vision of the field in hand, combined with an upgraded "Grabber II" this red camo team driven by Thing 1 and Thing 2 almost didn't need a driver.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team used several creative design and manufacturing approaches to increase robot stiffness and reduce the number of parts in the robot. The shoulder design integrated the batteries, shoulder gear reduction and pivot structure into one combined package ensuring ease of assembly and excellent controllable motion. Using these unique features the team hitched up their robot and rode their way into the creativity award.

This team 'Inspires" all students about FIRST by building relationships within their community and across continents. Core value of inclusion whether with sponsors, younger teams, or peers is the part of their legacy. By going rogue they are leading the way with FIRST values.

Throughout the years, this team has not only created a sustainable program but has recently expanded across their community. This team gets "extra brownie points" for having creative STEM workshops and experiences for girls throughout their community. This team's IMPACT goes beyond FIRST and has created a duct taped network beyond their team and into the future. They wear their heart on their sleeve and as well as their robot and are keeping a legacy alive.

This team showed everyone the benefits of embracing the full engineering process. They were super organized and had a procedure for winning. Their robot glides across the field "sideswiping" the competition with ease.
With their positive attitude they are always running to help others. This team's mascot is one of the fastest you have seen around. We all "appreciate" everything this team does for others.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has an image like no other. They had us hooked from the start, you can see them from the depths of the competition. Swimming their way to the top with style and scheme.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Looking simple while being complex & compact is a difficult design to achieve! This team "smoked" the competition with elegance. Despite the orange camo, this team stands out in the crowd.

This team has a fast and precise robot with elegant moves. It has an innovative swerve drive train, elevator, and intake that shows this teams amazing engineering abilities. We love to watch this purple robot speeding around the field like a panther, looking for its prey.

This team tickled the judges pink with their attitude towards their stewardship of FIRST values through helping teams across the state lines. They build connections by reintroducing STEM and FIRST to their elementary schools and hosting Lego camps for kidz. There are no "tricks" for these kidz as they "HOP" right in to lend a helping hand.

This team brought a "grounded" perspective to the field. The robustness and concept of their robot "catapulted" this team into the limelight. No one should be "perplexed" by this team receiving the quality award.
This team is an energized gem. Their robot belongs in a museum. They use a good support to prop up their wooden intake. Oops, they did it again.

This team is learning a new tradecraft for FRC. They have a mutually beneficial relationship with various robotic programs in their city. GP stands for Gracious Professionalism; but with this team GP includes inspiration.

This team displayed their enthusiasm and spirit for their team, our nation and FRC through a full display of Red, White and Blue. Their use of design sharing of a t-shirt missile launching system helps spread spirit, encouragement and love for FIRST.

This team truly leads by example in defining sustainability by creating an open shelf program for new mentors, and creating software libraries for future teams. This bright team is galloping their way through connecting and producing valuable leaders in the FIRST community. "Orange" you glad you have this team on your side to train your spirited colts?

This team is "courageous" in how they use software to get the most from their robot. They feature a custom programming language that is easy to read for non-programmers and builds their autonomous paths for them. They also feature a programming structure that can adapt to a sudden swap of electronics, so this team’s code will function no matter what gets in their way on the battlefield.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's creative design really drew us in. Their can-do attitude really shone through in their colorful robot. Their unique suction-cup manipulator design was clearly thinking outside of the cookie box.

This team left all the others in the "dust". Not only did they provide PPE to their community, but they also focus on reducing their drop out rates in their middle schools. This team "roped" over 2300 students into their STEM camps and have a mighty positive impact on their community.

This teams’ impact in spreading the FIRST mission is phenomenal. Shining across not only their community but internationally as well. They inspire STEM growth by creating resources and sharing their talent for the entire FIRST community. Opening their doors to the community for off season events and hosting international teams in their workspace. This team has insured that teams are successful in their FIRST journey by providing over twenty-thousand dollars worth of equipment to teams across FIRST. This teams’ mission of providing opensource resources for others has over ninety-seven teams sharing their designs and ideas, The Open Alliance is a what FIRST is about. This team's resources on Chief Delphi, Discord and on the FIRSTinspires website have made knowledge accessible to all teams.

After talking to all of the teams at this event, it is clear that the engineering process doesn't happen at at once, but happens over the entire build season. The judges spent lots of time "marinating" on which team was the best fit for this award. In the end, we really sunk our teeth into this team's pulled pork sandwich.

The judges were impressed with this teams dedication to helping make this district run destructively? Wait... no that's not right. Despite having a small team, their members stepped in to help with all aspects of the event and their assistance with field set-up was anything but devastating.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: A blue synthesis of machine and team, this group impressed us with their attractive, bright blue pits and cohesive team attire (complete with plenty of pockets). Despite thier camo pants, this team was definitely not hiding.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot in-'corp'-orated several functions into one elegant mechanism. Don't be fooled by it's simplicity, because the team has clearly spent a lot of time refining their design. Just like Mario and Yoshi, two intake mechanisms 'fuse' together into one functional unit.

This team holds their chest high when it comes to how they control their robot. They use industry-level technologies to ensure the robot knows exactly where it is at all times, and their out of this world scoring shows it. Additionally, their use of a custom path planning website makes sure that the autonomous period won’t be their weakness.

The Judges have decided to give this award to a team that's shown us exceptional engineering enthusiasm. This team really "Clawed" us in with their inclusivity and eagerness to talk about their program. They exceed in showing how STEM can relate to anyone by bringing everyone (including their school board) into a big Bear hug.
Just like Texas, this robot is really built to last. Its cone orientation mechanism design made our heads spin. Upon closer inspection, we found that their robot was as robust as their giant wrench.

Even as a rookie, this team's international impact is unmatched. During their first year in FRC, this team has worked with students from Nigeria and Pakistan, introduced their community to STEM through camps, and presented their FIRST experience at conferences. This team would be considered an "All-Star" at any event, which is even more impressive considering their rookie status.

This rookie team works extensively within their community. From robot fabrication in the local science museum to meet and greets to trash pickup, this team is involved with their small town community in every way. Their "energy" towards communication the FIRST mission is inspiring.
This team showed "Fur"-ocious team spirit both on and off the field. Their banners made other teams green with envy, and the judges could hear their howling across the arena.

This team is a 'force' to be reckoned with. Other teams, Leagues, and programs were swept up by their mentorship. Strong relationships with sponsors, solid documentation, and team structure. They ensure that future members will be able to "weather any storm"

No crime here, Peter Gunn; everything is legit in this covert operation. This team shoots a bullseye and is fully charged in less than 15. Operating non-autonomously in Silicon Valley they have great success with their bot.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team took an iterative approach to Teeter Totters. When on the Charging Stations, their dogs are always down to help. They always have it in the bag.

With heart, faith, and steel this team designed and developed a complete solution so that in the end there can be only ONE. With the speed, accuracy, and agility of a formula one race car, they quickly CHARGED UP the ranks. Their robot could not be KILT.
Loyalty to the robotics community describes this team. They mush right over when they see others in need and graciously give what they can, in a professional way.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The team's wild style is evident in every aspect, from their head to their paws and throughout their den. Their enthusiasm is contagious and can shake the place, regardless of the time of day. Witnessing them prowl the arena is sure to brighten your entire day.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Clearly, this team did not spend their season hibernating. They worked their paws off creating a practical robot with easy-access electronics. The form and function of this bot are sweeter than honey.
This robot is capable as their shirts are bright. Their claw does it all: Shuts, Flips, and Orients. You can’t call this team couch potatoes since they have been to World’s ten times!

This team’s hands were held high in growing FIRST’s mission and vision both at home and at the competition. They were always reaching out a helping hand lending tools, equipment, and space to those in their community.
In brutal competition, this team has climbed a mile high. With great looks, cool speed, and unique operations, their quality always shows. May the Force be with them.

When it comes to furthering FIRST and STEM, and inspiring Engineering, this team works tirelessly year-round. They make theatrical robots, present to the governor and legislature, fund other teams from their own funds, and provide mentoring and workspace to multiple teams in FRC, FTC, and FLL. Their crafted wings carry them and others to great heights.

This team started small but has branched out by creating FIRST programs locally and across their state. They ride like the wind to build a sustainable ecosystem of support for underrepresented communities. By planting the seeds of STEM and nurturing them into a forest, this team is transforming how students see opportunities for their future.
A new team blew into the competition this year. This bot blew down the competition flat as a pancake. These well-trained operatives are a shining, bright light on robotics. Mission Accomplished.

Something new crawled out of the classroom deep in rural America. An inspiring new First Robotics team emerged amidst the Bunsen burners and microscopes and will never be the same. They have risen from their lab and emerged as a small team to be reckoned with.
This team's excitement for FIRST was striking! When the competition gets tough, they're unafraid to make their voices heard. Their team spirit is as strong as their intimidating helmets.
Looking ahead to achieve their objectives, this team had a plan. They put in place a process to last through the ages for their community and teammates. These green giants are continually improving.

Right from the start of Autonomous, this machine is fully ON! This robot follows the "path" from the scoring grid to the charging station without a flicker. Their reliable performance had the judges "singing the body electric."

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team developed a creative solution to secure their success on the field. Using automation, simulation, and logging they are able to replay matches and create new strategies. This team's capability gives them a 10,000 foot view while they are soaring overhead.

This team has taken their passion for engineering and robotics beyond the competition. They have organized summer camps, charity events, hosted tournaments and mentored elementary and middle school robotics teams. When it comes to spreading STEM and FIRST these students are "roaring" with "pride" and determination.

This is a team that has truly exemplified the mission of FIRST with sustained commitment to increasing awareness of STEM. Their achievements are the result of the team's welcoming, open, and inclusive culture. This approach allows everyone to explore different areas on the team and find their passion. This team is removing language barriers to better engage the broader community and increase student participation by translating materials into Spanish. This team is truly living their goal of making STEM accessible for everyone. They have shown incredible resilience and tenacity in the face of the pandemic, persevering through and bouncing back with astonishing effect. Since 2020, they have started 28 FLL and FTC teams ensuring 70% of students in their school district have access to a team. This outreach includes teaching teams the importance of sustainability, how to apply for grants, and create their own websites so sponsors and other interested community members have easy access to team information. Just like their school's football team from that famous movie, these "Titans" have come together with a shared purpose and a commitment to excellence, showing that it is possible to succeed while also lifting up those around you.

This team's well engineered tower of a robot wowed the judges. Their preparation of team organization and schedules enriched the team's understanding of what engineering is all about. There is no mistaking that these cavilers wear their state pride on their sleeve.

This established team has a long tradition of demonstrating gracious professionalism within their own team and throughout FIRST Chesapeake. They have recently worked to support middle school robotics programs and rookie FRC Teams on an ongoing basis. In the words of one team member "What we really want is for the other teams to succeed."

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's imagery stood out in the crowd and caught the judges eyes. Their branding and colors make them stand out not only in their community but in their school. If this were a John Hughes movie they would be "PRETTY IN PINK".

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team "clawed" their way to the top with their simple and robust mechanics. Their modular components went through an iterative process that ensured the team was "red"-y for success. Their "Super" effective design is "out of this world".

This robot has a multitude of pioneering, flexible options. They operate their robot from a unique, clear and colorful console using a progressive optics board to place game pieces with just the touch of a button. This fine feline federation can balance on the edge to help their team mates.

The judges were impressed with this team's unique approach to fund raising. This resourceful team was able to lower the cost of their robot with reusable parts also raised funds in their community which included offering baby sitting services. These "Smart and crafty" students have really put the work in since the "Genesis" of the season.

This team uses color coding, checklists, and critical thinking to build and maintain their robot. Their craftsmanship is evident from the wiring to their powder coated finish. Even Newton himself would impressed with this "Force of Nature".

This small rookie team showed great determination in getting their robot ready for competition. Working closely with other teams they are already building "paws"-itive connections within the FIRST community and have big plans for growing their membership. This team lives up to their "purr"-fect motto: "Just because we're small doesn't mean we cant do it".

This rookie team has had many great accomplishments in a short period of time. They have a strong membership program, are active in the community, and are highly involved in engineering-inspired charity work with environmental outcomes. They surely bring a boom to the world of engineering.

The passion and enthusiasm of this team is "stellar". As a student driven team they boldly recruited new mentors, and with their astonishing team spirit, it is no wonder that new members and volunteers "gravitated" to them. Their true spirit is expressed in their motto: "We are building a team, not a robot".

This Team "SWOT"-ted away the competition. They were clear and not cryptic when talking about their team's plans. Their students swooped in with facts and data convincing the judges they would continue soaring into the future.
Their triple-performing play impressed the judges. This team consistently scored 2 cones in autonomous. Control theory is in their genes!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: A small team of future engineers can bring unique perspectives. Recognizing the risk of defensive robots, their robot can pick up from the front or back. The pendulum swung in their direction for this award and we expect big things in 2 weeks.
When it comes defending animals, they INSURE success. They have impacted communities close and far. This team repeats excellence this year, as a previous world champion!

They BLUE us away with their impact that spread far and near. As future lobbyists they advocated for STEM in underserved schools. We will be blinded by pearly teeth when all the folks they have impacted smile and say CHEESE.

This team's robot would make you almost GREEN with envy. Their engineering processes, outcomes and decisions were all outstanding. An APPLE didn't fall on our heads, we had already realized this TEAL robot team deserves this award!
The reported professionalism from this team flies high. They clawed their way to the top by sharing FIRST in the treetops. We read many kind acts from their tabloid!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This award recognizes the wild nature of this team. Their bright, sunny brand stays in the sights of the FIRST Chesapeake district. This DEER team personifies their brand!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Their biting design STRIKES game pieces and stacks up points for their team. Element 29 has a sleek design and leaves a trail of excellent documentation.

This teams automated articulation made collecting cones a breeze! Their blend of automation and driver control allowed them to score effortlessly. There's no doubt this far-reaching team armed themselves to score from anywhere.
This well-rounded team conquers the land and sea. This team impressed our judges with their teamwork, consistency, and passion for FIRST. Lookout, because this team's robot packs a MEAN punch!
This team flew around the field taking hits left and right! They guarded their treasure with a robust design and exceptional workmanship. They have developed a MECHanism of envy.
This rookie team emits energy into the competition. They put their community first, and the competition second. This team formed a business, to make tea and a STORM of money!
This team has engineered great success on a small budget. They have created friends and developed more friends across other teams. These rookies have learned that seniority does not mean superiority!
The team and their suport in the stands look ever so royal. Their enthusiasm and energy embody fantastic spirit. Who are all those people wearing the PLUMES?
This team soars above the rest. Their rookies receive robust university training. This team shows that robots can truly take flight!

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.script: This team's ability to score and balance in autonomous contributed significantly to their success on the field. The judges were particularly impressed with how this team used simulations to test and perfect their autonomous routine. This robot's precise and aggressive attack to autonomous can be described as anything but toothless.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: If you want triple balance at the end, this team is your pick. They would graciously move out of the way to make space for you. Their creative solution got to the GROOT of the problem.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.script: Always adapting, this team has been continuing outreach all season. From designing curricula to mentoring others, they inspire many. From kindergarten centers to senior centers, this team is sharp about spreading the news of STEM.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.script: This team's outreach and advocacy are both broad and purposeful as they work to make STEM and FIRST as accessible as possible to their region. They focus on including rookies in all events, giving them exposure to all aspects of their team, including mentoring the FLL teams that they support. Through this diverse team's devotion to "STEMINISM", they live the true values of their motto: "DOCENDO DISCIMUS" (By teaching, we learn).

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.script: The team used prototypes and simulation to ensure the functionality of their solutions. Multiple iterations of their elegant claw kept them fierce on the field. A robust stress-tested robot, they are torching the competition.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.script: This team has made themselves a pillar of support, both locally and globally. They acknowledge their shortcomings and have taken measurable improvements in both their own and other's development. Your current center of attention is from Centreville.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When not together, you'll still know they belong. While it isn't easy being green, they are lean and mean. Truly a team Dean can relate to.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's practical robot won't let anybody steal their cones. This team keeps their competition at bay and never gets turned around. Everybody goes berserk for this pendulum design.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.script: Using PID tuning and vision processing built into all aspects of their controls, This team picks a spot on the field and sets their robot on autopilot, Charting a bright course in the field of stars.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.script: While many teams help orient and train their underclassman, this team elevates it to the next level. Their diligent use of lessons learned and robust pre-match checklists are examples of how they entrust freshmen to confidently be up to the task of competition. No matter which "DAWG" you talk with, their commitment to the future comes through loud & clear.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.script: This team's robustness, workmanship, and quality kept their robot in total control. Their 3-D-printed parts, wire management, and swerve drive helped them scoot around the competition with ease. The robot is designed for now and later, letting you know it's time for the SPARKULATOR!

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.script: This team rolled in with their heads held high and their eyes so wide. They competed with veteran teams to form alliances and partnerships. Just like a turtle, they are slowly making their way to the top.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.script: This team operates cohesively, like a happy family. From their robot, attire, and pit, to their enthusiasm, support and much more.... They fly with pride and inspire others to do the same. They are CHARGED UP and buzzing with energy.

records.eventName: CHS District Glen Allen VA Event
records.script: This team understands the assignment - to foster the skills development of new members. They built their curriculum on the experiences across mentors, alumni, and senior team members before they leave the nest. With a clear framework for individual and team knowledge retention, ROBO U is now a foundational part of the team.

Their robot's autonomous mode was a triple threat to the competition. Their robot is high consistent, moves swiftly, adapts to various conditions and accurate in scoring points. Robotics is in their helical DNA!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team had a unique design for the cube and cone grip mechanism. They also implemented lessons learned, added a reinforcing crossmember and grippy fingers. If you haven't heard of the CHARGED UP DOG before, you have now!

This team could be called defender of the stars. Their collaboration with other teams, robot demonstrations, open houses and social media efforts charted new horizons, sharing their love for engineering with the world and beyond. With armor and swords their team is out of this world!

Traffic couldn’t stop this team from presenting their exuberant enthusiasm for FIRST Robotics, but that is just part of their story. They engage their bilingual expertise to spread robotics across perceived barriers and geographic borders, and honed their budgeting skills to strengthen their financial position. These busy bees are well-equipped to defend their hive.

This robot embodies design, performance, and aesthetics. They described and presented their intake design from conception to implementation, and WOWED the judges. The professionalism they exude lets everyone know they are in the presence of an officially constructed robot.
This team found a home in a rural region of Virginia. Their willingness to assist other teams greatly impressed the judges. Their exemplary gracious professionalism is not found among many teams.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This Team came together among their community with a bright pink appearance. Utilizing perfect coordination, robot and team members look almost alike. If the stress is getting to your stomach, ask them for some PEPTO.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team's robot design incorporates a robust multistage arm that enabled delivery of cones and cubes to the upper level. Staying coordinated over Slack, this small team managed to design a practical and efficient robot with clean engineering and a recognizable tail of yellow cable work. This team was able to TUG their alliance members to wins.

They are the Olympic runners of robotics, leading the way in highly maneuverable robotic systems. Their robot's sensing-control loop is tightly coupled for rapid and precise response. They have lit the path for innovations in control!

Even though the robot faced multiple design and performance issues, the team persevered and collaborated with other teams to improve their design and make their robot perform better. This Bubblebot helped their alliance charge-up at the end!

This team made extensive use of CAD to design a rugged robot to sustain performance in the rigors of competition. Constantly learning form previous experience, this team equipped their robot with a SWERVE drive system, pressure-based pickup, and an innovative light board indication system. This ongoing iterative design ensured that any inefficiency was merely a ghost of the past.

This team came to Portsmouth in colorful, classic headgear. They took to the field and rode up the standings Zippity-split, and made quite an impression in their interviews. They are the Road-STARS at this competition.

This team is completely student driven and run. They not only rocked team spirit this weekend but rock it everyday in everything they do. While this team's captain is shipping up to Boston, we know the future of this team is strong.
If you don't ground a wire, it might arc. They lost room for all their spare parts. Their outreach to students in under-funded areas is making quite a spark.

This team’s high performance auto left the competition in a state of shock. Their precision design shows how their code is the perfect PRESCRIPTION for success. These medical professionals took our breath away as their robot keeps their alliance from flat lining.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s creativity was on display for you all. Crossing the field front to back without a stall. Then spinning around their central main post. These RAIDERS scored from just off the coast.

This team didn’t just scratch the surface with their community outreach; they made a significant paws-it-tive impact. They took their passion for STEM and menstrual equity and whiskered it into their schools curriculum. These wildcats know that when it comes to making a difference, it’s all about purr-serverence and inclusivity.

Whether you’re in the community or in the pits, you will hear this team’s number being voiced by those around them. This team lends help with not only their parts, tools and code, but their shop, students and mentors are well known by all. Within their community, they host summer camps, visit elementary schools and work with local scouts to spread the message of FIRST. They are actively working to represent marginalized genders and ethnic minorities within FIRSTWA and their team. They advocated for and helped start 10 new STEM classes at their school this year alone. If it’s encouraging and supporting teams at Girls Gen or helping rookies win their FIRST awards, this is truly a team to be emulated, and they deeply embody the message of FIRST. Alex, I’ll take: Diversity for: 31.37% of marginalized genders Outreach for: 8 new summer camp curriculums Hands On Learning for: 1 yearly trip to FlowJet And “Impact” for: 2046

This team created a robot with impressive insight. In the competition, their calculated and balanced design took flight. Unlike DOING TAXES, watching the results of their engineering process is a delight.

This team impressed the judges with their approach to working with other teams. They’re out in front of the race to provide needed parts, compliments to their alliance partners and lending a helping hand at events. Their grace and consideration is reminiscent of knights in shining amour… riding forth to do good and spread cheer on their gallant chargers.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team excels in presenting a UNIFIED appearance. Their pit and uniforms really made it a CLEAN SWEEP. And they’ll leave feathers in their wake as they TREAD toward victory.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This orange team’s robot grips game pieces with great suction. Their detailed, in-house designed and manufactured frame provided many purposes: from routing wires to protection. This team INKED out the competition. Their robot truly embraces a TENTA-COOL aesthetic and functional design.

This team’s driver station keypad allows them to PHONE in on their target. The robot’s claw PIVOT-ALLY allows it to control cones and cubes from all angles. Stand at attention as these patriots control the competition.

Community Connection Award This team from the isles, everyone knows. Fundraising and outreach have helped them to grow. The pride of their students flows ‘cross the sea. An integral part of their community.

This team’s quality stood out, scoring low mid and high. With a robust design, their matches flew by. Clawing their way through all of their matches. These cats stayed cool, BEAR-ly fixing any scratches.

This team’s smiles were contagious and their inclusivity was ENCHANTING. With their signature orange hue, this team brought a bright MAGICAL presence to this competition. These UNICORNS impressed the judges most with how every member of their team contributed to their robot.

This team illuminated the path for newcomers on their team. Through their elaborate and inclusive recruitment efforts, SOPs, and Jedi/Padawan training program, this team has mastered the art of sustainability. Let’s give this team an OHHH-YUP.

Move over, hedgehog! You aren't the fastest rodent in town. This team is taking your name. This team's mastery of the autonomous period and semi-autonomous tele-op had them bringing home all the nuts.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Despite its name, this team really is the breadwinner. Their robot's unique design SUCKED the air out of the room, designing through FIRST principles. This team's creativity brought a new "PURRspective".
This team was blue when they noticed a need in the community. They provided a kit of parts with fun experiments for learning. When it comes to inspiration, they are the alpha team.

This team brings the STEAM to STEM! It's energizing to hear of all the unique projects and partnerships that they have blended to spread the Mission of FIRST in their community. Their sustainable practices have "lit" the way for many to see "brighter" days. Thanks a latte!!!!

This team roared into the minds of the judges by gracefully reigning over the discussion of their engineering journey. This do it all robot integrates numerous mechanical and software systems to create a fast and efficient "chimera" of a machine. These students truly are engineering "royalty".

When other teams call out for help, this team is quick to respond. By sharing data and scouting software, they breathe life into other teams. No need to call an ambulance with this team around. Their selfless acts make them the heartbeat of the event.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: We judges found this team's imagery to make a real splash. Clean visuals and aesthetics incorporated functionally into their robot pulled us into the deep. Give these imagery award winners a hand or maybe eight.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team truly reached for that balance of form, function, and aesthetics. From their intelligently designed transmission to their bumper clamps, their turret turned the judges' heads. Their attention to detail was truly "RAIDiating"

This noble team from across the water has come "armed" with numerous fantastic innovations. This outstanding group has truly "braked" the mold with their robot's ingenious parking brake and counter-balancing system on their own. Racing their light cycle to the win, this team showed innovation in how they controlled the grid.

When it comes to spreading the word of FIRST, this team circled the wagons. Inspiring those of all ages through their STEM clubs, STREAM kits and community events. This team went above and beyond the herd. Their efforts to reach, reshape and remove barriers charged up the judges to pick them for a Community Outreach Award.

This team designed reliability into their robot and it shows. Applying lessons learned last year, they strengthened their robot with sheet aluminum, gussets, and other reinforcements to achieve "ursine" structural strength. By bringing these methods to "bear", they really showed their mettle.
This team was out of this world. They act like a veteran team, sharing their interstellar wisdom and orbiting around their FLL teams. Give it up for the orange shirts from the red planet!
The vigor of this team kept the competition red-hot. The enthusiasm of each of their member left them as no slow pokes. Ultimately, their team spirit hit the snail on the head.

Far from in the red, this team has really invested in its future. Their keen business plans and sensible knowledge retention were really "knight" and day. We hope their sustainability may be "in-squire-ing" to the other teams.
There's nothing green about this team's movement on the field. Their speedy and accurate independent operation is no joke. This team really POPS out of the box.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has a bright future in robotics. They caught the judges’ attention with their out-of-this-world contortions on the field. Keep an eye on this team as they get ready to blast off to Mars.

This team is a pioneer in their community. Their mission is to spread the message of FIRST from DESSERTS to DESERTS. They chose to boldly go where no team has gone before. Let's give a round of applause and a hearty, "Live, long and prosper" to OLYMPIA ROBOTICS FEDERATION.

This team created a track to use their energy to engage the GEARS of their communities. Their five-year plan sustains and supports all the connections on their CIRCUIT BOARD. They completed the winning CIRCUIT for the FIRST Impact Award.
There’s nothing FISHY about this team’s engineering design process. Their well-documented process is ROLLED out online. This SQUAD is very passionate about sharing their designs.

This team impressed the judges with their consistent long term history revolving around helping others. Sharing their field, loaning parts, coaching, explaining, mentoring, and volunteering are all just the way they energize their community. Titans in their field, they tote others along as they redefine professionalism. In the end, the choice is very black and white.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team stood out both in the pits and on the field. The judges were impressed with the robot cut-outs and engravings that the team machined themselves. Of all the PAWssible contenders, this team CLAWED their way to the top to BEARly beat out the competition.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team has executed a clean and simple design. Compact and streamlined, with everything in its place, you won’t find a BIRD’S NEST of wires or components exposed. They are even integrated handles to TOTE it around. This team’s outstanding design helped them FLY through their matches.

Their driver doesn't need to feel BLUE. The Judges were impressed with this Seattle-based team's seamless communication between driver and robot. This team demonstrated an EXCELLENT integrated control system.
This team floated to the top of the pack. They create awards to thank their sponsors, and the judges award this team in return. This process OTTER help new team members bring order to CHAOS.
This team’s expert craftsmanship was a KNIGHT for sore eyes. Their efficient, reliable design and precise 49.11 degree angles set them apart to get powered up.

These young engineers impressed the Judges with their professionalism and commitment to their community. They’ve stirred up quite the admiration with their EGGcellent documentation, all while boiling up a recipe for success. So let’s all raise our chopsticks and give a noodle-riffic round of applause to this SOUPer star rookie team!

Don’t let this team’s fierce demeanor fool you; this team is known far and wide for their friendly disposition. They march through parades and spread FIRST Core Values with the spirit and determination of the finest explorers. Raise your shields and let out a thunderous roar for the team with KNITTED HORNS!

No other team understands the concept at a professional level and has built a structure which even some corporations would do well to adopt. Risk analysis and mitigation is at the heart of their energy for sustainability. Growing from post-competition retrospectives to a “leadership transition shadowing program”, the judges could find no better fit for the sustainability award than these knights in shining armor.

This robot was an animal scoring cubes and cones and engaging the charge station. The precise and smooth operation of the robot was consistent throughout the event and had the crowd going NUTS. The team may be a bit SQUIRRELY but programming ensured that their robot rocked! Congratulations to Team 2930 - Sonic Squirrels

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team can move in all directions, But at the end of the match they want to stand still, Their creative break was a CHECKMATE for us. Congratulations to Team 5588 - Reign Robotics

This team is revolutionizing their community. From creating a new curriculum to increasing inclusion, they forge a path to unify STEM learning. They are IRONCLAD in their mission of equity. Congratulations to Team 4131 - Iron Patriots

This team has a BA in local and international cooperation. They really answer the call for FIRST and are powerful advocates for STEM education. the IMPACT of their STEM outreach has grown to include the Girl Scouts of Western Washington. We really like how they "take charge!" Congratulation to Team 2412- Robototes

This team impressed the judges with their commitment to their FAITH in their engineering. Their integrated product is a carefully constructed delicate balance between strength and maintainability. Everything rotates around the SACTITY of their calculations and the SACRAMENT of their build. Just ask them what Jesus means to them. Congratulations to Team 2910- Jack in the Bot

This team knows that practice makes perfect, not by themselves but by working together. So they roll out the red carpet for all the robots to play. Sound the trumpets for this majestic team. Congratulations to Team 2522 - Royal Robotics

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's imagery fits right into the Pacific Northwest. Their robot, pit, and CUB members can be seen from a mile away. They CLAWED their way into the judges hearts. Congratulations to Team 4682 - CyBears

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their attention to detail and compact robot They didn't tolerate poor design and checked their lists to assure good industrial design Don't try to fence these CATS into a box!! Congratulations to Team 8248 ChainLynx

Roses are red, this robot is BLUE their robot amazed us and probably you too! From conception and design to implementation this team smoothly scored thanks to their system integration. Are you green with envy? Just CHUCKING it out there... Congratulations to Team 2147 - CHUCK

The judges would like to call this award the Grassroots Award. This team caught the judges attention for their numerous distinctions. Their grassroots upbringing, and rural ways kept their team deep rooted in their community. Put on a KETTLE of tea and give it up for Team 4980 the Canine Crusaders! Congratulations to Team 4980 - Canine Crusaders

Let's take a voyage shall we? From a frozen far north, this team's mills go brr making parts and spares to keep their bot in ship shape. This team makes sure their dyneme ropes aren't frayed and their belts are tensioned, because they know it will be a rough ride out at sea. Glacier Peak it's time to get out the tape and protect your ports, the Vikings will be heading on down. Congratulations to Team 2928 - Viking Robotics

This team charmed the judges with infectious enthusiasm, and dynamic partnerships, and expert professionalism in their FIRST year. Close work with an Eastside Alliance along with impeccable outreach is becoming of a FIRST team. This cup of soup stole the show. Congratulations to Team 9036 - Ramen Robotics

When their community is in need, they pounced into action. Their support RAMPS us up in improving equity for everyone in reach. They are wildly loud and wildly proud wherever they are. Congratulations to Team 2980 - Whidbey Island Wildcats

This team DOGGEDLY pursues its plans and sniffs out risks. These DOGS deliberately do their business and train their pups methodically. They go marching in toward a more sustainable future. Congratulations to Team 1899 - Saints Robotics

This team showed consistency when traveling across the charge station. It was TOUGH to tell if it was human or robot controlled. Not even glasses and a mustache can distinguish the success of their autonomous.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s creative use of components has them leading the field. Their unique arm design is helping them reach the summit. The squad’s approach to design is anything but Chaotic. Congratulations, Chaos Theory.

What stood out to the judges about this team was their commitment to the robotics community and helping other FIRST teams grow through their involvement with alliances and resource sharing. Their go above and beyond in promoting STEAM through webinars, in-person events, and student led classes. Their mascot may be small and cute, but we know they are Titans in the field!

This team strives to hold diversity, equity and inclusion in high regard. These ambassadors unify students and bring opportunities for all. This team is Iron Solid in equipping our future leaders and Patriots in inspiring passion for STEM.

This squad’s custom bearings and stable design has left them anything but blue. Their lighted cylinders and automated programming have put them right on target. This team’s approach to engineering and design has them aiming for success. Way to go, AEMBOT!

This team’s positive interactions are demonstrated on and off the field. They have rooted their sprouts as a gracious FRC team by lending others a helping hand. When it comes to FIRST values, they are working hard and having fun!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: After their last competition, this team’s robot needed a hand and seemed to be on its last leg. But the team knew they had suffered only a flesh wound! The judges loved this team’s creativity and humor- congratulations to the Sequim Robotics Federation!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The way this robot distinguishes itself is no surprise. With their elevator arm, they crank out links. (sing to tune of Pop Goes the Weasel) All around the mulberry bush….The winner is team 2910! Jack in the Bot!
This team’s innovation is on a roll. Their ability to control the robot has them slicing up the competition as they rice and shine on the field. Congrats, Sushi Squad!
In their dogged approach to overcoming obstacles, and their field play that has collared the competition, it is clear that this team should be judged Top Dog!
Weather or not! This robot’s design is not only small, but can stand tall. Of course, in atmospheric conditions, the use of vision gives it capabilities to detect its target.

This team overcame a major obstacle right at the beginning of the school year. Thought dogged determination they rebuilt their entire tool inventory after all their gear was stolen. Despite this major setback, you can tell these wolves are proud of their pack, and kept their spark alive all season. Congratulations, Robo Sparks!

When asked by the judges what they were proudest of for this year, one of their members immediately exclaimed, “Our improved rookie training!” Between their rookie training, FTC mentorship and community outreach, this team clearly makes investments. If the only guarantees in life are death and taxes, then maybe it’s no surprise that this year’s sustainability award is going to the IRS!

Flying around obstacles with no one in command, choosing from THREE DIFFERENT PATHS, this robot stuck to the plan. This team’s integration of autonomy set them above the rest, during the first 15 seconds their robot proved it was best.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team really has this award IN THE BAG. They were at the FRONT OF THE LINE with their unique retrieval and delivery system. You’ll have to CHECKOUT this robot
This team’s intake is so FAST, if you blink, then you’ll miss it. Their elegant bot was designed from the start for need and simplicity. They are no one’s PLUS ONE.

This team has made it their core value to increase diversity on their team. They have impacted teams both in and off the field by sharing their knowledge and resources. This team was instrumental in getting a school referendum passed, by advocating for the addition of STEM content.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team will have you HUNTING for the truth. Follow the CLUES in search of the secrets. You won’t have to keep your THIRD EYE OPEN to spot their imagery.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: While TIPPING up CONES, TACKLING CHALLENGES and TOPPLING their COMPETITION, this team’s robust, linear, 3-axis system does the work with no fuss. Coming in just under weight…

When the time came to innovate, this team took control and sank their TEETH into the challenge. They got to the CORE of the problem by building a COMMUNITY of solutions. They are FUTURE of Innovation in Control

For progressing one small step for students, this team’s impact is spreading like wild FIRE. In helping NASA develop software to further launch the Artemis mission, this team’s achievements are out of the world.
A clean design allows this robot to self-align and lift it’s fair share. Paddle out to sea, it’s HIGH TIDE, Feel free to catch a RIDE.

This team focuses on areas that allow them to FOSTER team work. They have specialized their ADAPTIVE abilities to put a smile on a face. They are FORWARD thinking which drives Engineering Inspiration.

This years’ Impact award winner is BUILDING a legacy in their small community that will be hard to follow. From FARMERS to FRAMERS, these guys are not turkeys. Whatever they are COOKING- it smells like success. Small town, Small School, HUGE Impact.

Last year, students with a common interest in STEM united to join the FIRST family. They prioritized the future growth of the team through developing technical skills beyond just the competition. This rookie team is an inspiration to current and future teams.
It was no ACCIDENT that this student-led team has spirit. Their focus on Inclusivity is proof that MORE EQUALS MERRIER (make no mistake).
This team’s outreach and planning is something to behold. This teams ARMY of STEM advocates will only grow. They scatter like ANTS to promote STEM and ensure all have access to their programs.

This team considered a number of factors to successfully manage the robot’s actions during autonomous such as lining up scoring nodes by coordinating trajectories based on 3D coordinated readings from April Tags, a limelight camera for vision, sensors to stabilize the robot, also signaling whether a cube or a cone that will be picked. This team methodically thought through the auto routines making the robot a consistently self-governing warrior on the field.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The start of the season offers a new beginning. New members, new challenges, and new ideas. It comes time to charge up the 3D printer and set your creativity into gear. This team took a step back and decided think small to overcome big challenges.

When it comes to a thought out design, this team goes the distance. From their initial design conception to final product, this robot is rock solid. This teams professional collaboration led to a robot that has no borders.

This team exemplifies gracious professionalism by conducting many off season camps and workshops. They have touched many programmers worldwide in small bytes. This team definitely does not hibernate in the off season.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team left a permanent mark on the judges and the FIRST community. Their meaningful team name and advocacy for FIRST core values are unparalleled. Their team’s coordination and innovative theme left the judges green with envy.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team went above and beyond to make their design the best. A mechanical marvel that overwhelmingly out performed the rest. This purposely built robot was at the top of the heap for Industrial Design, And best of all, we all know it is a BEAST!

From their use of multiple recognition systems for space and play pieces, to their intake and light systems, this team “tops” the field and is in control. Integration between the placement system and lighting gives visual feedback while their use of blue cora and limelight allows auto-correction of the robot for intake.

When approached by the judges, they spoke to us like another sponsor. They were not left black and blue by their minimalistic base. It was clear that aesthetics was a focus of their design, and they proved to be an extremely well-rounded team.

This years Quality Award winner is banking that their design, fit, and finish will improve their performance. The integration of carbon fiber and the functionality of their intake mechanism made their robot robust and ready to take on any challenge. Their robot has proven that their commitment to quality has paid off.

This team has passed along their inspiration for STEM by welcoming over 100 new FLL members over the past year alone. When recycling waste in the community, no teeth marks where left. They were featured on FIRST’s social media and are on to New Horizons.

By participating in a variety of events, ranging from open houses and 8th Grade Tours to Rockwell Automation Fairs, this team is spreading STEM and FIRST in Milwaukee. They ensure students from across the city have access to FIRST and STEM by providing a shuttle for transportation to and from their academy. These Tigers have clearly made an Impact.

No shift in energy needed with this team – from leading alliance cheers to making sure they are heard to the pits -this group embodies the energy and spirit of FIRST. Spirit is so important to this team it ranks its own committee named after this aware. This year’s Team Spirit Award goes to team 1259 – Paradigm Shift.
The night is always darkest before the dawn. This team rallies its fearless members when signaled. They snap on their wings to sustain their flight.

scope: official team judged award results, with citations when FIRST publishes them
